fix: await guild broadcasts so members reliably receive updates

broadcastGuild and pushGuild ran their member lookup + delivery via a
fire-and-forget `void db.guildMembers(...).then(...)` while being typed
`void`. Most call sites wrote `await this.broadcastGuild(...)`, but
awaiting a `void` return is a no-op, so the async work was never actually
awaited — and guildSetRank didn't await at all.

This means guild events (joins, promotions, kicks, leaves, guild chat)
could be lost or arrive out of order: if a member's connection state
changed, or the handler returned and unwound, between scheduling and the
deferred lookup completing, the delivery could be missed.

Make both methods `async`/return `Promise<void>` so the existing `await`
call sites become meaningful, and await them in guildSetRank. Adds a
regression test that defers the member lookup to a later macrotask and
asserts the promote notice is delivered by the time guildSetRank resolves
(fails before the fix, passes after).

fix: run moderation writes on a pinned pooled client

moderateAccount and forceCharacterRename issued BEGIN, their UPDATE/
INSERT statements, and COMMIT/ROLLBACK through pool.query(). With pg's
connection Pool each call may check out a different physical connection,
so the statements were not guaranteed to share one transaction:

- A mid-transaction failure could leave the action partially applied
  (e.g. account banned but the audit row and report resolution missing),
  and the stray ROLLBACK could land on a connection with no open tx.
- BEGIN could leave a borrowed connection in an open-transaction state
  for an unrelated concurrent request.

Pin a single client via pool.connect() for the whole transaction and
release it in finally, matching the existing pattern in db.ts
ensureSchema(). Update the moderation_db tests to assert the transaction
runs on one pinned client and rolls back + releases on failure.

fix: make evading mobs immune to damage while they reset

When a wild mob breaks leash it switches to the 'evade' state: it drops
its hate table, walks home, and only heals to full on arrival. enterCombat
refuses to re-aggro an evading mob, so it never fights back during the
retreat.

dealDamage, however, guarded only `dead` and `gm` targets — not `evade`.
So a player could keep landing hits on a retreating mob (re-seeding its
threat table) and even kill it outright before it reached home: a
risk-free kill that also breaks the classic reset contract, where an
evading mob is immune until it resets.

Add an early return in dealDamage for mobs in the 'evade' state (covers
both leash-broken wild mobs and pets freed to the wild, which both enter
'evade' with ownerId cleared). Damage and DoT ticks now no-op until the
mob resets and can be pulled again.

Adds tests/evade_immunity.test.ts covering: no damage/threat while
evading, can't be killed while evading, and normal damage resumes once
the mob is fighting again.

fix: reject party invites accepted while already in a party

The "a player belongs to at most one party" invariant was enforced at
invite time (partyInvite refuses targets already in a party) but never at
accept time. Because invites are keyed by invitee, inviting someone never
consumes the inviter's own pending incoming invite. A player can therefore:

  1. receive an invite from C (while solo),
  2. invite D, who accepts — making the player a party leader, then
  3. accept C's still-pending invite.

Step 3 pushed the player into a second party's member list with
partyByPid pointing at the new party, leaving them a stale member of their
original party (broadcasts, loot/threat crediting and disband logic all go
out of sync).

partyAccept now rejects the accept if the player is already in a party,
mirroring the guard partyInvite already applies to invite targets.

fix: snap remote entities on teleport instead of interpolating

A teleport (arena pit, dungeon portal, graveyard release) moves an entity
far further in one snapshot than any walking update could. The client's
applyWire interpolated across that gap from the old pose toward the new
one; when the entity's per-entity interpolation clock wasn't established
yet (netInterval undefined), the renderer fell back to the global snapshot
alpha and the entity stuck at its pre-teleport position until its next
real update (e.g. taking damage) re-anchored it. In the arena this showed
as your opponent standing outside the pit until you hit them.

Snap prevPos to the destination when a position update jumps more than a
walking step (>40yd), so teleported entities appear exactly where the
server placed them.

fix: free evading mobs pinned on camp props (Gravecaller Summoners)

Evading mobs walk a straight line home with no pathfinding, and
resolvePosition only pushes a body radially OUT of a collider — never
around it. So an evading mob whose line home crosses a prop (the
Gravecaller Encampment tent/crate/campfire) or deep water freezes at the
obstacle's edge. A recent change made evading mobs immune to damage while
they reset, which turned that benign stall into a permanently unkillable
mob — the Gravecaller Summoners that blocked progression in prod.

Fix: once an evading mob stalls (no progress home for EVADE_STALL_TIMEOUT),
it phases straight through the blocker one normal step at a time, stopping
the moment a normal collision-aware step works again (blockedTowardSpawn).
Phasing always makes progress, so arrival is the backstop. No teleport:
worst single-frame movement across 1743 previously-stuck starts was 1.13yd.

Overhead is negligible: the extra resolvePosition probe runs only for mobs
that are actually phasing (a rare, genuinely-stuck state); a normal evade
adds one dist2d per tick.

Adds regression tests: tent-pin recovery + killable-again, the no-teleport
property, and that a normal short evade is undisturbed.

fix(input): stop camera drag from cancelling held movement keys

Walking with W (or any held movement key) and then right- or left-dragging
to look around stopped movement the instant the mouse button was released.

A camera drag requests pointer lock; releasing the button exits pointer lock,
firing pointerlockchange -> releaseCapture('pointerlock'), which called
this.keys.clear() and wiped the still-held W/A/S/D. Regression from c967e53
(optional mouse-camera mode), which added the pointerlockchange handler.

Clearing held keys is only correct on focus loss (blur / tab hidden), where the
OS swallows the matching keyup and movement would otherwise stick on. A pointer
-lock exit keeps window focus, so keyup still fires normally — guard the clear
to skip the 'pointerlock' reason; mouse-drag state is still reset every time.

Adds regression tests for right- and left-drag keeping forward movement, plus

feat(mobile): long-press an action-bar slot to peek its tooltip without casting

On touch there is no hover, so the HUD shows an ability/item tooltip after a
~950ms long press. But a synthetic `click` still fires when the finger lifts, so
long-pressing a hotbar slot to read its tooltip ALSO cast the ability — and the
tooltip was never dismissed on touch (no `mouseleave`). Inspecting a slot on a
phone was effectively impossible.

Add a tiny `TouchPeekGuard` (src/ui/touch_peek.ts): a fresh touch press resets
it, the long-press tooltip marks a "peek", and the action-bar click handler
consumes that mark to suppress the cast and dismiss the tooltip on release. A
quick tap (timer never fires) casts as before. Resetting on every press keeps a
peek on one control from leaking into a tap on another.

Presentation-only — no sim/IWorld/net/server change. New tests/touch_peek.test.ts
covers the guard; 653 tests pass, tsc clean.

feat(chat): profanity filter with admin-managed lists and slur enforcement

Adds a two-tier chat moderation system.

Soft (cosmetic) words are masked client-side with **** — on by default,
toggleable per player (Esc > Key Bindings > Filter Profanity). The server
ships the soft list in the `hello` frame and pushes live updates when an admin
edits it, but never alters the text itself, so toggling the filter off shows it
raw. Masking is applied to both the chat log and the floating chat bubble.

fix(server): complete the #218 rate-limit backstop fix on both maps (#251)

#218 (landed as d433d4d) replaced the blanket authFailures.clear() backstop
with expired-only eviction, but that leaves a residual #147/#217 flagged on
both rate-limit maps: under a pure flood every entry is freshly timestamped,
so expired-only eviction removes nothing, the map grows unbounded past
MAX_TRACKED_IPS, and each call re-scans the growing map (O(n^2)). The "memory
backstop" stopped bounding memory exactly under the load it exists for. This
completes the fix on BOTH the per-account authFailures map AND the per-IP
attempts map.

Add a second eviction stage to recordAuthFailure() and rateLimited(): when the
expired pass leaves the map over the cap (the all-in-window flood case), evict
the least-recently-active entry until back under the cap — but never the
just-recorded key and never a currently-limited/throttled entry. A
burst/lockout-then-idle victim ages while a flood of newer one-off entries
arrives, so a naive LRA eviction would pick the idle victim as "oldest" and
reset its live limit; the skip-check prevents that. If everything left is
current or limited, the map is allowed a soft over-cap rather than resetting a
live limit (fail toward protection).

The "currently limited?" predicate is a shared atOrOverLimit() helper used by
authThrottled() and both backstops, so they cannot drift. The per-IP attempts
map is shared across routes with different limits (game login 20, admin login
10), so its skip-check judges "limited" by the STRICTEST policy
(STRICTEST_RATE_LIMIT) — otherwise a lenient-route flood could evict an IP
already limited under the stricter admin route and reset it mid-window.

Tests (tests/security.test.ts, with beforeEach map resets for isolation):
- account + IP: a >12k distinct in-window flood leaves the map bounded near the
  cap (fails on expired-only eviction);
- account: a throttled-then-idle victim stays throttled after a >10k
  newer-account flood (fails on naive LRA);
- IP: a burst-then-idle limited IP stays limited after a >10k newer-IP flood
  (fails on naive LRA);
- IP: a lenient-route flood does not evict an IP limited by a stricter route
  (fails on a per-call-threshold skip-check).

fix: scale mob armor from level 1 like hp and damage

createMob computed armor as `armorPerLevel * level`, while hp and damage
both scale with `(level - 1)` so that a level-1 mob equals its template
base values. MobTemplate has no `armorBase` field (unlike players, who
have `baseStats.armor`), so the intended base armor is 0 and the
per-level term should scale from level 1.

As written, every mob carried one extra level of armor — and even a
level-1 critter received a full `armorPerLevel` of mitigation it should
not have. Since `e.stats.armor` feeds `armorReduction()` for all physical
hits, this made mobs measurably tankier than designed across every level.

Align armor with the established `(level - 1)` convention and add a
regression test asserting a level-1 mob has 0 armor and higher levels add
exactly `armorPerLevel` each.

feat(sim): steep miss-chance scaling against higher-level targets

Anti-bot / anti-cheat. Bot swarms power-level by parking on mobs several levels
above them; the vanilla-derived hit table was too lenient for that (a +4-level
target was only ~13% melee miss / ~28% spell miss), so farming way-above-level
packs stayed efficient. The miss penalty for attacking a target above your level
now rises steeply: +2 ~19%, +4 ~85%, +6 capped at 95% — making above-level
grinding near-futile while leaving equal/lower-level play unchanged.

Applies to every attack path: melee swings, hunter Auto Shot + wands (via
meleeMissChance), and spells / Arcane Shot / Serpent Sting (via spellHitChance),
and symmetrically to mobs swinging at higher-level players. The curve
(~2.5 * diff^2.5) is stored as an integer lookup table (level diffs are always
integers) so it stays bit-for-bit deterministic across engines — Math.pow with a
fractional exponent is not guaranteed identical in the browser vs the server,
which would break the same-seed-same-world invariant.

feat(antibot): First version of behavioral bot detection

Adds a real-time, schema-free bot-detection layer that runs server-side
on every WebSocket session.

Three evidence kinds:
- Action timing variance: combat command intervals; stdDev < 15 ms →
  weight 0.7, < 50 ms → 0.3; TTL 2 min.
- Concurrent sessions per IP: soft evidence (weight 0.4) above
  MAX_WS_PER_IP_SOFT (default 5); hard close (1008) at
  MAX_WS_PER_IP_HARD (default 20).
- Reaction time: stimulus (castStop/death) → next combat command;
  median < 150 ms → 0.6, stdDev < 30 ms → 0.3; Phase 1 without RTT
  correction.

Escalation: score ≥ 0.5 + 2 kinds for 30 s → auto-report to
player_reports; ≥ 0.8 for 60 s → shadow-throttle (×2); ≥ 1.0 for
2 min → kick; 30-min safety valve.

fix(antibot): report-only mode + Phase 1 false-positive fixes

The first version of behavioral bot detection flagged legitimate players, and its
"≥ 2 evidence types" guard could be satisfied by a single behavioral trait — so a
fast, rhythmic, or shared-connection player could reach an automatic kick. Make the
system safe before making it smart: keep the moderator-facing reports but remove its
ability to act on its own. With the signals in tree today nothing escalates — by
design, until an independent behavioral signal lands.

- Disable the reaction-time signal: its stimulus was the player's own cast/death
  (self-generated and anticipated), so it measured rotation chaining, not reaction.
  (Its window-closing is also corrected to combat commands only, for the rebuild.)
- Gate escalation on independent behavioral families: timing + reaction are one
  "cadence" family, and multi_ip (shared IP / CGNAT) is context that scores and is
  reported but never gates a response.
- Fix the multi_ip lifecycle: mark every session on a crowded IP (not just the last
  to connect) and clear it when the IP thins out, instead of tagging one arbitrary
  session forever.
- Drop the moderate timing band (stdDev < 50ms): it flagged metronomic humans; only
  near-zero variance now produces timing evidence.
- Add ANTIBOT_ENFORCE (default off): shadow-throttle and auto-kick stay disabled
  until the signals are mature and the false-positive rate is measured; the
  moderation-report path stays enabled.

Removes the obsolete reaction hooks and e2e script; updates the design doc and adds
false-positive regression tests.

fix(camera): bypass follow-cam in Mouse Camera mode

Mouse Camera mode (OSRS-style, camera-relative movement) is meant to be
camera-authoritative, exactly like holding right-mouse for mouselook —
the character's facing is locked to camYaw and the player rotates the
view by dragging. But on desktop the mode reports isMouselookActive()
false, so updateCamera let the auto-follow/settle system keep running.
Since facing IS camYaw in this mode, the follow code chased its own tail
and fought the drag, drifting the view ~40-52deg off where the player
aimed (right-mouse mouselook avoids this only because it sets the
mouselook flag, which bypasses follow).

Fold Mouse Camera mode into a named cameraIsManual() predicate so it
takes the same bypass path right-mouse already uses. Classic mode is
unchanged (cameraIsManual(x, false) === x). Adds regression coverage for
the predicate and the multi-frame drag-drift property; this control path
previously had zero tests, which is how it rotted through the follow-cam
rework.

fix(render): stop online walk clip resetting from self predictor

The "Movement fixes" change added an online-only local-player render
predictor (selfPos, ONLINE_SELF_RENDER_ALPHA_LEAD=0.65). Because
selfSnapshotAlpha clamps at 1.25, the predicted target freezes for part
of each snapshot interval then jumps at the next snapshot; smoothing and
the >6u snap distort it further.

The animation state machine derived its inputs (locomotion speed,
backpedal, airborne) from that jittery position, so the base state
intermittently flipped (walk<->idle/run/jump) and visual.ts fadeTo()
reset the walk clip to frame 0 — the random walk-cycle reset.

Derive the anim inputs from the plain interpolated sim motion (ax/ay/az)
instead; the predictor now moves only the mesh. Offline ax==x, so
single-player is unchanged.

fix(sim): walk down slopes instead of detaching mid-hill

Descending a hill forced the player airborne: the grounded vertical step
treated any ground drop greater than a fixed 0.4 yd as "walked off a ledge",
detaching the player and zeroing horizontal velocity. At run speed (~0.35 yd
per 20 Hz tick) any walkable downhill steeper than ~1.14 rise/run crossed that
threshold, so the player got stuck stuttering at the top of the slope and had
to jump to make progress downhill — while uphill, which snaps to terrain via a
proper slope gate, worked at any angle.

fix(ui): restore touch scrolling in HUD windows on iOS

The mobile HUD overlay set `body.mobile-touch #ui { touch-action: none }`,
which on iOS blocks one-finger panning for the entire descendant tree.
Because Safari resolves touch-action by intersecting values down the
ancestor chain, a scroll container's own `pan-y` cannot re-enable what an
ancestor set to `none` — so the Bag and Market/Exchange lists could not be
scrolled by touch (desktop wheel-scroll was unaffected, masking the bug).

Relax the overlay to `touch-action: pan-x pan-y` (still blocks pinch /
double-tap zoom, which is also guarded in preventMobileZoom), and give the
scrollable lists iOS momentum + scroll isolation
(`-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch`, `overscroll-behavior: contain`). World
camera drag is unchanged — it is suppressed on #game-canvas, not via #ui.

perf(render): gate per-entity swim terrain sample behind the cheap depth test

The swimming-pose check in the per-frame entity loop sampled groundHeight()
(an FBM terrain-noise evaluation) for every non-dead visible entity, every
frame, and only then tested whether the entity's feet were below the water
line. Since swimming requires both conditions, reordering so the cheap
feet-depth field test short-circuits first makes the expensive terrain sample
run only for entities actually at/below the surface — i.e. essentially never
for the whole crowd standing on land.

The result is identical (it's a commutation of a side-effect-free &&), and it
removes work that scales linearly with on-screen entity count in a documented
frame-rate hot path. The airborne check just below already gates its own
groundHeight sample to players for the same reason; this brings the swim check
in line.

Micro-benchmark over a 120-entity scene (seed 20061, ~8% in water): the swim
check drops from ~73µs to ~7µs per frame (10x), with zero result mismatches
across all positions including the in-water swimming cases.

fix(market): always wire a seller their own listings

The World Market ships at most MARKET_WIRE_LIMIT (120) listings per
snapshot, sliced off a single global alphabetical sort. On a busy shared
market a seller's own goods can sort past slot 120 and never reach their
client, yet `myListingCount` is computed over *every* stored listing — so
the SELL tab reads "12 / 12 listing slots used" while only a handful of
the player's listings are actually visible.

Partition the wired set so the seller's own listings are always included
first, then fill the remaining wire budget with everyone else's. Because
MARKET_MAX_LISTINGS (12) is far below MARKET_WIRE_LIMIT (120), a seller's
goods always fit alongside a healthy slice of the wider market, and the
"X / 12" count can never exceed what the player can see. Pure sim logic;
server-authoritative and deterministic, no new strings.

Adds a regression test that floods the market past the wire cap and
asserts every one of the seller's listings is wired.

perf(ui): prewarm world-map terrain during idle so opening it never freezes

Opening the world map (M) stalled the main thread for a beat: the full-zone
terrain background is built lazily on the open path by renderTerrainCanvas at
MAP_BG_RES (480px), which samples terrainHeight + roadDistance for every one of
~230k pixels (~200ms+, longer cold / on slow hardware). The cache was a single
slot keyed by zone, so it also re-paid that cost on every zone revisit.

A background depends only on (seed, zone bounds) — both fixed for the session —
so it is immutable and safe to cache forever and to compute ahead of time:

- Cache backgrounds per zone in a Map (never invalidated), so a revisit is a hit.
- Prewarm the committed zone's background during idle time (requestIdleCallback,
  setTimeout fallback), painted in whole-row slices so it never blocks a frame.
  Kicked off at spawn and on each zone change, so the map is ready before the
  player opens it. Opening synchronously renders only as a fallback (map opened
  the instant we crossed a border).

Pixel output is unchanged. The per-pixel painter is lifted into a pure,
host-agnostic module (ui/map_terrain.ts) shared by the synchronous render and
the sliced prewarm; a Vitest proves a chunked render is byte-identical to a
single pass, is deterministic per seed, and differs per zone.

happens to share the number. Track which scheduler produced the handle
(mapPrewarmVia) and call only the matching canceller. When the idle path
lacks cancelIdleCallback there is nothing to call, but pumpMapPrewarm's
`if (!job) return` guard makes the stale callback a no-op.

fix(server): gate character rename on the force_rename flag

The character-select UI only renders a rename control when a moderator has set
force_rename (via the admin Force name change action), so a normal player sees
no rename option. But the route POST /api/characters/:id/rename only checked the
bearer token, account ownership, a valid name, and the character being offline,
never force_rename. Any owner could therefore rename their own offline character
at will by calling the API directly: a client-side-gating-is-not-security gap.

Make the server authoritative on the same rule the UI implies:
- renameCharacter gates the UPDATE on force_rename = TRUE, so the rename is
  race-free and self-limiting (a successful rename clears the flag, allowing
  exactly one rename per moderator action).
- The route fetches the character and returns a clear 403 when force_rename is
  not set, instead of a misleading 404.
- userFacingApiError maps the new error to errors.api.renameNotPermitted (English
  in the shell catalog, with the five forced non-Latin overlays filled).

Adds renameCharacter coverage to tests/character_db.test.ts asserting the gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(sim): tab-target cycles on-screen and engaged enemies first

Tab targeting picked the nearest enemy anywhere in the 40yd radius,
sorted purely by distance, so it would select mobs behind the player
or otherwise off screen instead of the ones the player can see or is
fighting.

The sim has no camera (the same core runs on the authoritative server
and headless), so "on screen" is modelled deterministically from the
player's facing: a front cone around the forward vector. "In combat
with you" comes from existing aggro state (a mob whose aggroTargetId or
targetId is the player). Candidates are ranked into priority tiers so
engaged, on-screen enemies cycle first while off-screen ones stay
reachable as a last resort, then by distance and id for stable,
replay-deterministic order.

Logic lives in a new pure module src/sim/tab_target.ts (orderTabTargets)
with unit tests, plus a Sim-level regression test reproducing the bug.

fix(game): pause click-to-move when the game menu opens, don't cancel it

Opening the Esc/game menu sets input.suspendMovement so WASD does not walk
the character behind the menu. That same flag fed clickMoveShouldCancel, which
permanently cleared the click-to-move destination, so pressing Escape silently
killed an in-progress run. Autorun did not have this problem: it is a flag that
readMoveInput simply gates while suspended and resumes when the menu closes.

Give click-to-move the same treatment. Replace the boolean clickMoveShouldCancel
with a tri-state resolveClickMoveAction returning 'cancel' | 'pause' | 'continue':
a menu (or load transition) now pauses the run (the destination is preserved and
the player holds still, then resumes on close), while genuine interrupts
(mouselook, death, feature disabled, a manual directional key) still cancel.
Cancel wins over pause, so a real interrupt during a menu still ends the run.

Pure-core change in src/game/click_move.ts with a thin consumer in main.ts's
resolveMove. Covered by tests/click_move.test.ts (pause vs cancel vs continue).

fix(sim): pet that isn't fighting no longer blocks owner health regen

A warlock standing idle with a summoned Infernal never regenerated health
while mana kept refilling. Out-of-combat health regen is gated on
`!p.inCombat`, but `p.inCombat` was held open forever because a pet was added
to `engagedPids` whenever it merely had an `aggroTargetId`, even when it was
not actually fighting (chasing an unreachable or stale target). Mana regen
uses the separate 5-second rule, so it kept ticking, producing the reported
"full mana, frozen HP" state.

Only keep the owner in combat while the pet is actively trading blows
(`combatTimer < PET_COMBAT_LINGER`); a pet's combatTimer resets to 0 on every
hit dealt or taken via enterCombat. A genuinely tanking pet still keeps its
owner in combat. The wild-mob-chasing arm is intentionally unchanged.

Adds tests/pet_combat_regen.test.ts (idle pet -> owner regens; fighting pet ->
owner stays in combat) and a max-graphics capture harness.

feat(sim): re-grant missing quest items from prior quests on accept

A quest can need a quest item that the player obtained during earlier
progression rather than during the quest itself (the canonical case is
the Crypt Keystone: rewarded by "The Abandoned Crypt", then used at the
ritual circle in "The Bound Guardian"). If that item was dropped,
discarded, or lost by abandoning and re-accepting the quest, the player
was permanently blocked: the item is no longer obtainable, so the
objective could never be met.

Quests now declare such items via a new optional `requiredItems` field
on QuestDef. On accept, the Sim re-grants any the player is missing. The
decision lives in a small pure module (`src/sim/quest_fallback.ts`,
`questFallbackGrants`) behind a `hasItem` predicate, unit-tested in
isolation, with the Sim a thin consumer.

This generalizes and replaces the single hardcoded keystone branch in
`acceptQuest`. `q_nythraxis_bound_guardian` now carries
`requiredItems: ['crypt_keystone']`, preserving the previous behavior
for all classes (the keystone is only a class reward for 3 of 9).

No new player-visible strings (the grant reuses addItem's existing loot
emit). Deterministic: no RNG involved.

fix(input): latch keyboard jump so fast taps survive the input sample window

A spacebar tap can be pressed and released entirely between two 20Hz input
samples (online send cadence and the offline sim-tick gap), so reading the raw
key-held state in readMoveInput() silently dropped it. That is the "every now
and then, seemingly random, jump stops working" report: short taps fell through
the gap while holds (sampled every tick) always worked.

The codebase already solved this exact edge-over-poll race for touch input
(triggerTouchJump / TOUCH_JUMP_LATCH_MS). This mirrors it for the keyboard:
onKeyDown (autorepeat already filtered) latches the jump for KEY_JUMP_LATCH_MS
(150ms > one 50ms window), and readMoveInput ORs the latch in alongside the
held-key and touch paths. Held jumps are unaffected (the key stays down); the
deterministic sim core is untouched (latch lives in src/game/).

Adds input.test.ts coverage (fast tap latches; held key still releases) and a
scripts/jump_latch_shot.mjs harness that reproduces 0/12 -> 12/12 fast-tap jumps
at max graphics.

had to press the attack keybind (slot 1) instead. Commit 6c069449 removed the
mob branch from handlePickedEntity's right-click handler, leaving only the
active-PvP-opponent case, so right-clicking an enemy targeted it but never

behavior: "Toggle auto-attack on your target. Right-clicking an enemy also
attacks." Right-click to engage is a load-bearing classic-MMO convention; left
selects, right attacks/interacts.

clickPickFromMouseGesture rejects a right-button gesture that moves past the

right-drag never produces a pick. Only a deliberate right-click reaches this
branch, so restoring it does not reintroduce aggro from camera rotation.

Restores the mob condition and flips the regression test to assert auto-attack
fires on a right-clicked hostile mob.

fix(mobile): only show touch UI on real touch-primary devices

Since the tablet-support change (PHONE_TOUCH_QUERY broadened to
"(pointer: coarse), (any-pointer: coarse)" plus a navigator.maxTouchPoints
> 0 clause), isPhoneTouchDevice fired on ordinary desktops and laptops
that merely expose a touch-capable peripheral: a precision touchpad and a
pen digitizer both report maxTouchPoints > 0 and match (any-pointer:
coarse) even though the primary pointer is a mouse. Those machines booted
straight into the mobile control UI (on-screen joystick and buttons)
across every browser, since the signal is OS/hardware level.

Tighten the query to "(pointer: coarse) and (hover: none)": the PRIMARY
pointer must be coarse AND unable to hover, which is true for phones and
hand-held tablets but false for any desktop/laptop driven by a mouse or
trackpad, regardless of attached touch/pen hardware. Drop the
maxTouchPoints clause (and the now-unused navigator argument) so a raw
touch-point count no longer forces the mobile UI; the native-app shell
still forces it via isNativeAppShell.

Rewrite the isPhoneTouchDevice tests for the new contract, including a
regression for the non-touchscreen laptop case. Removing the navigator
reference also lets the existing MobileControls lifecycle tests run under
the DOM-less Vitest env (they previously threw "navigator is not defined").

perf(render): frustum-cull off-screen characters (skinned rigs never self-cull)

Character rigs set frustumCulled=false on their skinned meshes — a skinned
mesh's bind-pose bounds don't track the animated pose, so Three's own cull pops
visible rigs out. The side effect is that every rig within draw range issues its
draws every frame regardless of being on-screen, which is the dominant cost
under a crowd (the per-character draws scale with entity count and are the #1
draw-call source once many mobs/players are around).

Add a manual, group-level frustum cull: build the world-space view frustum once
per frame and skip the draw for any non-self rig whose real world position +
a generous radius lies outside it. The rig's pose and footstep audio still
update (only the draw is skipped), and the radius leaves a margin so nothing
pops at the screen edge. Gated to shadowless tiers (low/lean) so a culled
off-screen caster can never drop a shadow that was visible in-frame; higher
tiers keep every rig for shadow correctness (and have the GPU headroom).

Measured offline with a dense crowd surrounding the player (≈180 visible rigs,
low tier): draw calls 975 → 786 (−19%), FPS 38 → 60 (+58%). Verified the
on-screen crowd still renders fully (no edge pop-out) and the local player is
never culled.

fix(sim): stop stationary mobs from hitting passersby out of reach

Excessive melee range: a mob's effective reach added a flat +3 yd
"moving target" grace whenever EITHER the mob or the target moved more
than 0.05 yd in a tick. Because that fired on target movement, a
stationary mob in a packed camp gained the full grace just because a
player walked past, swinging from ~8 yd (true range 5) and killing
low-level characters strolling by. Packed camps multiplied the effect.

The grace only exists to bridge 20 Hz position-sampling while a mob is
genuinely closing distance, so:
- gate it on the mob having moved this tick (pursuing), never on the
  target merely walking past a stationary mob, and
- shrink it from 3 yd to a tick-justified 1 yd (one tick of relative
  closing at ~7 yd/s is well under a yard).

A stationary scale-1 mob now reaches its true 5 yd; a pursuing one 6 yd.
Profiles that opt out (Nythraxis, movingRangeBonus 0) are unchanged.

fix(render): smooth camera-driven player facing instead of snapping

The player model's facing can be driven by the camera yaw: classic
right-mouse mouselook, or the always-on Mouse Camera mode while a movement
key is held. The renderer applied that override as a raw assignment
(`facing = renderFacingOverride`), with no rate limiting.

While the override is disengaged (standing still in Mouse Camera mode, or
before a right-drag crosses the camera-drag threshold) the player freely
orbits the camera while the model keeps showing the interpolated sim facing,
so the two diverge by up to 180 degrees. The instant the override engaged the
model snapped across that whole gap in a single frame: the character
"instantly rotated backwards", and right-mouse camera rotation made it snap
to a direction.

Rate-limit the local player's camera-driven yaw to a max angular velocity
(10 rad/s, well above intentional input: keyboard TURN_SPEED is PI rad/s and a
normal mouse drag is only a few degrees per frame). The model now rotates
smoothly to follow the camera; ordinary turning passes straight through and
only a discontinuity, or a violent flick, is smoothed. Scoped to the local
player (id === p.id); mobs and other players keep their existing
interpolation. Presentation-only: no sim, wire, IWorld, or i18n change.

The angle math is extracted into a pure, host-agnostic module
(src/render/facing_smooth.ts) with unit tests covering the shortest-path
wrap, the per-frame cap, multi-frame convergence, and pass-through of
sub-cap input. scripts/facing_snap_shot.mjs drives the live ?gfx=ultra build
and confirms the first-frame yaw change is capped at 0.167 rad (a teleport
would be ~PI).

A character name held only by a deactivated ("invalid") account stayed
reserved forever: deactivation is a soft delete (accounts.deactivated_at)

perf(render): prewarm all entity shaders to kill the crowd/zone-load freeze

Production profiling on a real GPU (driving the game via Playwright + the in-game
perf API) traced the multi-second freezes players feel when entering a populated
or varied area to synchronous WebGL shader-program compilation on first render of
a new model type: renderer.programs jumped 78->190 while traveling and the worst
main-thread block was 1713 ms.

Two root causes in the load-time prewarm:
- Coverage gap: it built only 18 representative mob templates and ZERO NPCs, so
  the other ~86 mob species and all 21 NPCs compiled their shaders live in-world.
- The compile timed out: programs.compile raced compileAsync against the leftover
  view-build budget (deadline - now); on a cold/larger scene the builds ate the
  budget and the async compile never settled, so even prewarmed materials (e.g.
  player classes) linked synchronously on first sight.

Fix (client renderer, load-time only):
- Prewarm one of every distinct mob MODEL (deduped by visualKeyFor, the model
  selector — mobs sharing a family model build once; the in-world pool still
  keys per template) + every NPC model + all player classes, building players
  first (the top trigger in a crowd).
- Give programs.compile its own budget (PREWARM_COMPILE_MAX_MS = 10s) so it
  finishes during the loading screen instead of racing the build budget to a
  timeout — capped modestly since a long hold there is worse than the freeze.
- Raise the prewarm budget and reserve tail margin (PREWARM_BUILD_RESERVE_MS) so
  the compile + final-frame steps always start before the deadline (runEntry
  skips entries that begin past it).

Verified on a real GPU (teleport tour across every zone + a player crowd): worst
freeze 1713 ms -> 223 ms (-87%); Webwood/Highwatch/crowd arrivals now compile 0
new programs with 0 long frames; prewarm completes in ~1.9 s with
compileTimedOut=false. The residual ~223 ms at the most content-dense far zones
is biome terrain + composed structures (not entities) — a separate, heavier
prewarm, left as follow-up.

fix(render): release WebGL contexts on page teardown

The client returns to the login screen by reloading the page: logout,

Switching the performance overlay's metric set from "Everything" back to
"Minimal" left the frame-time sparkline stuck at the wide (expanded) size; only

width) still fed the shrink-wrapped panel's max-content size, capped at the

clientWidth read stayed wide after the extra metric rows were removed: the

sizing: the panel now sizes to its rows and the graph follows it. The HiDPI
backing store is derived from a new pure helper frameGraphCanvasMetrics()
(unit tested); a fake-DOM regression test pins that the canvas never gets an
absolute px CSS width and that the wrapper (not the canvas) is what toggles.

fix(net): carry negative aura values on the wire so stat-saps read as debuffs online

A negative-value buff_* aura (a stat-sap: an AP or int drain riding a buff_* kind) is
classified as a debuff by auras_view.isAuraDebuff via `kind.startsWith('buff_') &&
value < 0`. The online wire dropped aura.value and the client decode hardcoded 0, so that
branch was offline-only: online the sap read as a buff, the low graphics preset's
debuff-priority aura cap could hide it, and the debuff border was offline-only.

The server now sends the aura value SPARSELY, only for a negative-value buff_* aura (the
exact predicate isAuraDebuff reads value for), sent raw so the sign survives the wire; the
client decodes `a.value ?? 0`. Positive buffs, absorb shields, and negative-value non-buff
auras (a fear's random facing angle) stay off the wire and decode to 0 exactly as before,
so no other online behavior changes (the absorb overlay stays offline-only). value is an
optional field, so the wire stays backward compatible in both directions.

Closes the graphics-fairness gap where a preset could hide an actionable debuff; the
classification stays in the UI (the wire only carries the data it was missing). A real
encode/decode round trip and the view to painter low-cap path are pinned by tests.

fix(render): default unrecognized first-run devices to the medium tier, not ultra

An unset graphicsPreset (a player's first boot before main.ts persists, or a
device whose detection stays inconclusive so nothing is ever persisted) used to
fall back to DEFAULT_PRESET=ultra in tierFromHints while the HUD/nameplate
data-fx-level fell back to the medium settings default, so an unrecognized
device (a masked GPU is roughly a third of clients: Safari "Apple GPU",
Firefox resistFingerprinting, Brave, Tor) launched the 3D pipeline at ultra
with the FPS governor switched off. That is the opposite of the intended
medium fallback and a 3D-vs-HUD divergence.

- tierFromHints now resolves an unset preset device-aware via
  resolveDefaultGraphicsPreset (medium fallback; recognized weak/software -> low;
  strong desktop -> high/ultra), so the 3D tier matches the medium data-fx-level
  on every first-run/inconclusive path without relying on the persist running
  first. An explicit stored preset still wins; software GL with no preset still
  floors to low; the URL-forced tier still takes precedence.
- shouldUseAutoGovernor now keys off the resolved tier (governor on for every
  non-ultra tier, including the medium fallback, so weak/unknown devices adapt;
  off only at ultra) instead of the unset-preset -> ultra label.
- classifyGpuRenderer's software clause now includes the bare "software" token
  so it stays in lockstep with isSoftwareGL, keeping the 3D and HUD tiers both
  low for a string like "Apple Software Renderer" (no low-vs-medium divergence).

perf(render): generic async-compile gate so new content never first-use-freezes (#1015)

* perf(render): generic async-compile gate so new content never first-use-freezes

THE ROOT CAUSE of the whole prewarm/shader saga: WebGL links a shader program
SYNCHRONOUSLY the first time a unique (material x geometry x render-state) combo is
drawn, stalling the frame 50-1700ms. The program cache key has ~70 axes (lights,
env map, shadow, skinning, instancing, UV sets, fog, tier...), so one material
spawns many program variants. The boot prewarm is a workaround that must reproduce
EVERY variant's exact render state up front - inherently incomplete (real-GPU walk
profiling caught an env-map-lit beast material linking ~240ms only when you walk
into a biome) and high-maintenance: every new mob/prop/effect/tier/state combo has
to be remembered or it freezes in-world.

Fix it generically: when a view streams in, link its programs OFF the main thread
(KHR_parallel_shader_compile via compileAsync) against the live scene's exact
lights + environment, and keep the view hidden until ready - it pops in a frame or
two late instead of freezing. This enumerates NOTHING, so current and future
content never hitches in-world; the boot prewarm degrades to a pure optimization
(already-compiled spawn content resolves instantly, no pop-in). Degrades safely:
no extension -> no gating (unchanged behavior); a 1.5s guard never strands a view
invisible if a driver stalls the compile queue.

NOTE: tsc + build green, but NOT yet live-verified (the dev session exhausted the
machine's Chrome-launch capacity); validate with scripts/profile.mjs walk before merge.

The async-compile gate hid every freshly-created view until its shaders linked,

* perf(render): budget entity-view point lights into the constant count

Real-GPU walk profiling (now that browser launch is unblocked) pinned a residual
open-world travel recompile: numPointLights toggled 6<->7 as the player moved, and
the 6->7 frame linked +6 programs. Cause: the quest-object glow (a PointLight per
ground quest object, quest_objects.ts) streams in/out with interest but was counted
OUTSIDE the constant fire-light budget, so it changed numPointLights - and Three
keys every lit material's program on the light count, so each toggle recompiled
them. The fire lights were already pinned to a constant visible count (and the
impact light folded in); entity-view lights were the gap.

Fold them into the same budget: createView registers a view's point lights, removeView
unregisters them, and budgetFireLights ranks fire + view lights together, keeping
exactly maxPointLights visible. View lights have no flicker pass to relight them, so
the budget drives their intensity directly (design intensity remembered once, so
pooled object views survive a budget that dimmed them). Verified in-world:
numPointLights now holds constant at 6 across a full traversal (was 6<->7).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(render): pool skinned visuals on overflow to stop bone-texture upload churn

Real-GPU upload profiling pinned an open-world asset-upload hitch to Skeleton
bone-matrix DataTextures churning: as mobs streamed in and out of interest, their
skinned visuals were disposed (Skeleton.dispose frees the bone texture) and
re-created (re-uploads it). createView only ever recycled the few prewarm-seeded
pool copies (PREWARM_MOB_POOL_COPIES per template); every mob past that count was
built fresh with its pool key NULLED, so removeView disposed it instead of pooling
it. With ~hundreds of mobs in interest, the bone textures cycled constantly
(measured: ~1400-2800 DataTexture deletes over a short walk, texMem oscillating
+/-150).

Fix: keep the pool key on a fresh (pool-miss) visual so removeView returns it to
the pool, which self-sizes to demand instead of disposing. The key is per template
(+color/scale), so the pool stays bounded by the peak simultaneous count. Also pool
NPC visuals (skinned too) the same way. Verified: 0 texture deletes over a 500-unit
walk (was ~1400-2800), texMem flat (swing 2, was ~150), pool bounded (~104 peak, no
leak), all mobs still render. Geometry-upload hitches are a separate source.

not swiftshader) and diffing program cacheKeys before/after each hitch: the dominant

every material's program cache key - never changes while travelling. The nearest
maxPointLights stay visible (one stable program per material); lights past the live
budget or out of range contribute nothing (intensity 0) but still count. The
impact-site light now rides the same budget (moved out of its cull-toggled group)
instead of flipping the count on its own.

dropped 34 -> 8 and the worst hitch 1375ms -> ~54ms; post-prewarm program count

fix(server): bound decodeBase58 input length before decoding (#959)

bs58.decode runs an O(n^2) loop, so a long attacker-controlled string fed
to decodeBase58 (via the wallet-link address/signature paths) pins the
event loop for the duration of the decode. The charset regex guaranteed
the decode never throws but said nothing about cost.

Reject any input longer than 128 chars before decoding. The longest input
we ever legitimately decode is a 64-byte ed25519 signature (~88 base58
chars), so 128 leaves comfortable headroom for every real address and
signature while bounding the work. Guarding inside decodeBase58 covers all
three callers (isSolanaAddress, verifySolanaSignature) at once.

Test-first: tests/wallet.test.ts asserts an over-long all-'1' string
(valid base58, so rejected by length alone) decodes to null, and that
inputs at the cap still decode.

fix(sim): despawn hunter/warlock pet when its owner dies (#974)

When a Hunter or Warlock player died, their summoned pet/demon became
immortal. handleDeath's player branch tore down the dying player's own
combat state and retargeted mobs off them, but never touched the owned
pet entity. The pet then hit a dead spot in updatePet: the despawn guard
only fires when the owner is ABSENT (logged out), and petPickTarget is
gated on `!owner.dead`, so a dead owner's pet could neither acquire
targets nor be cleaned up. It sat in the world at full HP, unkillable.

Fix: route the owner's live pet through handleDeath in the player-death
branch. The existing owned-mob death branch then applies uniformly:
warlock demons unravel (corpseTimer 3, fully despawn) and a hunter's
beast leaves a revivable corpse (corpseTimer Infinity, classic Revive
Pet). Neither stays immortal.

Pure sim/server-authoritative change behind the Sim/ClientWorld seam: no
IWorld member, wire field, or SimEvent added, so ClientWorld needs no
mirror (the client drops the demon entity / renders the hunter corpse
from the normal snapshot path). Killing an owned pet draws no rng, so the
parity gate's draw-order log is unperturbed (154 parity cases green).
Duels and fiesta takedowns resolve without handleDeath, so pets there are

perf(render): reuse one AnimState buffer instead of allocating per entity per frame (#786)

* perf(render): reuse one AnimState buffer instead of allocating per entity/frame

The per-entity sync loop built a fresh AnimState object literal for every
visible character every frame, purely to hand it to CharacterVisual.update()
and the pose-selection helpers. Those consumers only read the state within the
call and never retain it (the character-creation preview already drives a single
shared constant), so the allocation is pure churn that scales with on-screen
entity count — exactly the kind of per-frame garbage the renderer otherwise
avoids (cf. the pooled, allocation-free fire-light budget loop).

Hoist a single scratch AnimState onto the renderer and reassign its fields each
iteration. Identical values reach update(); it just stops minting N short-lived
objects per frame, easing minor-GC pressure (and the frame-time spikes a GC
pause causes) in crowded scenes. Reusing the buffer also benchmarks slightly
faster than the literal, so there's no downside.

swim pose still resolve correctly, no errors, frame rate unchanged.

* feat(sim): add Spell Power, an Intellect-derived caster damage stat

Casters were the one archetype whose damage did not scale with their primary
attribute: Intellect only fed the mana pool and spell crit, so a geared mage hit
no harder than a fresh one. This adds Spell Power, a derived combat rating (like
Attack Power) that converts Intellect into bonus spell damage.

Model (vanilla-style, tuning constants in types.ts, pure helpers in
src/sim/spell_scaling.ts):
- Spell Power = round(Intellect * 0.5) (1 Spell Power per 2 Intellect), plus a
  gear `spellPower` affix and a `buff_spellpower` aura, derived in
  recalcPlayerStats (the one place stats are derived).
- Direct nukes add SpellPower * clamp(castTime, 1.5, 3.5) / 3.5 (the coefficient
  caps at 1.0). The cast time is the RANK-RESOLVED one, so a rank-4 nuke scales
  off its real (slower) cast, not the rank-1 base.
- DoTs add SpellPower * duration / 15 spread across ticks, snapshotted at cast.
  A DoT that rides a direct nuke (Fireball, Pyroblast, Immolate) takes no extra
  Spell Power: the direct part already took the cast-time coefficient, so the
  rider does not double-dip. Pure DoTs (Corruption, SW:P) scale fully.
- AoE spells take a 0.333 penalty; channelled spells split the channel
  coefficient across ticks; Judgement (paladin holy nuke) scales too.

Applied at every spell-damage site: directDamage, aoeDamage, aoeRoot, dot,
groundAoE (combat/effect_dispatch.ts + sim.ts pulseGroundAoE), and channel ticks

* fix(sim): cap fleeing-mob speed at the player base run speed

A cowardly low-HP mob flees at FLEE_SPEED_MULT (1.4x) its base move
speed, capped at the player base run speed (RUN_SPEED) so a chasing
player can always catch and kill it before the flee drags in social
aggro. The cap was applied to the BASE projection and then multiplied

form_travel haste aura escaped the cap and outran the player:

Fold the multiplier inside the cap so the FINAL speed the mob travels at
is bounded by the player base run speed, while a slow aura still drags it
below the cap:

Extracted the flee-speed math into a pure src/sim/flee_speed.ts leaf with
a direct unit test (tests/flee_speed.test.ts). The common no-aura path
(mult === 1) is byte-identical, so the parity goldens stay green.

feat(sim): deal projectile damage on impact, not on cast (#990)

* feat(sim): deal projectile damage on impact, not on cast

Ranged attacks were hitscan: a spell cast, ranged auto-attack, channel
tick, or pet bolt emitted its `fx:'projectile'` visual AND resolved its
damage in the same 20 Hz tick, while the renderer flew the bolt at 26
yd/s. The damage number therefore popped before the bolt visually landed.

Re-time it: the launch site emits the visual now and schedules the whole
resolution (hit roll, crit/damage draws, dealDamage / runEffects) to run
when the bolt reaches the target. Because every Rng draw is deferred to the
landing tick, a projectile whose caster or target dies or despawns
mid-flight fizzles: it draws nothing and deals nothing.

- New pure leaf `src/sim/projectile_travel.ts`: PROJECTILE_SPEED (26, matches
  render/vfx.ts), projectileTravelTime (pure), and a PendingProjectile queue
  with scheduleProjectile / drainPendingProjectiles. Drained in the tick
  prologue on a fixed, deterministic phase boundary.
- All four hitscan sites defer through it: applyAbility (single-target spell),
  applyChannelTick (Arcane Missiles), rangedSwing (Auto Shot / Wand),
  petRangedAttack (imp bolt). Boss telegraphs (Nythraxis) already time-separate
  their damage from the visual, so they are untouched.
- `pendingProjectiles` is an append-only SimContext primitive view, mirroring
  delayedEvents; transient (not serialized).

Determinism holds (proven by the regenerated parity goldens, which the gate
re-records twice). The five forked goldens (casting, effect dispatch, auto
attack, pet, warlock pet) show the expected timing shift: damage rolls move
off the cast/swing tick to the landing tick. New unit + e2e tests in
tests/projectile_travel.test.ts; before/after chart via
scripts/projectile_impact_chart.mjs.

fix(talents): revalidate persisted talent allocations on load

A stored talent allocation replayed verbatim on load: addPlayer fed it
straight to computeTalentModifiers, which trusts the apply-time gate, but
the load path never ran validateAllocation. An over-budget, prereq-broken,
gated, or tampered build (stale tuning, a level-down, an edited save) still
granted its full stats and ability grants.

Add a pure, deterministic repairAllocation(cls, alloc, availablePoints) to
content/talents.ts: it rebuilds the allocation top-down (class tree then the
chosen spec, in row/col order), refilling each node up to its persisted rank
but never past a point validateAllocation would reject. Because every
prereq/pointsGate references rows above, a top-down fill satisfies them by
construction and the running budget check clamps the total. A spec is dropped
below FIRST_TALENT_LEVEL (availablePoints === 0). On an already-valid,
in-budget build it is the identity, so honest saves load byte-identically
and the parity gate is unaffected.

Call it at the load site in sim.ts, and at the deleteTalentLoadout auto-apply
(the one loadout path that bakes a stored alloc into live mods without a user
gate; switchTalentLoadout already validates).

fix(guide): frame the /wiki/models turntable from posed bounds

The live 3D turntable rendered several skinned creature rigs (wolf, murloc,
spider, kobold, demon, and similar) blank or off-frame while their baked
thumbnails were correct. It framed BIND-pose bounds at the spin-axis origin from
values measured before the mixer existed, and never disabled frustum culling, so
a rig whose idle clip displaces the mesh off the bind box fell out of frame.

Add a pure, Three-free framing module (frameTurntable) that re-centers the posed
bounds onto the Y spin axis and frames the bounding sphere by the tighter of the
horizontal/vertical fov, so the 4/5 inline embeds do not clip wide rigs. Measure
the POSED, skin-aware bounds in scene.ts after advancing the idle clip, and share
one skinAwareBounds across buildModel, the live viewer, and the still renderer so
they cannot drift. Re-frame on resize without re-measuring.

Critical: drive the skeleton with scene.updateMatrixWorld, not a mid-tree
root.updateWorldMatrix. three's SkinnedMesh refreshes bindMatrixInverse only in
updateMatrixWorld, so a mid-tree update measures posed bounds far off and frames
empty space. A single representative pose suffices (measured idle drift is under
about 10 percent of the radius).

tracking a posed bone.

fix(game): commit final camera yaw on mouselook release

Holding right-mouse to rotate the camera, then briefly releasing, left the
character a fraction of a turn behind the camera, and moving forward made the
follow camera backtrack to sit behind it (a visible snap).

Facing is only committed to the sim while mouselook is active (the per-tick
facing intent is set to camYaw). Input is sampled at frame rate but facing
commits on a 20Hz sim tick, so the slice of mouse motion between the last tick
and the release is dropped the instant mouselook turns off: the model then
settles back to a stale facing slightly behind the camera.

On the mouselook falling edge, latch the final camera yaw via a small pure
module (mouselook_release.ts) and fold it into movementFacing after the render
and controller overrides so it only fires when nothing else owns the heading.
The yaw is LATCHED rather than applied only on the release frame: offline a sim
tick runs on roughly 2/3 of frames, so a release on a zero-tick frame would
otherwise drop the one-shot. The latch is cleared once a tick consumes it
(offline) or once the per-frame stream sends it (online), and whenever the
camera or controller reclaims the heading.

Scoped to classic right-mouse mouselook; the always-on Mouse Camera mode has
its own facing path.

* fix(talents): revalidate persisted talent allocations on load

A stored talent allocation replayed verbatim on load: addPlayer fed it
straight to computeTalentModifiers, which trusts the apply-time gate, but
the load path never ran validateAllocation. An over-budget, prereq-broken,
gated, or tampered build (stale tuning, a level-down, an edited save) still
granted its full stats and ability grants.

Add a pure, deterministic repairAllocation(cls, alloc, availablePoints) to
content/talents.ts: it rebuilds the allocation top-down (class tree then the
chosen spec, in row/col order), refilling each node up to its persisted rank
but never past a point validateAllocation would reject. Because every
prereq/pointsGate references rows above, a top-down fill satisfies them by
construction and the running budget check clamps the total. A spec is dropped
below FIRST_TALENT_LEVEL (availablePoints === 0). On an already-valid,
in-budget build it is the identity, so honest saves load byte-identically
and the parity gate is unaffected.

Call it at the load site in sim.ts, and at the deleteTalentLoadout auto-apply
(the one loadout path that bakes a stored alloc into live mods without a user

* fix(game): commit final camera yaw on mouselook release

Holding right-mouse to rotate the camera, then briefly releasing, left the
character a fraction of a turn behind the camera, and moving forward made the
follow camera backtrack to sit behind it (a visible snap).

Facing is only committed to the sim while mouselook is active (the per-tick
facing intent is set to camYaw). Input is sampled at frame rate but facing
commits on a 20Hz sim tick, so the slice of mouse motion between the last tick
and the release is dropped the instant mouselook turns off: the model then
settles back to a stale facing slightly behind the camera.

On the mouselook falling edge, latch the final camera yaw via a small pure
module (mouselook_release.ts) and fold it into movementFacing after the render
and controller overrides so it only fires when nothing else owns the heading.
The yaw is LATCHED rather than applied only on the release frame: offline a sim
tick runs on roughly 2/3 of frames, so a release on a zero-tick frame would
otherwise drop the one-shot. The latch is cleared once a tick consumes it
(offline) or once the per-frame stream sends it (online), and whenever the
camera or controller reclaims the heading.

Scoped to classic right-mouse mouselook; the always-on Mouse Camera mode has
its own facing path.

fix(sim): keep the taunt/forced-target window counting down while a mob is stunned

The stunned-mob early return in updateMob (mob/locomotion.ts) exits before the
aiState switch that calls updateMobTarget, which is where forcedTargetTimer is
decremented. A stun landing mid-taunt therefore froze the taunt window for the
stun's full duration, stretching a 3s taunt into 3s + stun. A taunt/growl window
is real-time and must keep elapsing under crowd control.

mob/targeting.ts and call it on the stun path, without touching aggro (a stunned
mob cannot act; when the stun ends the normal path re-applies the forced target if
the window is still running). Untaunted mobs carry forcedTargetTimer === 0, so the
helper is a no-op for them and the parity draw-order is unchanged (gate green).

Tests: pure unit cases for tickForcedTarget plus an integration case driving a
stunned mob through updateMob and asserting the window ticks and expires.

Options > Interface. Using an offensive ability also engages your white-swing

measurement - it died, released spirit, and teleported to a graveyard, ending the

fix(server): isolate each session in the broadcast/event/tick hot loops (#949)

The 50 ms tick callback and the per-session broadcastSnapshots and
routeEvents loops iterated every session with no try/catch. A throw
while building or routing for one player's state unwound the whole

socket must not be able to crash the loop (server/CLAUDE.md).

persistent one degrades to a single bad session instead of all.

fix(net): terminate WS sessions on unbounded send backpressure (#950)

sendRaw checked only readyState, never ws.bufferedAmount. ws.send() never
blocks, so a client that stops draining its socket (frozen tab, wedged proxy,
or a deliberately non-reading attacker) accumulates an unbounded outbound
buffer. With a snapshot pushed to every session 20 times a second, one stuck
reader can OOM the whole process and starve every other player of snapshots
and events.

Guard sendRaw with a hard buffer limit (8 MiB, far above one legitimate burst
given the 16 KiB inbound maxPayload). When a session exceeds it, terminate()
the socket (close() would try to flush the already-huge buffer) and run the
idempotent leave() cleanup via the existing 'close' path.

The decision is a pure, unit-tested helper (server/ws_backpressure.ts); an
integration test drives GameServer with a fake socket to prove a stuck session
is torn down while healthy peers keep receiving snapshots.

* fix(market): realm-scope the World Market so realms stop clobbering it

The World Market was persisted to a single bare `world_state` row keyed
'market', shared by every realm process pointed at the same DATABASE_URL.
Each realm only ever overwrote that row from its own in-memory copy and
never re-read it, so two realms silently fought over it: whoever autosaved
last won, and the other realm's listings, escrowed items, uncollected
proceeds, and nextListingId counter were lost on the next restart. No
attacker required, and it leaves no log line when it triggers.

Everything else (characters, friends, guilds, presence) is already
realm-scoped; the market was the one global-state surface that was missed,
exactly the isolation DEPLOY.md promises for horizontal scaling.

Fix: key the market on `market:<realm>` in load/saveMarketState. Additive,
no schema change. On a realm's first boot its scoped key is absent, so we
copy (never move) the pre-scoping bare 'market' row into it, so existing
listings/proceeds are not stranded and every realm adopts the same starting

* fix(net): terminate WS sessions on unbounded send backpressure (#950)

sendRaw checked only readyState, never ws.bufferedAmount. ws.send() never
blocks, so a client that stops draining its socket (frozen tab, wedged proxy,
or a deliberately non-reading attacker) accumulates an unbounded outbound
buffer. With a snapshot pushed to every session 20 times a second, one stuck
reader can OOM the whole process and starve every other player of snapshots
and events.

Guard sendRaw with a hard buffer limit (8 MiB, far above one legitimate burst
given the 16 KiB inbound maxPayload). When a session exceeds it, terminate()
the socket (close() would try to flush the already-huge buffer) and run the
idempotent leave() cleanup via the existing 'close' path.

The decision is a pure, unit-tested helper (server/ws_backpressure.ts); an
integration test drives GameServer with a fake socket to prove a stuck session
is torn down while healthy peers keep receiving snapshots.

feat(professions): add tool effect slotting with durability and depletion (#1136)

Layers a slottable bonus effect on top of a base gathering tool: a
ToolEffectSlot carries its own durability, separate from the tool's tier.
applyEffectBonus adjusts a harvest/craft outcome (quantity, quality, or

feat(http): bound the two log-only mismatch sinks against flood amplification

The Content-Type and cross-site-Origin gates run ahead of the route-local
rate limiters, so a crafted mismatch flood on a mutating /api route could
amplify log volume one warn line per request. New mismatch_warn_throttle.ts
caps the default sinks at MISMATCH_WARN_MAX_PER_WINDOW (5) lines per

first line of each new window carries the prior window's suppressed tally,
so a flood stays visible. The throttle gates only the warn line: the
enforce decision (415/403) is unaffected, and neither enforce flag is
flipped. Clock injected for deterministic tests; cardinality is bounded by
the registered route table. Satisfies the pre-flip precondition recorded
beside DEFAULT_DISPATCH.

feat(net): linkdead grace holds disconnected characters in-world for 5 minutes

A dropped WebSocket no longer logs the character out. The session goes
linkdead: the character stays in the sim (still online for friends, the
play-session analytics row, and the concurrent-player counts) for a
5-minute grace window, and a re-auth on the same character resumes the
held session seamlessly (same pid, full snapshot re-sync, input acking
restarted). Logging in on a different character on the account displaces
the linkdead session immediately instead of being blocked by it. Forced
disconnects (moderation, takeover, anti-bot, kicks) bypass grace via the
existing leave() path, and a live duplicate join is still rejected so
takeover stays explicit.

Client side, ClientWorld auto-reconnects with exponential backoff behind
a translucent reconnecting overlay instead of dropping straight to the
fatal you-have-disconnected screen; a server error frame still ends the
session for good. The server also pings each live socket every 30s so
NAT/proxy idle timers stop silently dropping quiet (AFK) connections,
the root cause of the kicked-while-AFK reports, and a backpressure
terminate now lands in the grace instead of a full logout.

fix(net): resume after black-holed drops (pong liveness + bounded conflict retry)

Review follow-up (FernandoX7 on #1506). An abrupt drop that never delivers a
FIN/RST (mobile WiFi-to-cellular handoff, NAT rebind) left the server
counting the old socket as live, so the client's re-auth was rejected with
'character already in world' and the client treated that frame as fatal:
the resume never fired in exactly the case the grace exists for.

Two halves. The keepalive sweep now tracks pongs (browsers reply
automatically): a socket that misses a whole 30s ping interval is
black-holed and is terminated into the linkdead grace, so the server
notices an abrupt drop within a ping interval or two instead of TCP's
minutes. And the client, while a reconnect is in flight, tolerates the
in-world conflict rejection (bounded at 8 occurrences, pure decision in
src/net/reconnect_policy.ts) and keeps backing off instead of ending the
session, so a genuine takeover by another device's live socket still ends
in the fatal overlay.

Also drops the self 'has entered the world' notice on resume (the player
never saw themselves leave), and rebases onto the current release/v0.22.0
(generated i18n trio regenerated).

Verified with unit tests (keepalive sweep, pong-identity guard, policy
bounds) and a live black-hole E2E: paused TCP socket, early re-auth hits
the transient conflict, the sweep flips the session linkdead within 70s,
and the same-pid resume succeeds.

  depth floor at all.

  movement, mob locomotion, fishing) read the same per-position water
  surface instead of the global constant.

  not one plane spanning an entire zone's width.

refactor(equipment): make weapon requiredClass list every class that can equip

A weapon's requiredClass was an archetype SIGNATURE, not the real list: e.g.
Thronebane was ['warrior','paladin'] yet canEquipItem, via weaponArchetypeForItem,
opened it to the whole warrior-weapon group (warrior, paladin, rogue, hunter,

equip it. Weapons are proficiency-based, not class-locked, but the data did not
say so.

exactly the classes that can equip it (warrior group -> warrior/rogue/hunter/
shaman/paladin; caster group -> mage/priest/warlock/shaman/paladin/druid; rogue
group was already its full set). weaponArchetypeForItem now recovers the archetype
by matching that full list against each group set (order-independent equality)
instead of a subset of the legacy signature sets, so equip results and the item
tooltip (which still suppresses the redundant class line for group weapons) are
byte-identical to before. A future weapon with a genuine bespoke class lock has no
archetype and correctly shows its class line.

New guard: tests/equipment_proficiency.test.ts asserts, for every weapon with a
requiredClass, that the field equals exactly the set of classes canEquipItem
allows, so a weapon authored with the short archetype form fails until it lists the
full group.

fix(content): equalize heroic dungeon difficulty at level 22 (#1693)

Heroic 5-man difficulty was uneven and soft against geared characters.
The per-dungeon damageMultiplier ladder (3.4/3.8/4.2/4.6) made the four
heroics land wildly different hits, and the level-20 pin (equal to the
player cap) gave players maximum armor mitigation, so a full-geared mail
shaman took only ~160 per swing, roughly half the intended feel.

Retune the four five-mans so an average elite-trash swing lands ~300
post-mitigation on the reference geared shaman (full heroic mail: 2142
armor, 1493 hp, 48.55% DR vs a level-22 attacker), i.e. ~20% of max hp,
with final bosses ~22-24%. Solving each dungeon for that target inverts
the multiplier ladder, because the harder dungeons already carry bigger
base weapon damage:

  hollow_crypt      3.4 -> 6.8
  sunken_bastion    3.8 -> 6.2
  drowned_temple    4.2 -> 5.7
  gravewyrm_sanctum 4.6 -> 5.4

All heroic mobs (including the Nythraxis raid arena boss and its add
waves) now spawn at level 22 instead of 20. The raid keeps its 2.0
multiplier; the level bump raises its boss-on-tank swing from ~47% to
~54% of max hp and adds-on-cloth from ~50% to ~57%.

Level 22 is a deliberate gear gate: blues cloth takes ~76% per trash hit
and a trash crit one-shots, while the reference mail shaman sits at ~20%.
It also raises player-side miss (white 5% -> 19%, spell/CC hit 96% ->
82%) and mob armor/hp via the per-level terms, lengthening heroic fights.

Empirically validated with a scratch probe (not committed) that spawned
real heroic instances and measured landed hits: trash 284-307 avg,
bosses 321-354, Nythraxis boss ~467 and adds ~220, every mob level 22
with the heroic transform intact. Update the test pins that hardcoded
level 20 and the old multiplier table, add level-22 pins to the raid
add-wave test, and rewrite the stale calibration comment.

fix(game): hold camera follow through the touch-look release echo (no shake)

While touch swipe-look / the camera joystick / right-mouse mouselook is live,
every sim facing commit is an echo of camYaw, visible only through the render-
interpolated facing that lags the commit by up to a tick offline and a round
trip online. The instant the drag released, follow re-engaged and its rigid

heading the player chose; the settle term then dragged it back. That overshoot

latches the final camYaw and keeps follow disengaged (cameraDriven, which
still advances lastInterpFacing so re-coupling never snaps) until the
interpolated facing converges within the wire-rounding seam (0.02 rad), a
manual keyboard turn takes the heading, or an echo-scaled grace expires.
main.ts wires it into updateCamera for both the offline and online paths.

pre-fix bounce (documented as a mechanism pin) and proves the fixed path has

lockout-checked the player claiming a FRESH instance. One unlocked member

  final-boss death, lock every current member of the owning group plus any

  unconditionally from the death hub beside grantNythraxisLockout. The
  lockout no longer rides awardHeroicMarks (marks stay participation-gated).
- grantNythraxisLockout now locks the whole owning raid group via the same
  instanceLockoutMetas sweep (room radius kept as a no-claim fallback).
- enterDungeon door gate: a locked player may enter a live heroic claim
  only when its final boss is already down, so corpse-runs and loot
  retrieval into a cleared run still work but a locked party can no longer
  ride an unlocked recruit into a fresh run.

  vs lockout split, left-party-but-inside lock, recruit-ferry door gate,

perf(render): merge skinned rig parts so a remote player costs one draw, not nine (#1726)

* perf(render): merge skinned rig parts so a player costs one draw, not nine

KayKit character GLBs are mesh-quantized, and the glTF pipeline bakes each
primitive's dequantization transform into its own copy of the inverse bind
matrices. `sameBindData` read that as "genuinely different bind poses" and
bucketed every body part on its own, so `mergeSkinnedParts` never merged
anything: not one `_bodymerged` mesh existed in a live scene.

The cost was paid per remote player, every frame, in both the main and the
shadow pass: ~9 SkinnedMeshes, and because `SkeletonUtils.clone` clones a
Skeleton per SkinnedMesh, ~9 Skeletons each recomputing its bone matrices and
re-uploading its own GPU bone texture.

Those per-part inverses are not arbitrary: they differ from any canonical part
by ONE constant transform T, the same for every bone. Substituting that into
three's skinning equation collapses the difference to a single pre-transform of
the vertex, so rebaking a part's positions/normals by it makes the part skin
identically against the canonical skeleton and the parts merge safely.

`mergeSkinnedParts` moves to its own tested module, derives T per part, VERIFIES
it against every bone, and leaves any part it cannot prove safe unmerged.

Measured on the crowd profiler (ultra, 1920x1080, dpr 1, fresh server per build,
identical rig counts):

  90 players: 45.4 -> 61.3 fps (+35%), draw calls 65.7 -> 36.4, skeletons 900 -> 261
  60 players: 57.4 -> 72.2 fps (+26%)
  30 players: 72.1 -> 88.2 fps (+22%)

The win grows with the crowd, which is the point. Offline solo, GPU textures
drop 1000 -> 492 as the redundant bone textures disappear.

* perf(render): drop the quadratic nameplate declutter and crowd-scale anim cadence

Three per-frame costs that grow with the visible player count, found with the
CDP sampling profiler on the merged-rig build at 90 players:

1. `declutterNameplates` ran for every visible plate on EVERY rendered frame
   (it sits outside the painter's fullPass gate) and was quadratic: it cloned
   all anchors, built a Map, sorted a copy, then `.filter`ed the whole array
   once per unvisited anchor. The hot path is now `declutterNameplatesInPlace`:
   a reusable spatial hash over cells sized to the collision thresholds, so a
   cluster is found in its 3x3 neighbourhood, with zero per-frame allocation.
   A randomized oracle test pins it against the old O(N^2) rescan.

2. Every visible plate built TWO transform strings per frame: one in the
   projection loop and one again after declutter. The write is now deferred to
   the single post-declutter pass. The `{id,sx,sy}` anchors are pooled too.

3. The mixer throttle compared against the UNSCALED shadow range while the
   shadow bands themselves are crowd-scaled, so in a crowd every rig kept
   animating every frame. Both the near band and the mid cadence now follow the
   same crowd LOD (extracted to `crowd_lod.ts` as pure, tested policy).
   Sampling clips and rebuilding bone matrices is the per-rig cost that scales.

Animation smoothness is cosmetic, but a cast windup is a telegraph players react
to, so the local player, the current target, and anything mid-cast are now
exempted and animate every frame. The old code had no such carve-out: a casting
mob past 25yd already animated at half rate.

Self time at 90 players (8.2s window), growth from a 20-player crowd:
  nameplate_painter.update  +120.6ms -> +43.4ms
  PropertyBinding.apply     +181.0ms -> +100.4ms
  Interpolant.evaluate       +90.8ms -> +52.5ms
  slerpFlat                  +75.8ms -> +37.2ms

On a GPU-bound desktop this does not move FPS (the frame is submit-bound there:
+0.5%, inside noise). Under a 4x CPU throttle, which is where most clients live,
it is 11.3 -> 11.9 fps and 74.5 -> 70.9ms of renderer time at 90 players.

* test(render): pin the rebind law against the shipped character GLBs

The rig merge rests on a property of the real assets, not of our code: every
KayKit body part ships its own glTF `skin` (knight has 9 meshes and 9 skins),
and those inverseBindMatrices differ from any canonical part by ONE constant
transform, the per-primitive dequantization `KHR_mesh_quantization` bakes in.

Read the committed GLBs (decoding EXT_meshopt_compression to reach the
inverseBindMatrices), and assert for all eight player rigs that:
  - every skin rides the same joint list, in the same order,
  - each skin rebinds onto the canonical one through a single transform,
    with a residual well inside REBIND_EPS,
  - the bind data really is per-part (otherwise the test proves nothing).

If a re-export ever breaks this, the game stays correct (rig_merge refuses to
merge parts it cannot prove safe) but silently loses the optimization, which is
exactly the kind of regression a perf fix needs a guard for.

* fix(render): inherit frustumCulled on the merged rig, bound the declutter cell key

Two findings from the QA review of this branch:

- The merged SkinnedMesh did not carry `canon.frustumCulled` across, so it
  defaulted to true. Harmless today (visual.ts turns culling off on every rig
  after assembly, because a skinned mesh's bind-pose bounds do not follow the
  animation) but it silently re-decided a policy the rig owner owns. Inherit it.

- `cellCoord` now clamps each cell coord into 16 bits, so `cx * STRIDE + cy` is
  an injective packing rather than a hash that could grow unbounded (or go
  non-finite) for a point projected near the camera plane. Clustering is
  unchanged either way: a shared bucket only over-collects candidates, and
  membership is decided by the exact |dx| / |dy| test, never by the key.

Tests: anchors past the clamp share one edge bucket yet still cluster exactly as
the O(N^2) reference does; a non-finite projection does not throw.

Screenshots (docs/screenshots/rig-merge-*):
- crowd before/after: 91 players, same fresh server, 1920x1080, ultra, dpr 1.
  41.1 -> 63.1 fps, 1% low 30.8 -> 45.9, skeletons 900 -> 261, GPU textures
  1743 -> 694 (the per-mesh bone textures are gone).
- character-detail: magnified before/after of the same rig, showing the rebaked
  skinning is pixel-identical (helmet, visor, cape, limbs all intact).

* fix(render): pin the rig-merge guards and the crowd-LOD fairness carve-out

Review follow-ups. The merge algebra was right, but several of the things
keeping it SAFE were asserted only in prose, so a refactor could have removed
them with the suite still green.

Source:
- Extract the animation-cadence carve-out to `animatesEveryFrame` in crowd_lod.ts.
  It is the only thing keeping the crowd cadence compliant with the invariant that
  a perf knob may never delay actionable information (a cast windup is a
  telegraph), and it lived as an inline predicate in renderer.ts with no test.
- Refuse to merge a part carrying morph targets: `rebakeGeometry` rebuilds only
  attributes + index, so a blendshape would have been dropped silently. No shipped
  rig has one today; the module's contract is to leave anything unprovable alone.
- Carry `renderOrder` and `layers` onto the merged mesh, like the other flags. The
  merged part stands in for the canonical one and must present identically.

Tests:
- Pin REBIND_EPS and BIND_EPS to literals, and add a rejection case that deviates
  only just above the tolerance. The old assertions compared against the same
  constant the source uses, so loosening REBIND_EPS 1000x kept every test green.
- Cover the bind-matrix guard, the morph bail-out, and the render-flag inheritance
  (frustumCulled was itself a bug fix with no regression test).
- Cover `declutterNameplatesInPlace`'s `count` prefix bound: the pooled anchor
  array is only safe because of it, and every test called the 1-arg form.
- Extend the shipped-GLB rebind pin from the 8 player rigs to the 6 enemy rigs,
  which merge too and are what actually fills a dungeon crowd, plus a canary that
  no shipped rig grows a morph target.

A local `npm install` during the release merge pruned 15 lines from the lock
