fix(server): publish deed records only after the authoritative save lands

A rejected saveCharacter used to fall through to recordDeedUnlock anyway,
creating the one drift direction the insert-only join reconcile can never
heal: character_deeds, Renown, rarity, and Steam (chained off the insert)
claiming a deed the character blob does not have, permanently, if the

Unlock ids now queue on the session and saveCharacter publishes them after

unlock granted mid-write waits for its own queued save). A rejected save
leaves them pending for the next save attempt (30s autosave, next unlock,
or the leave save), so a transient failure delays the public record instead
of publishing ahead of the source; if no save ever lands, blob and index
stay consistently without the deed. The marquee broadcast is cosmetic and

fix(ui): focus the Book's close button on cold open

The focus trap only engages once focus is inside the dialog root, and the
game input path rebinds Tab to enemy targeting while focus stays outside,
so a keyboard user opening with Shift+Z could never enter the window.
Matches the sibling cold-window pattern (arena, spellbook, leaderboard).

fix(ui): render the viewer's active title in the lifetime-XP sticky self row

The off-page sticky standing hardcoded an empty title cell while regular
rows localize theirs, so a titled viewer lost their title exactly when
they fell off the visible page. The view-model now carries the deed id
(both worlds already expose activeTitle through IWorld) and the painter
localizes it the same way rowHtml does.

fix(server): fail closed on unknown deed ids across the public strips

The rarity payload and the public character-sheet recent strip treated an
unknown deed id as public. Production runs a mixed-version fleet over one
shared database, so a not-yet-upgraded (or rolled-back) process could serve
a newer hidden deed's descriptive slug anonymously, violating the hidden
contract (invisible until earned, existence included). Public surfaces now
require a known, non-hidden definition (isPubliclyListableDeedId); the
owner arm and the broadcast caller (which already pre-checks !def) are
unchanged, so an earner never loses their own content.

fix(server): count only eligible accounts in the realm-rank reads

The boards delist banned and suspended accounts via ELIGIBLE_ACCOUNT_SQL,
but lifetimeXpStanding and lifetimeXpRankForCharacter still counted them
in ahead and total, so the visible number one could be reported as rank
two. Both count arms now gate on the same eligibility predicate the
boards use; the ownership subquery stays ungated.

fix(sim): reset the delve deedMaxParty watermark on slot claim and free

The per-run party watermark only ever grew (Math.max in enterDelve), and
neither claimDelveRun nor freeDelveRun reset it, so a recycled slot that
once hosted a duo blocked dlv_solo_heroic for every later genuine solo
heroic clear in that slot until process restart. Both mirrored reset
lists now zero it beside deathsThisRun; the in-run watermark still
climbs, so a mid-run joiner keeps withholding the deed.

fix(guide): state the true per-character deed scoping on the wiki

The deeds page claimed every hero adds to one account-wide collection,
but the Book, Renown, titles, and progress are character-scoped; only
the realm leaderboard (and the Steam mirror) aggregate across the
account, counting each deed once. Reworded the English and re-translated
the full sentence in all 18 filled locales in the same change, since the
registry re-stamps srcHash on an English reword and would otherwise keep
stale fills marked translated. Resolved artifacts regenerated and the
sha256 baseline re-stamped in this commit.

fix(sim): key encounter restriction rosters on the stable character id

The Thunzharr death taint and the Morthen trio roster recorded transient
entity pids, so a mid-fight relog (which mints a new pid) laundered a
death out of the unbroken check, and a heal-only fourth member who died
and released, or walked out alive before the kill, vanished from the trio
count entirely. Encounter bookkeeping now stores deedCharKey (characterId
with a pid fallback for offline), the death scan records engaged
non-damagers for participant-tracked bosses, and the 1 Hz sweep folds the
boss's live threat table owner-resolved into the participant set. Pure
deed runtime bookkeeping: no rng draws, parity goldens byte-identical.
Recipient selection (presence-based credit) is unchanged.

fix(sim): mark deed evaluation on loadout save/delete and battlefield-XP skill gain

saveLoadout applied a staged talent build (spec and capstone included)
without the markTalentDeeds wrapper every sibling talent mutation uses,
deleteLoadout auto-applies the next loadout equally unmarked, and the
potion-drink battlefield-XP trickle could cross a craft-skill threshold
without a dirty mark. All three deed families ('flag', 'craftSkill', and
the talentPoints meter) are full-pass-only by design, so the grants sat
until an unrelated mark or relog. Each mutation site now marks exactly
like its siblings; the trickle marks only when skill was actually
granted, keeping the common plain-potion path mark-free.

fix(server): make Steam delivery at-least-once and squatted links reclaimable by proof

The mirror dropped an unlock permanently after four failed pushes, the
only reconcile ran at link time (which an already-linked account can
never reach again), and shutdown drained deed records but not queued
Steam work, so an outage or deploy could desync a permanent achievement
forever. character_deeds already is the durable idempotent outbox, so
reconcileOnLogin now replays a linked account's earned mapped deeds at
join, throttled per account (6h TTL), and shutdown awaits steamMirrorIdle
after deedRecordsIdle.

The push-time link revalidation moved inside the retry ladder so an
unlink or relink landing during backoff stops the remaining attempts.

A stolen-ticket squat is now recoverable without support surgery: a
fresh valid ticket proves current control of the Steam account (strictly
stronger than the squatter's stale stolen ticket), so the link handler
displaces the other account's link in one transaction, flips the old
owner's cached mirror view in-request, and reconciles the caller. The
same-account already-linked pre-check is unchanged, and the ticket.ts
residual-exposure comment now describes the real bound.

perf(ui): split the deed locale chunk per base locale

The lazy deed-i18n chunk packed all 18 locales into one ~531KB module, so
the homepage warm prefetch shipped a non-English visitor 17 locales they

* feat(social): operator-set AI and streamer account flair

Adds an admin-set account flair with two independent marks, surfaced in the game
client and set from the dashboard's existing account search.

AI accounts are DISCLOSED: an animated-rainbow [AI] tag renders immediately before
the player's name in chat, on the overhead nameplate, and on the target unit frame.
One shared .ai-tag CSS class serves all three (nameplates are positioned DOM divs,
not canvas textures, so the gradient is compositor-animated and costs no repaint).
Because it is a disclosure and not decoration, the tag carries role=img plus an
aria-label naming the MEANING: a title alone is announced inconsistently, and a
screen-reader user would otherwise hear the name with no hint a bot is behind it.

Streamers get NO chat marker. Their Twitch / X / Kick / YouTube links appear as
icon rows in the player context menu, opened from a chat name or a nameplate, and
only the platforms that have a link are shown.

The streamer URLs are operator-entered text that ends up in window.open on every
player's client, so normalizeStreamerLink (src/sim/account_flair.ts) is the single
security boundary and runs at four independent points: the admin write, the wire
encode, the render, and again at click. It is https-only against an exact
per-platform hostname allowlist, rejects embedded credentials, and is length
capped. The href is deliberately never interpolated into HTML (a single quote
survives URL normalization), and a mutation-verified guard pins that.

Flair rides two seams. Entity identity fields (ai / slk) cover players in interest
scope and re-broadcast for free on the identity diff, so an operator's flip lands
on connected clients with no reconnect. A sparse flair on the chat event covers
senders far OUTSIDE interest scope, which is the whole point: general, world, lfg
and guild chat reach you from players who have no local entity record. Guild and
officer chat never pass through routeEvents, so they are decorated at their own
fan-out site in SocialService.

An ordinary player's chat line is byte-for-byte unchanged on the wire.

Schema is three additive, idempotent columns on accounts (PG fast-default, no table
rewrite). The links bag is three-valued by design: an object replaces it, an explicit
{} clears it, and an ABSENT key leaves it untouched, so unmarking a streamer preserves
their stored URLs rather than making an operator retype four of them.

Reviewed by privacy-security-review (32 hostile payloads, incl. Cyrillic homographs
and java\tscript:, all rejected), migration-safety, cross-platform-sync, and the QA
gate. Every load-bearing wire line is now pinned by a mutation-verified test: the
guild/officer decoration, the routeEvents decoration, and the identity encoder could
each previously be deleted with the full suite still green.

The drain worker had no catch: a push attempt that rejected (a contract
breach anywhere below attemptPush) would turn the detached drain promise
into an unhandled rejection, process-fatal under Node defaults, and wedge
every queued push behind it until a future enqueue restarted the worker.

* perf(deeds): memoize multi-key dirty unions and single-flight the board refresh

Two measured hot spots from profiling at this head. (1) The multi-key
arm of deedListForKeys walked and filtered the full non-manual catalog
per dirty player per tick (a crit tick costs about 8x the single-key
shape, 141us at 100 players); the union is a pure function of the static

5min) before resolving, and awardSharedLootItem/assignMasterLoot granted the

inventory. This is the "loot bugs during rolls in heroics and I lose the
gear" report: in a busy heroic run a party member frequently drops or logs
during the roll window, and the winner they picked evaporates for everyone.

return the item to the corpse exactly like the everyone-passed branch
already does, instead of destroying it.

fix(input): request pointer lock synchronously on Firefox mousedown (#1840)

* fix(input): request pointer lock synchronously on Firefox mousedown

Firefox denies Element.requestPointerLock() unless the call happens
synchronously inside the handler for the user gesture itself (mousedown), not
a later mousemove once the drag threshold is crossed, even though that
mousemove fires within the mousedown's lingering transient activation window.
Its own error message says so: "was not called from inside a short running
user-generated event handler, and the document is not in full screen."
Chromium is lenient and happily consumes the lingering activation from the
deferred mousemove call, which is why this only broke Firefox.

Add pointerLockNeedsSyncGesture (UA sniff) and
shouldEngagePointerLockOnMouseDown to the pure src/game/pointer_lock.ts
decision module, gated to the button that can start a camera drag in the
active camera mode so a plain click-to-move click never triggers it. input.ts
requests the lock from onMouseDown on Firefox and keeps the existing
deferred-mousemove path on Chromium, unchanged, so the #116 fix (no banner
spam on a quick right-click) is untouched there.

Fixes #1834

* fix(input): cover both drag buttons and fix pointer-lock edge cases

Address review feedback on #1840: shouldEngagePointerLockOnMouseDown now
covers both left and right buttons (camera drag can start on either, in
either camera mode), not just the active mode's nominal look button, so
Firefox left-drag orbit in Classic mode and right-drag in Mouse Camera
mode both get the synchronous lock request.

Explicitly excludes the click-to-move button from the synchronous
request instead of implicitly restricting to one look button, since a
plain click on that button must not take the lock. This keeps #116
fully fixed only on Chromium: an ordinary Firefox right-click used to
loot/target/interact still takes and releases the lock, a visible
flicker, an accepted trade-off documented at the call site and in
shouldEngagePointerLockOnMouseDown.

Also: guard against a fast mouseup beating the async requestPointerLock()
grant (pointerlockchange now exits the lock if it lands with no drag
button held), swallow the requestPointerLock() rejection on the
mousedown call site, and replace the local Firefox UA regex with the
existing detectBrowserEngine() from browser_env.ts.

fix(ui): bind death-screen respawn buttons via touch-tap (#1624)

On a phone the browser only synthesizes a compatibility 'click' for the
PRIMARY pointer, so any button wired with a bare addEventListener('click')
goes dead the moment a second finger is already down. The three death-screen
buttons (Release Spirit, Resurrect at Corpse, Resurrect at Spirit Healer)
were still on bare 'click' while every other touch-facing HUD control had
been migrated to bindTouchTap. A player who died mid-run with the movement
joystick still held (the joystick finger owns the primary pointer) could tap

release command reached the server, the ghost flag never flipped, and the
death overlay (keyed off dead and not ghost) never cleared. Stuck on the
death screen, exactly as reported, and only on mobile.

the more-menu close, and every other touch-facing button. bindTouchTap keeps
the desktop mouse and keyboard (Enter/Space) path, so there is no desktop
regression; this is purely additive touch handling. No server, wire, or sim
change: the online release path itself was already correct, the tap just
never reached it.

tests/client_shell.test.ts asserts all three buttons use bindTouchTap and
none is left on a bare click binding (the same source-scan pattern that
already guards the more-menu close X).

fix(audio): restore no-repeat-biased random SFX variant selection (#1901)

#1818 (the SFX Studio production overhaul) replaced the no-repeat-random
variant picker from #1771 with a plain sequential cursor (nextVariantIndex/
commitVariant just incrementing 1, 2, 3, 1, 2...) as part of a from-scratch
rewrite of the buffer/loading model. Not a deliberate change, collateral
damage from the class rewrite, but it turned every multi-take SFX (most
visibly footsteps) into a metronomic cadence instead of sounding organic.

Restores randomized selection, adapted to the current variants/failedLoads
shape rather than #1771's original variants/lastVariant Map<string,
AudioBuffer[]>. Weighted rather than hard-excluded this time: the
immediately previous variant gets a low (0.15) weight instead of zero, so a
2-take pool (hard exclusion degenerates into rigid A-B-A-B alternation,
itself still metronomic) gets real randomness, while an occasional
back-to-back repeat stays rare. A variant that failed to load is still
skipped outright, which #1771's original didn't have to handle (no lazy
loading existed yet).

Updated the three sfx_loading.test.ts tests that pinned the old sequential
order to the new weighted rolls, and added two decisive tests: one proving
distinct variants land correctly across a 3-take pool, one proving an
occasional repeat is still reachable (not hard-excluded) on a low roll.

fix(ui): preview every chroma swatch on hover in the character creator (#1627)

In the character creator, hovering an outfit (chroma) swatch inconsistently
updated the avatar preview: after selecting one outfit, hovering the swatch
directly next to the selected one did nothing, while non-adjacent swatches
previewed fine.

Each swatch carried its own mouseenter (preview this chroma) AND its own
mouseleave (revert to the selected chroma). When the pointer moves directly
between two adjacent swatches, the departed swatch's mouseleave and the
entered swatch's mouseenter both fire, and their order is not guaranteed. In
Firefox the mouseenter ran first (preview the hovered chroma) and the
neighbor's mouseleave ran second (revert to the selection), so the preview
snapped straight back and the hover looked like a no-op. Only the swatch
adjacent to the current selection is affected, which is why it read as
"outfit 1 does not update" in the report (outfit 2 was selected).

Extract the wiring into src/ui/skin_picker.ts and bind the revert ONCE on the
row instead of per swatch. A row-level mouseleave does not fire on
child-to-child transitions, so every swatch previews consistently on hover
and the preview still reverts to the committed selection exactly when the
pointer leaves the picker. renderSkinPicker becomes a thin consumer that
builds the portrait swatches and delegates the interactions.

tests/skin_picker.test.ts drives the wiring with a hand-rolled fake DOM and
reproduces the exact repro: with outfit 2 selected, hovering its neighbour
previews; moving between swatches never reverts; leaving the row reverts to
the committed selection; and a click commits and moves the selection.

fix(net): re-derive follow-up quest availability immediately after turn-in (#1897)

Talking to an NPC right after turning in a quest that gates a follow-up
quest (requiresQuest) showed the default dialog instead of the new quest,
even though the player already qualified. Closing and reopening the
dialog once the exclamation mark reappeared showed it correctly.

Root cause: ClientWorld.turnInQuest() is a fire-and-forget wire command.
The HUD's renderGossip() already re-queries questState() live for every
quest right after the turn-in click, so the UI re-render was never
stale. The staleness was in ClientWorld.questState() itself: its
prerequisite check (quest.requiresQuest && !questsDone.has(...)) reads
questsDone, which only updates once the server's qdone snapshot field
round-trips, so any OTHER quest gated on the one just turned in stayed
"unavailable" until the next snapshot arrived.

Extend the existing pendingQuestCommands optimism (already used to show
the just-turned-in quest as active) to prerequisite checks for every
other quest: while a turnin command is in flight, treat that quest as
done when resolving anyone else's state. Extracted into a pure,
DOM-free module (src/net/quest_state_optimistic.ts) per the module-first
convention, host-agnostic and unit-tested without spinning up
ClientWorld.

* feat(sim): manual bag order, drag a stack onto any bag cell

Dragging a stack onto another bag cell now puts it there. The bag grid paints the
inventory ARRAY (its default view is literally the unsorted list), so a cell IS an
index and the drag is a reorder of that array, which is serialized with the
character: the arrangement survives a relog.

The array is dense, which decides the two cases: a drop on a filled cell SWAPS the
two stacks, and a drop on a free square moves the stack to the END (an array with no
holes cannot hold a stack "somewhere in the empty space"). The new inv_move command
is authoritative like every other inventory verb: the sim re-validates both indices
against the live bag, so a hand-crafted pair cannot duplicate or drop a stack.

Reordering is only offered in the raw-array view (no sort, no filter, no search).
Under a quality/name sort or a category chip the grid is a derived view where a cell
names no position, so the cells are not stamped and the drop is refused rather than
guessing an index and moving the wrong stack.

New pure leaf: src/sim/inventory_order.ts, shared by the sim command and the HUD's
drop feedback so the two can never disagree.

* fix(ui): never refuse a bag reorder silently, and allow it under a filter

A drop that does nothing is indistinguishable from a broken drag, and that is what

Two changes. A category chip or a search only HIDES stacks (the survivors keep their

now allowed. A quality/name sort genuinely REORDERS the view: a cell names no array
position and the sort would put both stacks straight back, so that view refuses the

fix(server): production stability hardening for reconnect, brownouts, admission, and ops (#1930)

* docs: codex plan

* chore(agents): add database-performance-reviewer and wire its dispatch

* feat(sim): add mob.update attribution counters behind the perfLap seam

The mob AI scan hot paths (both idle aggro-scan callbacks and both
threat-table walks) bump two plain integer visit counters through the
SimContext seam, held in the new pure leaf src/sim/mob/scan_counters.ts,
reset at the top of tick(), and exposed to the host via a readonly
getter. SimConfig.perfLap also gains an optional subkey so the per-mob
lap carries e.templateId. The counters feed no gameplay branch and draw
no rng, so the deterministic core is unchanged.

* feat(server): bucket the mob.update lap and surface scan counters in the heartbeat

The injected perfLap probe attributes each mob.update lap to a
per-family profiler bucket (MOB_UPDATE_BUCKETS appended to
SIM_LAP_PHASES, with a memoized templateId lookup behind
perfDetailActive), so a hot mob family shows up in a capture instead of
hiding in the aggregate. The [perf] heartbeat gains aggroVisits= and
threatVisits= tokens, and PerfCaptureResult gains four accumulator
fields folded per tick by the new server/mob_scan_tick_stats.ts module
and mirrored in the admin types.

* test(server): pin the bucketed lap output and the counter observer proof

Pins the 27 base lap names and the 12 family buckets as literals
against the derived SIM_LAP_PHASES, proves family attribution end to
end through the real probe (a beast mob and the other fallback), unit
tests the capture fold (totals versus per-tick peaks, the non-capturing
freeze, reset semantics), and adds exact-count scenarios for every
counter increment site plus a 50-tick pure-observer proof that reading
the counters leaves the world bit identical.

* docs: require a body in every commit message

Commits on this repo were landing as bare titles, which leaves no
record of intent when reading history. The Conventions section now
requires a short body (what changed and why) after the title on every
commit, alongside the existing Conventional Commits scope rule.

* perf(sim): resolve the scan-counter view once per mob scan

The four increment sites resolved ctx.mobScanCounters through its live
getter chain once per visited candidate, inside the exact hot loops the
counters exist to measure. Each site now hoists the view into a local
before its loop, and the module header states outright that the counters
are deliberately always on in every host.

* fix(server): tie the mob.update buckets to the MobFamily union

MOB_UPDATE_BUCKETS was a hand-maintained literal with no link to the
MobFamily union, so a future family added to the union would derive a
bucket name TickProfiler never registered and its mob.update timing
would be silently dropped. The satisfies clause now rejects any
non-family entry at compile time; the matching exhaustiveness pins land
in the capture test suite.

* test(server): close the loop-fold and family-coverage gaps from review

The capture accumulators were only ever asserted at zero because every
test drove sim.tick() directly, so deleting the per-tick fold in the
GameServer loop kept the suite green while shipping empty captures; a
new test drives the real interval loop with a dead player in an idle
wolf's scan radius and pins non-zero sums, the per-tick peak, the
threat side staying zero, and the accumulator reset on a fresh capture.
Also adds the type-level MobFamily exhaustiveness pin plus a runtime
check that every family used by MOBS is bucketed, pins the four capture
fields against the admin dashboard mirror in both directions, asserts
the two heartbeat tokens, folds the rng internal state into the
observer-proof world comparison, and corrects the stale comment that
claimed a non-zero-sums test already existed.

* feat(scripts): add the mob-stall co-location repro harness

Reproduces the #1833 co-located-crowd shape against a local dev server:
seeds disposable bot clients, teleports them into one tight cluster,
stages idle-crowd, mass-pull, or boss-pulse, and records the
PERF_TICK_LOG heartbeat, the per-family mob.update buckets, and frozen
perf-capture windows as JSONL under tmp/. Both the game-server target
and the database host are loopback-enforced, and every seeded row
(including the throwaway ops.perf admin account that enables captures)
is deleted at cleanup.

* test(scripts): extract the stall-harness parse logic into a pinned lib module

The heartbeat and simline regex parsers, the staging thresholds, and the env
clamp helper move from the harness entry script into scripts/lib/mob_stall_parse.mjs
with a hand-written .d.mts, per the scripts module-first rule. The new Vitest
suite pins the formats with real captured server lines (tick= must not capture
tickMs= or tickHz=, family buckets, absent-means-missing, the OVER token) so a
silent parse regression cannot corrupt future regression numbers. Also treats a
set-but-empty numeric env var as unset instead of clamping 0 to the minimum.

* fix(scripts): harden the mob-stall harness after its first review pass

Reads the wire fields as actually encoded: dead is numeric 1 omitted while
alive and health rides under hp (h is the hostile flag), so dead bots now
release, respawn, and re-tap, which lets mass-pull and boss-pulse sustain their
threat tables through death waves instead of decaying to an empty field, and
corpses no longer consume tap dwells. Closes a loopback-guard bypass by
resolving the DATABASE_URL host with pg-connection-string (a ?host= query
override defeated the WHATWG hostname check). Hardens operator failure modes:
fail fast when the child server dies or SERVER_LOG is unreadable, distinguish
missing heartbeats from a genuine staging miss, tear down on SIGTERM/SIGHUP,
register seeded accounts for cleanup as they are created, refuse pre-existing
usernames and reused results files, shorten seeded tokens to one hour, and
report bot deaths in the summary. Parsing now comes from the tested lib module.

* fix(sim): narrow idle aggro scans to MAX_AGGRO_RADIUS

Both idle scan sites queried the player grid at radius 25 while the
effective detection radius is clamped to MAX_AGGRO_RADIUS (20) and every
further modifier only shrinks it, so the extra band only visited players
that could never be detected. Querying at the clamp is behavior-identical
(detection is strict, d < radius) and sheds the never-detectable visits
under co-located crowds; the scan-counter boundary pins move to the new
radius in the same change. Parity stays green with zero re-baselines: the
scans draw no rng and the surviving cell walk keeps its visit order.

pins per-tick aggro-scan visits to the exact mobs-times-players product
(with a former-window ring that must contribute zero visits), and a

* feat(net): jittered reconnect backoff behind a pure computeBackoffDelay module

Every dropped client used to replay the same deterministic 1s/2s/4s/8s/15s
schedule with a zero-delay visibility retry, so a server restart made the
whole population re-hammer the server in lockstep. socketClosed now draws
each delay from a full-jitter band (0.5x to 1.5x of the step, capped at the
max) via the new injectable-rng module, the visibilitychange fast retry is
spread across 0 to 1000 ms instead of firing on the same beat, and both
timer callbacks clear their stale handle before opening so a foreground
event mid-connect can no longer double-open a socket.

* feat(net): treat the server auth-timeout rejection as transient with its own bound

The 'authentication timed out' rejection is only ever sent by the
first-frame auth timer in server/ws_auth.ts, which fires during server
event-loop stalls or reconnect races, never on a credential verdict or a
database brownout (the timer clears before any database work runs). A
reconnecting client now keeps backing off through it instead of ending the
session, bounded by a separate timeoutRejections counter (20, sized to
outlast a saturation stall episode where the conflict bound of 8 covers
only the keepalive sweep) that resets with the conflict counter on a
successful hello. The fatal path still delivers the raw untranslated
literal, matching the diagnostics passthrough.

* test(net): reconnect policy and backoff schedule coverage

Pins the jitter band, cap, and strict positivity of computeBackoffDelay at
both rng extremes and the midline across all 40 real attempts, the timeout
predicate's own bound and its independence from the conflict predicate by
string and by counter, and the wire literal on both sides (the client
constant plus a source-text pin of server/ws_auth.ts, whose error table is
not exported). The visibility suite's stubbed rig now records timer delays
and routes the bare global clearTimeout, pinning exact delays (1250 backoff,
750 and 420 spread) under a stubbed rng: foregrounding replaces the long

timers, and a foreground while the fresh socket is still connecting opens
nothing.

The backoff header claimed a jittered span of roughly 4.5 to 14 minutes, but

across 40 attempts is roughly 4.6 to 9.4 minutes with an expected total near 8
minutes. The reconnect_policy note also implied api_error_i18n.ts carries a
match arm for the auth-timeout literal; it is deliberately an unmatched
protocol diagnostic, so the comment now says that instead.

The pure predicates were unit-tested but nothing drove ClientWorld.onMessage
with the frames themselves, so reverting the tolerance block, swapping the
counter, or dropping the reset on hello all passed the suite. New cases drive
an auth-timeout error frame mid-reconnect (session survives, own counter
increments, hello resets it), a fatal rejection (session ends, verbatim reason,
pending retry cleared), the backoff callback clearing its own timer handle, and
close() clearing a pending spread retry. Also pins the second server copy of
the conflict literal in the ws_auth source scan alongside the timeout entry.

* feat(server): pool timeouts, error handler, and heavy-aggregate exemptions

Give the pg pool a connect deadline (5s), a server-side statement_timeout
session default (15s), and a client-side query_timeout backstop that sits
above the raised heavy allowance, since a driver timer cannot be lifted by
SET LOCAL. The known heavy aggregates and both character save functions run
through a new runWithStatementTimeout helper (BEGIN, SET LOCAL, COMMIT on a
checked-out client) at a bounded 60s; boot DDL moves to a dedicated non-pool
client so no request deadline can cancel the advisory-lock wait or the market
backfill. An idle-client pool error is now logged and counted instead of
crashing the process, and a database failure during the WS handshake is
caught at the caller and converted into the existing retryable timeout
rejection instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection with no error frame.

* feat(server): same-account character-lease takeover with additive account_id

character_leases gains a nullable account_id column (additive, idempotent,
no backfill) stamped from the authenticated account at every acquire, and the
upsert steal predicate gains a same-account arm alongside expiry and
same-holder, so the owner can reclaim a lease stranded by a dead or wedged
process before the TTL expires while a foreign account still fails closed
(NULL rows match no arm under plain equality). The steal re-stamps the nonce
in the same atomic statement, and both character save functions accept an
optional lease nonce that fences the write with an EXISTS probe inside the
UPDATE itself, so a displaced session's in-flight save matches no row instead
of clobbering the new holder; a fenced-out session is kicked with the
existing takeover signal rather than left playing unsaved.

* fix(server): self-clocked keepalive sweep

pingLiveSessions ran on a fixed interval and terminated every session still
awaiting a pong from the previous round, so a single event-loop stall longer
than the interval mass-terminated every connected client whose pongs sat
unprocessed in the queue. The sweep now records its own last-run timestamp
and, when it fires later than 1.5x the interval (the process stalled, not the
clients), terminates nobody and re-arms every live session instead; a
genuinely dead socket still terminates one clean interval later. The
threshold decision lives in the new pure server/keepalive_sweep.ts module.

once game.clients.size plus the in-flight fresh admissions reaches the configured

Api.realmStatus now reads players_cap (guarded to a positive number, 0 for older

Add the env passthrough to the game service allowlist and a commented .env.example

* fix(server): treat a whitespace-only realm cap value as unset

Number('   ') is 0, so an untrimmed MAX_PLAYERS_PER_REALM containing only
stray spaces read as an explicit 0 and silently disabled the admission cap,
unlike other garbage values which fall back to the safe default. The read is
now trimmed, scoped to this key because retention-style keys sit on the safe

and a spaced explicit 0 to 0.

The realm-full refusal now has its localization hop pinned: the server emit
and the FATAL reconnect classification were already covered, but a drifted
matcher literal would have shipped raw English on the refusal overlay with
every test green (verified by mutating the literal). /api/status players_cap

corpus. The population banding suite gains sub-cap cases proving a positive

* feat(server): expose game-loop liveness on /livez with a drain exemption

GET /livez now answers 503 once the authoritative game loop has completed no
tick pass for longer than LIVEZ_STALE_MS (30s), so a wedged world loop whose
HTTP surface still answers is detectable from outside the process. Draining
keeps /livez at 200 and wins over staleness, so a graceful shutdown is never
misread as a wedge. A loop-start backstop (loopStartedAt) covers the boot-time
case where the loop throws on its first pass and never completes one, which
would otherwise leave the last-pass timestamp null and read as warmup forever.

The liveness source is injected from inside startServer via registerLivenessSource
and read from a module slot, so a /livez probe never constructs a GameServer
(the lazy-boot pin holds). /readyz is unchanged: 503 on drain only, no liveness
input. Health bodies stay plain dev-channel English.

* feat(ops): game container healthcheck, stop grace, memory limits, NODE_OPTIONS

Give the game service a real health signal and enough time to shut down. The
healthcheck probes GET /livez with a node one-liner (the alpine runtime image
has no curl) that exits nonzero on a non-200 status and on a refused connection,
so docker turns a wedged loop into an unhealthy container. stop_grace_period is
75s to cover the shutdown chain (saves, FIFO drains, the Steam mirror deadline,
lease release, pool close) with headroom over the runbook's stop -t 60 fallback.
mem_limit 5g plus memswap_limit 5g cap the container so a runaway process is
OOM-killed inside its cgroup instead of taking the host down, and a leak cannot
lean on host swap. A NODE_OPTIONS passthrough lets a deploy size the V8 heap
under mem_limit; it ships empty (empty means node's defaults) and is documented
in .env.example. Nothing is baked into the Dockerfile.

Pins for every new line, scoped to the game service so a knob cannot pass on the
wrong service, plus a Dockerfile CMD-tail pin (node must be the final exec so it
receives SIGTERM as PID 1, which the stop grace depends on).

* feat(deploy): game watchdog and the hardened update runbook

Docker's restart: unless-stopped only fires on process exit, so a wedged but
alive container needs an external watcher. deploy/game_watchdog.sh restarts the
game container only when docker reports it unhealthy, and only when it is
running (a stopped container keeps its last health status, so a running-check is
what stops the watchdog from fighting a deliberate stop). It carries a lock, a
cooldown above the healthcheck re-evaluation floor, a dry-run mode, and never
touches a draining container. user-data.sh installs it via cron with logrotate.

The DEPLOY.md update runbook now pulls the private bot-detector clone and runs a
type-check drift gate before the image is built. The gate runs in a node
container (the deploy host has docker but not node), with the host .env dropped
and dependency install scripts disabled so a deploy cannot leak production
secrets or run untrusted install hooks as root. The Caddy config keeps /livez,
/readyz, and /metrics off the public edge so /livez is not a public wedge oracle.

The watchdog is exercised end to end against a fake docker and flock on PATH, so
a behavior change that keeps the pinned literals intact still fails the suite.

* test(server): correct a stale fake-timers note in the health test header

The liveness suite gained an exact-boundary case that fakes the clock to land
precisely on the 30 second window, so the header note claiming the window is
never driven by fake timers is no longer accurate. Reword it to say most cases
use a reported age while the one exact-boundary case fakes the clock.

* test(server): pin the liveness staleness-read precedence and the late-step stamp

The staleness read prefers the completed-pass clock over the loop-start
clock, but no case distinguished the two operands: swapping them kept
every suite green while a healthy server past 30s of uptime would answer
503 and be restart-looped. Pin the fresh-pass-stale-start case at both
the health layer and against a real running loop, and pin that a throw
from the final pre-stamp step (flushPeriodicSaves) leaves the stamp
untouched. All three pins verified decisive by mutation.

* fix(deploy): close the ops-endpoint edge gap on existing hosts and widen the gate sweep

The Caddy 404 block for /livez, /readyz, and /metrics only lands via
first-boot provisioning, and the runbook still told operators the two
probe paths stay open, so a host provisioned earlier keeps exposing
/livez, which can now answer 503 and tell anyone polling it when the
world loop is down. Document the by-hand retrofit (matcher, validate,
reload, verify), align the by-hand Caddyfile example, and point scrape
jobs at loopback. Also sweep every .env and .git out of the type-check
gate copy instead of only the top-level .env, strengthen the generic
drifted-detector guidance in the post-deploy verification, and include
the cron poll in the stall-to-recovered budget.

Test side: execute the probe extracted from the pinned healthcheck line
against real 200, 503, and refused endpoints; run the watchdog twice to

and sha256 baseline are regenerated in the same change so the freshness and

The per-IP hard-limit refusal previously closed the socket raw with code 1008,
so the player saw nothing while the client silently retried into the same cap.
It now rides the same {t:'error'} frame as every other handshake reject, with a
byte-exact client matcher arm localizing it and the reconnect policy keeping it
fatal. The refusal decision logic is unchanged; the load harness scripts now
surface their cap hint off the error frame instead of the retired close code.

sessionsByDay, clientPerfSummary, the accountDetail playtime aggregate, and
pruneChatLogs now run through runWithStatementTimeout at the heavy allowance,
matching their interval-driven siblings; clientPerfSummary threads one bound
client through its helpers. The player character-select read deliberately stays
on the default timeout so logins fail fast during a brownout, pinned by a new
negative test alongside per-function wrapper pins.

* fix(sfx): measure export conformance with the bundled ffmpeg toolchain

The export bundle validated published clips with the PATH ffmpeg while the
conform gate measures with the bundled ffmpeg-static, and the two disagree by
tens of milliseconds on MP3 duration, flipping four clips across the one-second
peak/LUFS boundary and rejecting audio the gate accepts. Validation now resolves
the bundled binaries, pinned by resolution and call-site tests.

* test(server): pin that a successful fresh join releases its in-flight admission

The in-flight admission counter was pinned on both failure arms and the
two-handshake race, but no case proved the release on the SUCCESS path: a
decrement moved off the unconditional finally into a catch-only path kept
every existing case green while leaking one admission per successful join,
eventually refusing below-cap joins. Two sequential successful joins against
a static clients.size now red exactly that mutation (verified by applying it).

wrapper runs READ COMMITTED and its own header says each statement takes its

is acceptable for these TTL-cached cosmetic reads, so no future maintainer
leans on a consistency guarantee that does not exist.

The narrowed aggro-scan comment claimed the former 25 yd query had the same

Under set -euo pipefail a non-numeric WATCHDOG_COOLDOWN made the cooldown

knob exists to prevent. The value now gets the same numeric-allowlist
sanitization as the state-file stamp, falling back to the default 300.

accountDetail now runs its unbounded play_sessions aggregate through
runWithStatementTimeout, but this suite replaces the whole db module with a
pool-only mock, so the wrapper resolved to undefined and the suite was the

order.

* docs(server): document the resilience seams in the area guides

The area guides now carry what shipped: the db.ts timeout ladder and the
runWithStatementTimeout rule, the three-arm lease steal and fenced saves in

rule on ws_auth, the keepalive_sweep and mob_scan_tick_stats modules, the

* fix(deploy): harden the ops surface per PR 1930 review

Reword the restart-countdown runbook step to secret-gated: nothing enforces
loopback (the edge hides only /livez /readyz /metrics), so the secret must
not be treated as a low-stakes internal value. Bound the runbook drift-gate
container at 2g memory plus swap so a heavy tsc on the live box cannot
create the pressure the game mem_limit exists to prevent. Bound the
watchdog docker inspect and restart calls so a hung daemon cannot park a
run on the flock forever; the restart bound exceeds the 75s stop grace on
purpose (a wedged process eats the full grace, so a working recovery
routinely outlasts a minute). Scope the admission-cap compose pin to the
game service slice so it cannot pass with the knob on discord-bot.

* fix(server): flush the realm-full refusal aggregation tail at the window edge

A burst's tail used to accumulate silently until the next refusal after the
window, which may be hours later, so incident-time counts read shifted into
the wrong burst. Refusals inside the window now arm one unref'd trailing
flush at the window edge; a heartbeat fold was rejected because PERF_TICK_LOG
is opt-in and counts would vanish with it off. Also corrects the same-process
lease comment: after a cross-process same-account takeover rotates the nonce,
the held session's row belongs to the other process until the fence-out kick
lands, so 'already owns the lease row' overstated the invariant.

* fix(net): clear a pending reconnect timer on re-entry into socketClosed

On the zombie-socket path the visibility handler drives socketClosed
manually and the socket's real onclose can land right behind it; the second
entry overwrote reconnectTimer without clearing the first handle, stranding
a live timer and opening a double socket. Clearing any pending timer before
scheduling makes the 'never two live timers' contract true on this path
too; the new test fails against the pre-fix code.

* docs(deploy): finish the secret-gated reword across the operator docs

The QA pass found the DEPLOY.md correction left two sibling 'loopback-only'
claims stale: the RESTART_COUNTDOWN_SECRET blocks in .env.example and
docker-compose.yml still framed the countdown endpoint as network-restricted,
exactly the low-stakes reading the reword exists to remove. Both now state
the secret header is the only gate. The step-3 parenthetical also stops
calling the bare-host tsc run 'the same gate' since it lacks the container's
memory bound. The accurate loopback comment on the 127.0.0.1 port publish
is untouched.

* fix(server): disarm the pending refusal-flush timer on every flush

Two QA reviewers independently flagged the same narrow race: an inline
window-edge flush left an armed trailing timer live, so it could fire
moments into the new window and flush a fresh burst's first refusals early,
splitting one burst into two misdated lines. Every flush now disarms the
pending timer, making the callback's zero-count guard purely defensive.
The new g3 test fails against the pre-disarm code. Also updates a sibling
test comment that still stated the absolute lease-ownership premise the
previous commit corrected.

* test(deploy): pin the watchdog's default docker call bounds

The exec-harness hang tests override both timeout knobs to 1s, so nothing
guarded the shipped defaults. Pin the literals: the 55s inspect bound fits
inside the one-minute cron interval, and the 150s restart bound exceeds the
75s compose stop_grace_period on purpose (a wedged process eats the full
grace, so a working recovery routinely outlasts a minute).

* fix(net): treat a duplicate close signal as the same drop, not a fresh one

The fresh correctness pass caught that clearing-and-rescheduling on the
zombie double-close path still burned two of the bounded reconnect attempts
per physical drop and re-fired onConnectionLost, and at the attempt cap the
late duplicate onclose took the exhaustion branch: endSession cleared the
just-scheduled final retry and dumped the player on one drop. A pending
reconnect timer can only mean the same physical drop (no socket is open
while one is pending), so socketClosed now returns early instead, keeping
the scheduled retry and the attempt count. Both new tests fail against the
previous clear-and-reschedule code.

* fix(deploy): make the watchdog bounds hold against TERM-immune and zero-knob cases

Three correctness-pass findings on the new bounds. timeout without -k never
returns if the docker CLI sits in uninterruptible sleep, re-creating the
park-on-the-flock hang the bound exists to close: add the KILL escalation.
GNU timeout reads a bound of 0 as NO bound, so an operator 0 now maps to the
default instead of silently restoring unbounded behavior. Wrapper and exec
failures (exit 125 and up) were folded into the quiet container-absent arm,
hiding a permanently broken watchdog: they now log loudly. DEPLOY.md also
notes that drift-gate exit 137 means the memory bound, not a type error.

* test(server): restore the aggregation spies in a finally and note the unref loss

A failing assertion in the g2/g3 aggregation tests would have leaked a
frozen Date.now and a silenced console.log into every later test in the
file (no global restoreAllMocks hook); the restores now live in the finally
beside useRealTimers. The unref comment also records the accepted loss: a

* fix(db): re-disable the statement timeout for the post-commit metrics index build

The release side's boot hardening (#1930) disables statement_timeout for
the boot transaction via SET LOCAL, which reverts at COMMIT. This branch
added a post-commit CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY migration that #1930 could
not know about, so it ran with an operator-set database- or role-level

tests/schema_wiring.test.ts.

* fix(db): self-heal an INVALID metrics-index carcass at boot

Cross-merge hazard between this branch and #1930 that neither side could
see alone: the post-commit CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY migration runs
before server.listen, and #1930's compose healthcheck plus deploy
watchdog give boot roughly a 105 to 120 second budget before restarting
the container. A build killed mid-CONCURRENTLY strands the index INVALID,
and IF NOT EXISTS treats an INVALID index as existing, so every later
boot would skip the rebuild forever while play_sessions writes keep
maintaining the dead index.

Boot now checks pg_index for an INVALID carcass under the session
advisory lock and drops it (CONCURRENTLY, so peer realms' session writes
never stall) before the create, making the migration self-healing.
Pinned by both schema_wiring arms (healthy boot never drops; carcass
boot drops before create) and a real-Postgres integration test that
reproduces an actually failed CONCURRENTLY build.

* fix(sim): credit rare personal drops by damage contribution, not tap

The tap-predicate change (requiring the owner's own hit to tap a rare) did not
close the greyjaw_fang camping exploit: handleDeath falls back to the killer
when a corpse is untapped, and a pet's killer resolves through ownerId back to
the owner anyway, so a pet-solo kill still credited the owner regardless of the
predicate. Worse, it opened a new theft vector: any other player could land one
hit on an untapped rare and steal the whole kill, including the fang, from the
legitimate farmer.

Revert the predicate: pet damage taps a rare exactly like any other mob, again.
Instead, extend the world-boss damage-contributor tracking (mob.bossDamagers,
worldBossLootContributors) to rare templates, and thread that contributor
roster into rollLoot as an optional fourth argument used only by the questId
branch: a guaranteed personal quest drop (e.g. greyjaw_fang, chance: 1) is now
credited to every quest-needing contributor, not just whoever currently holds

* fix(input): request pointer lock synchronously on Firefox mousedown (#1840)

* fix(input): request pointer lock synchronously on Firefox mousedown

Firefox denies Element.requestPointerLock() unless the call happens
synchronously inside the handler for the user gesture itself (mousedown), not
a later mousemove once the drag threshold is crossed, even though that
mousemove fires within the mousedown's lingering transient activation window.

user-generated event handler, and the document is not in full screen."

deferred mousemove call, which is why this only broke Firefox.

active camera mode so a plain click-to-move click never triggers it. input.ts

spam on a quick right-click) is untouched there.

* fix(ui): preview every chroma swatch on hover in the character creator (#1627)

In the character creator, hovering an outfit (chroma) swatch inconsistently
updated the avatar preview: after selecting one outfit, hovering the swatch
directly next to the selected one did nothing, while non-adjacent swatches
previewed fine.

Each swatch carried its own mouseenter (preview this chroma) AND its own
mouseleave (revert to the selected chroma). When the pointer moves directly
between two adjacent swatches, the departed swatch's mouseleave and the
entered swatch's mouseenter both fire, and their order is not guaranteed. In
Firefox the mouseenter ran first (preview the hovered chroma) and the
neighbor's mouseleave ran second (revert to the selection), so the preview
snapped straight back and the hover looked like a no-op. Only the swatch
adjacent to the current selection is affected, which is why it read as
"outfit 1 does not update" in the report (outfit 2 was selected).

Extract the wiring into src/ui/skin_picker.ts and bind the revert ONCE on the
row instead of per swatch. A row-level mouseleave does not fire on
child-to-child transitions, so every swatch previews consistently on hover
and the preview still reverts to the committed selection exactly when the
pointer leaves the picker. renderSkinPicker becomes a thin consumer that
builds the portrait swatches and delegates the interactions.

tests/skin_picker.test.ts drives the wiring with a hand-rolled fake DOM and
reproduces the exact repro: with outfit 2 selected, hovering its neighbour
previews; moving between swatches never reverts; leaving the row reverts to
the committed selection; and a click commits and moves the selection.

* fix(net): re-derive follow-up quest availability immediately after turn-in (#1897)

Talking to an NPC right after turning in a quest that gates a follow-up
quest (requiresQuest) showed the default dialog instead of the new quest,
even though the player already qualified. Closing and reopening the
dialog once the exclamation mark reappeared showed it correctly.

Root cause: ClientWorld.turnInQuest() is a fire-and-forget wire command.
The HUD's renderGossip() already re-queries questState() live for every
quest right after the turn-in click, so the UI re-render was never
stale. The staleness was in ClientWorld.questState() itself: its
prerequisite check (quest.requiresQuest && !questsDone.has(...)) reads
questsDone, which only updates once the server's qdone snapshot field
round-trips, so any OTHER quest gated on the one just turned in stayed
"unavailable" until the next snapshot arrived.

Extend the existing pendingQuestCommands optimism (already used to show
the just-turned-in quest as active) to prerequisite checks for every
other quest: while a turnin command is in flight, treat that quest as
done when resolving anyone else's state. Extracted into a pure,
DOM-free module (src/net/quest_state_optimistic.ts) per the module-first
convention, host-agnostic and unit-tested without spinning up
ClientWorld.

fix(bot): reflect live Discord role changes and resolve duplicate special-role ids (#1986)

Admin flair was invisible in game for members holding the Admins role. Three
bot-side defects, fixed without touching the wire format, the discord_role
storage token, or the client render path:

- No live role tracking: memberRoles was seeded once from GUILD_CREATE and
  GUILD_MEMBER_ADD never set roles, so a role granted after startup stayed
  invisible until a restart. Now handle GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE (replace the cached
  role set and re-push the member's meta) and GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE (drop the
  member); GUILD_MEMBER_ADD now seeds roles/join date too.
- Duplicate special-role ids collapsed: refreshSpecialRoles kept only the first
  role id per key, so a guild with both an Admin and an Admins role dropped one
  and its holders resolved to no flair. Now index ALL matching role ids to their
  key so a holder of either resolves.
- Offline members omitted: identify sent no large_threshold and the bot never
  chunked, so offline members (incl. staff) were missing in large guilds. Now
  send large_threshold and REQUEST_GUILD_MEMBERS (op 8), consuming
  GUILD_MEMBERS_CHUNK to backfill the full member list.

Pure reconciliation (reconcileMemberRolesFromUpdate, indexSpecialRoleIds,
topSpecialRoleKeyFor, memberRolesFromPayload, requestGuildMembersPayload) lives
in bot/logic.ts with unit tests; IO stays in main.ts/gateway.ts.

fix(bot): size members-meta batches by bytes, not the server entry cap

A full 1000-member batch of realistic records serializes well past the
server's 64 KiB readBody cap, which the members-meta handler coerces to
an EMPTY member list (200, updated: 0): the whole batch dropped silently
and a large-guild roster never got its meta pushed. Batch at 200 (a
worst-case record is about 300 bytes, so a full batch stays under the
cap with headroom) and log a zero-row push of a non-empty batch in the
client as the silent-drop signature. Tests pin the byte budget against
DEFAULT_JSON_BODY_MAX_BYTES so growth on either side fails loudly.

fix(server): reset bot-pushed guild meta when a link repoints ids

The discord_links upsert kept discord_role and discord_joined_at when an
account relinked to a DIFFERENT Discord id, carrying the previous
identity's staff flair and join date over to the new one. Reset both to
NULL on an id change; a same-id relink keeps them and the bot re-pushes
current values within one sync interval. Noted as an adjacent defect in
issue #1986. Also lands discordIdsWithGuildFlair, the read-only query
the departed-member reconcile consumes in the follow-up commit.

fix(bot): clear stale flair for members who left while the bot was offline

GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE only covers leaves the bot observes live, so a
member who left while it was down kept their in-game verified/staff
flair until some later relink. After every COMPLETE roster seed (a small
guild's GUILD_CREATE, or the final op 8 chunk) the bot now fetches the
ids the server still has flagged (new secret-gated read-only GET

dual-edit rule) and clears exactly the flagged ids missing from the
live roster through the existing member + members-meta endpoints, so a
truncated request can never mass-clear anything. The reconcile is gated
on rosterComplete so a partial seed never misreads unseeded members as
departed; the characterization spine (inventory, completeness,
ownership sweep) pins the new route on both arms.

Addresses code review on PR #2045: fitsAfterSwap's capacity pre-check used
fitsAll, which assumes every unit of a receive can stack onto an existing
plain stack of the same itemId. The real transfer (transferOffer) grants

* feat(sfx): land every custom recording, computed gain-ceiling system, and gain map

Marks every one of Jamie's hand-recorded custom SFX (mob vocalizations across
all 13 families, combat/melee/impact one-shots, footsteps, movement, lockpick,
quest, wand, and the six magic-school proj_/impact_ pairs) with custom: true,

ceiling.

Adds the computed per-key gain-ceiling mechanism (scripts/sfx/sfx_gain_ceiling.mjs):
for every custom key, measures the worst-case true peak across all its takes
and computes exactly how much real headroom exists below the -1dBFS safety
floor. That ceiling becomes each key's individual maximum in the gain map
(playback_profile.mjs's resolvedGainDb), replacing the old flat 0dB cap for
custom content only; every other key keeps the original ceiling untouched.
The generated ceiling file is regenerated alongside the manifest, so it can
never go stale, and is the actual enforcement mechanism (a PR that tries to
exceed it fails outright), not just documentation.

scripts/sfx/sfx_gain_map.json is pinned so every one of the 130 custom keys
sits at its own individually-computed maximum boost.

fix(economy): let a linked-but-disconnected wallet buy Claudium on the crypto rails (#1952)

* fix(economy): let a linked-but-disconnected wallet buy Claudium on the crypto rails

Players who verified (linked) a Solana wallet see their $WOC balance on the
player card even when the browser extension is not connected this session (the
game has a dedicated "linked but disconnected" state for exactly this). But the
Claudium store's crypto rails read the balance only from the actively connected
session wallet (currentWallet().address), so a linked-but-disconnected player
saw, for example, 130k $WOC on their card while every SOL/WOC buy button stayed
silently disabled: the snapshot fed a null wallet balance, so claudium_view
computed every rung as unaffordable. This blocked real purchases (revenue) with
no explanation.

Fall back to the account's linked wallet pubkey when nothing is connected this
session, so the store reads that wallet's on-chain balance and the buy button
enables when the player can afford it. The buy click already surfaces the
existing "Connect a Solana wallet before buying" prompt (the signAndSend path
throws "connect a wallet first" when disconnected, caught into
checkoutWalletRequired), so the flow becomes: enabled button, click, connect to
sign, instead of a dead button. When connected, behavior is unchanged (the
fallback only fires on a null connected address); a player with no linked wallet
at all still correctly sees disabled rails.

Follow-up (not in this change): auto-open the connect flow on the buy click when
disconnected, so the player does not have to reconnect manually before re-clicking.

fix(desktop): relaunch to make Linux PRIME render-offload actually reach the GPU process

Review on PR #2075 measured on real hybrid hardware that setting the PRIME
env vars via process.env in the running main process is a functional no-op
on Linux: Electron's GPU process there forks from a zygote that already
exec'd (and snapshotted its environ) before any main-process JS runs, so the
mutation never reaches it. A follow-up review, also hardware-verified, found
two more gaps in the originally-proposed fix: __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME alone
is a decoy for this app (Chromium's context is EGL, not GLX), and the correct

any PRIME variable is missing, main.cjs re-execs the app (before crash
reporting, logging, or any window) with the corrected variable set -

if every variable is already present, no relaunch happens. Documents two
known follow-ups (unconditional relaunch rather than hybrid-gated, and the
second-instance deep-link interaction is unverified) rather than claiming a
completeness the change does not have.

synchronously from resolvedGltf inside the per-frame render path, which
permanently stalled Renderer.sync while sim and audio kept running (the
v0.27.0 training dummy freeze, fixed for that one model in PR #2078).
createCharacterVisual now catches the construction failure, logs it once
per visual-key-plus-cause via the new asset_miss_log module, and returns
null; every renderer call site skips that entity's view and leaves it a
future candidate, and a failed build sits out a 2 second retry cooldown
so it cannot burn a view-creation budget slot every frame (under the
hitch backoff the budget is 1, so a first-sorted failing entity would
otherwise starve every other pending view).

Scope decisions: the lazy preload gates keep their memoized no-retry
behavior (a per-frame retry would spam fetches on a permanent failure)
but their catch logging now dedupes through the same module; the
post-construction weapon re-attach path (setWeapon and the stow swap)
stays uncaught because every weapon and weapon-skin URL is pinned into
the tier-independent preload union by tests/render_asset_preload.test.ts
and the renderer latches the diff field first, so a miss there throws
once per change, not per frame. Closes #2079.

fix(render): throttle all failed visual retries

Route required views, lazy preloads, form builds, and visual swaps
through a shared per-slot cooldown. Expire retry state and prune
departed entities so long-lived clients do not retain failed IDs.

fix(render): clear the preload cooldown on fetch resolution

The lazy gates armed the full retry cooldown while the fetch was merely
in flight, and nothing cleared the slot when it landed, so a mech or
training dummy popped in up to two seconds after readiness, and via the
required-view path a player logging in with the mech cosmetic active
stayed invisible for that window. The gates now clear their slot when
the preload promise resolves: pop-in returns to the next frame after
readiness, a rejected fetch still waits out the cooldown, and the
in-flight window still burns no per-frame budget slot.

Also pins two gate behaviors the suite missed: prune retains unexpired
entries for still-present entities (a clear-everything regression would
silently defeat the throttle), and cooldowns are keyed per entity so one
entity's failure never blocks another.

fix(render): dequantize baked-pose uv before merging character geometries (#2092)

bakeStaticPose (src/render/characters/assets.ts) clones each visible mesh's
uv attribute verbatim when building the far-LOD / shadow-proxy idle geometry.
KayKit primitives quantize uv differently per part (normalized Uint16Array on
some, plain Float32Array on others), so THREE.BufferGeometryUtils
.mergeGeometries() rejects the mismatch ("BufferAttribute.array must be of
consistent array types across matching attributes") and returns null for any
affected visual key. That leaves prep.idleGeo null, which silently drops the
far-LOD proxy and shadow-only proxy mesh (src/render/characters/visual.ts),
so the character always renders its full skinned rig and never casts via the
cheap shadow proxy.

Extracted dequantizeAttribute into its own pure module (denormalizes any
BufferAttribute into a fresh Float32Array via getComponent, mirroring the
existing rebakeGeometry pattern in rig_merge.ts) and used it for uv in
bakeStaticPose so every baked geo shares one attribute type before merging.

balance(warrior): v0.27.1 hotfix for the fury overpower incident (#2112)

* balance(items): re-budget two-handers to differentiate on dps, never stats

A two-hander used to carry both hands' stat budgets (TWOHAND_STAT_MULT = 2)
under the assumption that the offhand slot was sacrificed. Titan's Grip broke
that assumption by filling BOTH weapon slots with double-budget two-handers:
86 weapon stat points against 38 for a dual-1H pair, which made every other
item slot feel irrelevant and fed the v0.27.0 fury overpower incident.

The new model: TWOHAND_STAT_MULT drops to 1.3 (strictly below the 1.75
combined mainhand + offhand slot weights, so every dual-wield or shield setup
out-stats a two-hander), and the damage side of the tradeoff is codified as
TWOHAND_DPS_MULT = 1.15, the previously informal Eastbrook/Highwatch
greatsword rule. The four authored epics are re-statted onto the new budget
in place (same ids, no new items): Deathless Greatblade 46 -> 30 points and
lifted onto the premium dps curve (52-78 at 3.4), Wyrmfang 36 -> 23 and
lifted (33-53 at 2.6), Bonewrought and Direfang 40 -> 26 with their already
on-premium weapons unchanged. Heroic variants re-derive automatically, with
the variant scaler now rounding the fractional budget and applying the same
dps premium a two-hand base carries.

tests/twohand_rebudget.test.ts pins the constants, the structural
out-stat invariant, and full-catalog stat and dps conformance for every
leveled two-hander; the v0.26 itemization pins are re-minted to the new
budgets and the heroic flair dps assertions are premium-aware.

* balance(warrior): flat 12% physical damage penalty while titans-gripping

Titan's Grip shipped with no detriment of its own: a fury warrior paid only
the generic dual-wield penalties (50% offhand swings, 10pp white miss) that a
dual-1H rogue already pays, while the offhand two-hander contributed its full
double stat budget and a bigger swing on every axis, a strict upgrade.

This adds the WoW 3.1.0-model penalty: while dual-wielding with a two-hander
in either hand, all physical damage done is reduced by 12%
(TITANS_GRIP_DMG_PENALTY). The state derives at equip time in
recalcPlayerStats (entity.titansGrip) and applies source-side in dealDamage,
physical school only, so whites, weapon strikes, and physical dots pay it and
spells never do. Solo two-hander and dual-1H loadouts are untouched, and the
fury spec description now states the cost.

The penalty was chosen over a miss-chance detriment deliberately: Blizzard
shipped the miss version at 15%, cut it to 5% within weeks under player
revolt, deleted it in 3.0.8, and settled on the flat 10% physical cut in
3.1.0. A miss variant stays on the table as a balance-simulator experiment.

* balance(warrior): fix the fury rage economy on four axes

Fury's whole rotation was rage-positive: Twinstrike (free, +8, 2 charges),
Bloodletting (free, +12), and Bladed Gyre (free, +5 to +10 rageOnHit) all
minted while Anger Management added +25%/+15% and warrior auto-attacks ran a
hidden 9x mint instead of the classic 7.5x outgoing scale. Total income was
~13-17 rage/s against Red Harvest's 80 cost, an 80-rage spender firing every
~6 seconds forever, the core of the v0.27.0 fury overpower incident.

The fix makes Bloodletting the ONE generating builder and restores the
classic scale:
- warrior auto-attack rage back on the shared rageFromDealing 7.5x scale
  (the 9x special case in dealDamage is deleted)
- Twinstrike gainResource 8 to 4
- Bladed Gyre mints nothing (rageOnHit removed; still free, keeps the echo)
- Anger Management trimmed to +10% auto / +5% ability rage (same row id, so
  saved talent picks survive)
- Bloodletting keeps +12; Red Harvest is deliberately untouched (a spender
  should be gated by its resource, not a cooldown)

Arms' Brute Swing builder (+8) is deliberately untouched: Arms was not the
overpowered spec and already absorbs the 2H re-stat. Expected sustained
income lands near 8-9 rage/s, a Red Harvest every ~10-12s.

tests/warrior_rage_economy.test.ts pins the 7.5 scale literal, the
builder values, and the trimmed row; the v0.26 contract, row-runtime, and
whirlwind-echo pins are re-minted to the new values.

applyRageSpendCooldownRefund had no cap, no floor, and no window: at 0.1s

per minute and collapsed Recklessness/Avatar from 180s to an effective ~78s
(roughly 2.3x the intended offensive cooldown uptime).

The fix transplants the exact mechanism the mage's Overflowing Power (which
copied Colossal Might and got the cap the original never had) already uses:
the shave is bounded to COLOSSAL_MIGHT_CAP_SECONDS = 10 per
COLOSSAL_MIGHT_CAP_WINDOW = 30 rolling seconds, with the accumulator riding

spam. The row tooltip states the cap; the row id and cdrPerRage rate are
unchanged, so saved picks survive.

* fix(sim): Wildfang Rally never stacks with itself, and no group buff can

Two hunters casting Wildfang Rally stacked two copies of the +45 AP and +5%
haste on every ally: the aura dedupe (aura_stacking.ts) only collapses

allowlist, and neither of Wildfang's halves (aspect_of_the_wild,

fix(sim): stop Nature's Fury re-announcing its buff every refresh pulse (#2110)

Nature's Fury pulses once a second to refresh its 3s spell-crit window on
the moonwing druid and nearby party members, so the buff never actually
lapses while the conditions hold. Every pulse round-tripped through
applyAura(), which unconditionally emits an 'aura' gained:true SimEvent,
so the buff-gained FCT/SFX cue fired again every single second even
though nothing had changed for the player: it looked and sounded like
the buff was constantly being reapplied and never settling.

Fix: when a pulse finds the aura already present from the same source,
refresh its remaining/duration in place instead of calling applyAura
again, so the gained event (and its sound cue) only fires once, on the
actual first application. Added a test that ticks past several refresh
pulses and asserts the druid's 'aura' gained event fires exactly once.

release: v0.27.2, iOS world-entry crash hotfix (memory trims, watchdog-safe prewarm, crash guard) (#2138)

* fix(game): downgrade a saved Ultra graphics preset on iOS Safari, not just the native app

iOS WebKit can terminate a tab's WebContent process mid-scene-build on Ultra/
Advanced world entry on recent phones. The existing safe-startup-tier
downgrade only checked isNativeRuntime(), so it protected the Capacitor iOS
app shell but left iOS Safari itself unprotected even though it runs the
same engine and hits the same per-tab memory ceiling. A player who ever
saved Ultra/Advanced on an iPhone got stuck in a load, crash, reload loop
in the browser, before the in-game Options menu was ever reachable to back
out, in both online and offline mode since the crash happens during the
shared scene-build step both worlds share.

Extracts the decision into a pure, unit-tested safeStartupGraphicsPreset
(src/game/startup_graphics_safety.ts) so main.ts stays a thin caller, per
this repo's module-first convention, and widens the gate to any webkit +
mobile browser environment in addition to the native runtime.

* fix(render): shed the world-entry GPU memory spike on phone-class WebKit

Medium and above allocate a 2560+ shadow map, three PMREM env targets,
ten splat textures, and three mip-chained 4K backdrops synchronously at
world entry. On iOS WebKit that one-shot spike crosses the per-process
memory ceiling and the OS kills the WebContent process before the first
frame, exiting the game with no error.

Adds a constrainedMemory profile to GfxSettings (from the existing
isConstrainedBrowser predicate): smaller shadow maps (1536 medium, 2048
high/ultra), no composer MSAA, a 1.48 pixel-ratio cap, no backdrop mip
chains, and IBL prefilter deferred to idle timers for the non-default
biomes. Every knob is cosmetic sharpness only, so the graphics-settings
fairness rule holds. Bumps GFX_CONFIG_VERSION so telemetry can segment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(game): step graphics down and break the resume loop after a world-entry crash

iOS WebKit kills the WebContent process with no event when world entry
crosses its memory ceiling; the shell reloads, the active-play resume
marker re-enters the world, and the player cycles through the welcome
screen up to the attempt cap with no reachable graphics control. The
Auto default (masked iPhone GPU resolves to medium) could land straight
in that trap.

Adds a world-entry crash probe (src/game/entry_crash_guard.ts): stamped
before the synchronous scene build, cleared on survival, handled
failure, or page-hide (a backgrounded eviction is not an entry crash).
A probe still armed at boot means the last entry died mid-build: on
iOS/native runtimes the persisted preset steps down ONE tier, the auto
default is pinned so it can never re-select the crashed tier, the
resume marker is dropped so boot lands on chrome with the footer
graphics selector reachable, and a start-screen banner tells the player
what happened. Console [entry-guard] lines support on-device isolation.

On-device logs from an iPhone 17 Pro showed the Medium crash happening

prewarm, not the allocation spike: it may hold the main thread for 12s
of view builds plus up to 10s of shader linking with only microtask

the earlier run that survived had effectively run only required views

Make the minimal configuration deliberate: constrained devices run only

fix(sim): reclaim emptied spatial-grid cells instead of leaking them (#2122)

* fix(sim): reclaim emptied spatial-grid cells instead of leaking them

SpatialGrid.remove() deleted an entity from its cell's array but never
deleted the cells Map entry once that array emptied out. Every entity
that crosses a cell boundary (ordinary movement, every mob spawn or
despawn) could leave a permanently retained, dead empty-array entry
behind, so a long-lived server process accumulated one leaked Map
entry per distinct cell any entity ever vacated, independent of the
live player or entity count.

This matches production Grafana evidence: Sim Tick Time (p95/max),
Event-Loop Lag p99, and Heap Used all sawtoothed upward over each
multi-hour window between restarts and reset right after each deploy,
while online player count stayed flat the whole time. The grid backs
every forEachInRadius interest query in the 20 Hz tick loop and the
per-tick broadcast, so a growing dead-cell map raises per-tick scan
and GC cost purely with uptime, producing the stutter and the growing
event-loop lag that mobile clients (more sensitive to keepalive and
snapshot delay) trip on first as disconnects.

Adds cellCount() for testability and a regression test that walks an
entity through 500 distinct cells and asserts the tracked cell count
stays at the true occupied count instead of growing with the number
of moves.

* docs(sim): stop overstating the spatial-grid leak as the tick sawtooth

Both PR #2122 reviewers (Rubsey, EnriqueGF) independently confirmed the
cells.delete(key) fix itself is correct and complete, but flagged that the
in-code comment and test narrative still asserted "cells grows without
bound over uptime" / "root cause of a production sawtooth" as fact. That
claim doesn't hold: insert() reuses an existing array, so cells.size was
already bounded by the number of distinct cells ever occupied, not by
movement/spawn churn. Reworded both comments to describe only what the
code actually does, so a future reader doesn't conclude the still-open
Grafana sawtooth investigation is explained by this bookkeeping fix.

fix(input): stop Firefox camera rotation freezing after a forced pointer-lock unlock (#2131)

* fix(input): stop Firefox camera rotation freezing after a forced pointer-lock unlock

Firefox denies requestPointerLock() for a short, undocumented cooldown after
it force-unlocks the pointer via its own default gesture (Escape, or losing
focus) rather than our own exitPointerLock() call. A player who presses
Escape mid-drag, or alt-tabs, hits exactly this: the very next camera drag
attempt on Firefox is silently denied (no pointerlockerror handler existed to
even notice), pointerLockRequestedForDrag is left wrongly set, and rotation
then freezes the moment the unlocked cursor reaches the screen edge. This is
the likely source of the long-running "Firefox camera only works some of the
time" reports, since Escape is also the game-menu key and a very common
reflex when the cursor already feels stuck.

Track when a forced unlock happens (pointer lock lost while a drag button is
still held) and skip the doomed requestPointerLock() call during Firefox's
cooldown window, letting the drag continue unlocked instead (rotation still
works away from the screen edge). Also add the missing pointerlockerror
listener so any other denial resets the request flag instead of leaving it
stuck for the rest of the press.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(input): also arm the forced-unlock cooldown on pointerlockerror

EnriqueGF's review on #2131 flagged that forcedUnlockAt was only set from
the pointerlockchange handler when a drag button was still held, which
misses the focus-loss ordering where blur (clearing leftDown/rightDown)
can land before pointerlockchange fires. A denied requestPointerLock() is
itself the strongest evidence of Firefox's post-forced-unlock cooldown,
so record forcedUnlockAt in the pointerlockerror handler too: this makes
the mechanism self-healing regardless of event ordering, covering the
gap without needing to track blur vs pointerlockchange ordering directly.
Also tightened the pointerlockchange comment, which previously implied
exitPointerLock() only ever runs after mouseup clears the drag flags;
setLockCursorOnRotate()/setMouseCameraEnabled() call it directly and can
fire mid-drag, a small accepted trade-off worth documenting accurately.
