fix(render): character preview never loads on a cold, first-visit cache (#2245)

* fix(render): retry character preview assets independent of the global preload barrier

New players on a cold, first-visit browser cache sometimes saw a permanently
blank character model on the character-creation screen. The landing preview
was gated on the site-wide assetsReady() promise with no failure handler; that
promise is a single barrier over every registered preload (terrain, dungeon,
foliage, character GLBs, ...), so one unrelated transient fetch failure
anywhere silently sank the preview forever with no retry, which only "healed"
on reload because the HTTP cache was warm by then.

Add charactersReady() in render/characters/assets.ts, a narrower gate that
only waits on character-boot assets and retries whatever is still missing
(loadGltf/loadTexture already evict a failed URL on rejection, so a fresh
call is a real re-fetch), and wire main.ts's preview init through it with a
catch so an exhausted retry logs instead of leaving an unhandled rejection.

* fix(render): decorate class chips off portrait readiness, widen retry backoff

decorateClassChips() had moved onto charactersReady(), the narrower gate the
prior commit introduced for the 3D preview's cold-cache recovery. portrait.ts
latches its own readiness off a separate, wider assetsReady() snapshot made at
import time, so the same transient failure charactersReady() now recovers
from left portraitsReady() permanently false and every class chip stuck on a
plain label (decorateClassChips is one-shot per chip). Wire the chip decoration
to portrait.ts's own onPortraitsReady() instead, independent of the preview
gate. Also move the preview's .catch() to the end of its promise chain so it
actually guards the .then() body instead of running unconditionally after
logging the failure, add a backoff delay between charactersReady()'s outer
retry attempts (reusing the existing loadGltf backoff schedule) so a flaky
connection is not hammered three more times in one tick, and pin the exact
retry call count in the boot test instead of only asserting the promise
resolves.

fix(balance): healers-vs-heroics rebalance wave for v0.29.1

The v0.29.0 heroic retune multiplied instance damage ~4x while healing and
tank pools stood still: Monte Carlo benches on the real Sim measured best-case
healer output covering 55-78% of heroic boss damage into the best tank, top
heals restoring 6.5-8% of a buffed tank pool (classic reference: 15-25%), and
heroic Nythraxis one-shotting the main tank at t=1.5s on the pull. This wave
rebalances both sides. Every change was built test-first; contract tests pin
every tuning literal.

Healing output:
- Every mainline heal gains or revalues a level-20 cap rank (about 1.45x each
  ladder's old top; sub-cap ranks pinned untouched, so leveling is unchanged).
  chain_heal / healing_stream / tranquility deliberately skipped: their
  descriptions hardcode numbers (reword follow-up).
- HEALING_SP_SCALE = 2: heals and HoTs take double Spell Power (1 healing per
  point of Intellect). Damage spells and mage barrier absorbs unchanged.

Tank survivability:
- Tank crit immunity: mobs cannot critically strike a Protection warrior,
  Protection paladin, or Feral druid in Sloth Form (combat/tank_crit_immunity.ts;
  the 5% roll is still drawn so the rng stream is unchanged).
- Tank parity: protection paladin baseline staPct +0.35; Sloth Form armor
  1.9x -> 2.3x plus feral staPct +0.25. All three tanks land within 88-108%
  of the prot warrior's effective HP (were 76% / 66%).

Encounters:
- Gravebreaker (Nythraxis) is a charged auto-attack: the 12s cadence arms the
  boss and the next LANDED swing releases the frontal splash (1.5x the same
  swing roll, bystanders only, never crits). The old free-standing cast fired
  at t=1.5s and stacked with the opening swing, killing tanks before any heal
  could land. Avoidance holds the charge.
- Grave Inferno replaces Korzul's Necrotic Shockwave on both difficulties: a
  30s-cadence, 8s stationary uninterruptible channel (no melee while it runs)
  with four escalating unmitigated fire pulses in 14yd, telegraphed by
  radius-true spellfxAt terrain rings (the rendered edge is the dodge edge).
  Generic infernoChannel mechanic, reusable by future bosses.
- Boss-summoned adds are wave pressure, not extra bosses: damage floors drop
  from the 500 mob line to 250 (Vael 16.25x, Ysolei 15.25x, Velkhar 14.25x;
  Nythraxis adds 3.75/3.75/8/6), and every summon path seeds the boss's
  current target with 750 threat (was 1, which peeled every wave onto the
  first healer to cast). Voss drops to the heroic speed floor (11 -> 8) so
  slows create real escape velocity; his CC-able / taunt-immune contract is
  pinned so no future immunity sweep deletes his counterplay.

Tuning:
- Heroic Nythraxis nerf: boss swing floor 1200 -> 1000 (damageMultiplier
  8.75 -> 7.25) and skeleton waves to 1.2x their NORMAL-mode health (3,768,
  via the new healthMultiplierByMob per-mob map). The court trio keeps full
  health: measured off the critical path, and its respawn gate self-limits.
- Normal Gravewyrm Sanctum retuned for fresh level-20 groups in quest gear:
  trash floor 300 -> 200, bosses 600 -> 420, summoned bonewalkers 150, with
  doubled health kept. A best-geared warrior still takes well over his
  self-heal ceiling, so it stays non-soloable.

Bench outcomes on this tree (12 seeds five-man / 8 seeds raid): normal
Nythraxis kills at 100% with zero median deaths; all five heroic five-man
bosses sit in one single-healable band; heroic Nythraxis raids reach phase 2
at 46-60% boss HP with worst-case scripted play (no interrupts), a genuine
but brutal kill path for real groups. Parity goldens re-minted for the
Gravebreaker and threat-seed changes.

fix(input): stop the browser pointer-capture notice on ordinary camera drags (#2382)

Every camera drag requested pointer lock, so the browser painted its own
"press Esc to show your cursor" notice over the game on essentially every
right-drag look, the most common gesture there is.

The lock only earns its keep at the viewport edge, where the OS cursor
stops moving, movementX/movementY clamp to 0 and the camera freezes (or
the cursor slips onto a second display). A drag through the middle of the
window integrates its deltas perfectly well unlocked.

So the request is now deferred until the pointer enters a margin band
around the viewport edge, decided by the new pure pointer_lock_edge.ts
module and re-checked on every move of an active drag. Ordinary looks
take no lock and show no notice; the anti-freeze guarantee is preserved
exactly where it mattered. Gecko, which can only lock from the gesture
handler itself, applies the same test to where the press starts.

* feat(render): keep far characters animated instead of freezing them

Past the articulated LOD band a character used to swap straight to its baked
idle-pose mesh, so anything beyond 58yd (34.8yd once the crowd knob pulled the
band in) read as a sliding statue rather than a distant figure. Insert an
animated far band between the two: the rig stays articulated and advances its
mixer every 4th to 6th frame, so the clip still plays at its real speed with
fewer pose updates, and only past that edge does the frozen mesh take over.

The extension is a pure policy in crowd_lod.ts (characterLodBands, plus the
cadence ladder and the frozen-mesh predicate the renderer now consumes), capped
per tier by GFX.farCharacterAnimScale and eased back to exactly 1 by the crowd
knee and live frame-budget pressure, so a throng, the low tier, the phone memory
profiles, and a machine at its budget all keep today's behaviour bit for bit.
An actionable pose (self, current target, anything mid-cast) additionally never
freezes inside the uncrowded base range: a cast windup is a telegraph, and a
frozen idle mesh hides it more completely than a throttled cadence does.

* fix(render): default Apple Silicon Macs to medium graphics, not ultra

Apple Silicon (M1..M9) was bucketed with strong desktop discrete GPUs in
classifyGpuRenderer, so resolveDefaultGraphicsPreset returned ULTRA on a

desktop cards with active-cooling headroom, so a sustained ultra load spins the
fans, overheats, and drains battery — a worse-than-necessary default.

safe middle (PRESET_MEDIUM) on a Mac (non-touch), matching the inconclusive-GPU
fallback the runtime governor can climb from. An M-series iPad (touch) keeps its
existing HIGH cap, and ultra stays a manual opt-in in the graphics picker. Strong
desktop discrete GPUs (NVIDIA/AMD/Arc) still reach ultra — the split did not
demote them.

* fix(sim): stop a DoT tick from ticking twice when it breaks its own carrier's aura

updateAuras walks e.auras backward by LIVE index, but a DoT tick's own
ctx.dealDamage call runs its own backward sweeps over that same array: it can
splice out a breaksOnDamage control aura (the Fear family) or a depleted absorb
shield mid-walk. When the removed aura sits at a lower index than the DoT, the
shift pulls the just-processed DoT back under the cursor, so it is processed a
second time in the same sim tick: remaining and tickTimer are decremented twice
and the target takes a second tick of damage.

Walk an up-front snapshot instead, skip any entry a side effect already removed,
and splice expiries at the aura's live index. The snapshot is taken in the
identical order the live walk had, so every aura that survives its own turn is
processed exactly as before, and the fix only REMOVES a spurious dealDamage call
rather than adding one. The parity gate confirms it: green with no golden
regeneration, so both the full-state trace and the rng draw-order log are
byte-identical.

The new test in tests/combat_auras.test.ts pins the crossing case (a fear at a
lower index than a 50-damage DoT): it reads 100 damage against the old walk and
50 with this change.

* fix(game): stop the Android world-entry audio crack by routing the landing theme through WebAudio

On Android (reported on a Pixel 9a), entering the world played a loud
crack. The landing-page theme is a bare HTMLAudioElement still playing
when world entry opens the game's first AudioContexts (sfx/music init),
and opening the first low-latency WebAudio output stream during bare
media playback makes Android reconfigure the audio output, which cracks
the in-flight playback. Verified on-device with an isolation probe: a
context opened during bare-media playback cracks; a context opened
first, or any additional context, is clean.

Route the theme through its own dedicated AudioContext from the first
play (the src/game/music.ts stream pattern), so the low-latency output
path opens WITH the theme and the world-entry inits land in the clean
"additional context" case. Playback is gated on the routed context
running so it is never swallowed by a suspended graph, and WebAudio
being unavailable falls back to plain element playback.

* feat(dev): searchable item picker for the Developer Command Center

The give-item field was a native <select> holding every one of the ~672 ITEMS. It
rendered taller than the viewport and covered the window it belonged to, was
sorted alphabetically with no way to narrow it, and showed names that are not
unique: 57 display names are shared by exactly two ids each (a base piece and its
generated heroic variant), so two adjacent rows could read identically.

Replaced with a combobox. The input IS the command field (data-dev-field="item"),
so it carries the item id and the existing values() collection is untouched; a
tester who already knows an id can still paste it directly.

- Shows NOTHING until you type. An empty query returns an empty list, not 672
  rows, which is the actual fix for the overflow.
- Caps at 12 rows with a "showing 12 of 84" hint. The cap is load-bearing, not
  cosmetic: it is what stops the list growing back into the bug it replaces.
- Matches BOTH the localized name and the raw id, so "ashstalker" and "heroic_"
  are both useful queries. gnarled_staff displays as "Bogoak Staff", so a
  name-only filter would leave it unfindable by id.
- Ranks exact id, then name prefix, id prefix, name contains, id contains, with a
  trailing id tie-break so a duplicate-name pair holds a stable order between
  renders instead of swapping under the cursor.
- Each row carries the localized name (coloured by quality, reusing the canonical
  .q-* hexes as text-colour twins), a Heroic tag, the slot, and the raw id.
- A live status line resolves whatever is typed: "Selected: <name>", or "No item
  has that id" when it does not name one. Previously a bad value silently did
  nothing.

Ranking lives in src/ui/dev_item_picker_view.ts, a DOM-free and i18n-free pure
core registered in UI_PURE_CORES; the painter resolves names via tEntity and
passes them in, the same shape deeds_view.ts uses. The localized candidate list is
built once and rebuilt only on a language change, since the picker re-filters on
every keystroke.

Interaction follows the existing .soc-sugg-item combobox: non-focusable
role="option" rows driven by aria-activedescendant (focusable rows would be pulled
into this dialog's focus-trap tab cycle), mousedown rather than click so blur
cannot tear the list down first, and a blur-clear delay mirroring
SUGGEST_BLUR_CLEAR_MS. Escape closes the list and stops propagation, so the first
press does not dismiss the whole Command Center. The suggestion list repaints its
own subtree and never calls render(), which rewrites the window's innerHTML and
would destroy the input mid-keystroke.

* feat(dev): fresh-level-20 gear presets for all 27 class and spec pairs

Testers were being kitted out by hand through the database. /dev kit [spec], and
the matching Equip fresh-20 kit action in the Developer Command Center, now dress
a character in one step.

TIER: deliberately the PRE-SANCTUM set, because the thing being measured is
whether a fresh level-20 group can clear Gravewyrm Sanctum. Included: quest greens
and blues, gold-vendor gear, and normal dungeon drops from every dungeon EXCEPT
Sanctum. Excluded: Sanctum's own 38 drops (wearing the loot of the encounter under
test would contaminate the number the run exists to produce), plus heroic variants,
heroic five-man, raid, the heroic-mark vendor and PvP gear, all of which sit ABOVE
Sanctum in progression and are unreachable by the character this simulates.

The Sanctum exclusion needed its own derivation: item_level.ts's source index keeps
only { level, raid } per item, so it can say something is level-20 content but NOT
which dungeon it dropped in. dungeonLootIds walks the dungeon's spawns to their
mobs' loot tables instead.

BAGS FIRST, and the ordering is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Sim.addItem never
refuses a grant, but equipping a piece displaces whatever it replaces back into the
bags, and THAT return leg is capacity gated: with only the starter backpack a full
12-piece kit can run out of room mid-apply. All four sockets take the largest bag in
the table before a single piece is granted. Both hands are cleared before the weapon
pass so an incumbent two-hander cannot block a shield or offhand.

All 27 pairs are covered (9 classes x 3 specs), not the 16 gear-identity groupings a
shared-kit approach would collapse them into. Selection is a deterministic argmax
over per-spec stat weights with an id tie-break, so a balance run is repeatable: no
rng, no clock, same spec always yields byte-identical gear.

The weights (src/sim/content/dev_kit_roles.ts) are a TESTING CONVENIENCE, not a
balance statement. They derive from each spec's declared SpecDef.role plus the class
archetype, and follow this game's own declarations rather than genre convention:
mage/arcane is a HEALER here and druid/feral is a TANK.

GEAR ONLY. Level, spec, talents and quests are untouched; /dev level and the spec UI
already own those, and welding them together would stop a tester varying one without
the other. Pinned by a test.

Bug found and fixed while building: shaman/enhancement was first given
hands: 'dualWield', but canDualWield grants that to rogues and fury warriors ONLY,
so the second weapon was refused and the spec silently lost its offhand entirely.
Corrected in the data, given a held-offhand fallback so a mismatch can never again
leave a bare hand, and pinned by a test that fails if any spec claims a hands
capability the equip rules refuse.

SimContext gains equipBag/equipItem/unequipItem passthroughs so the kit applies
through the seam rather than reaching around it; every validation still happens in
the Sim inventory hub.

Tests: 27-pair coverage both directions, the Sanctum and tier exclusions, the
requiredClass re-check that canEquipItem skips for armor, determinism, no duplicate
ring, shield specs getting a one-hander, casters never taking a strength piece over
an intellect one, bags-before-gear ordering, hands cleared first, and end-to-end
/dev kit runs against a real Sim including that it is inert when devCommands is off.

* fix(dev): exclude above-tier gear by table identity, not inferred item level

The shipped fresh-20 presets leaked gear the tier explicitly forbids. Reported from
dev: the priest kit was wearing Heroic Marks badge jewelry.

Root cause: exclusion tested an INFERRED source level (`> DEV_KIT_LEVEL`), which is
not sound for this question.
  - the Heroic Marks vendor registers its stock at EXACTLY source level 20
    (HEROIC_VENDOR_SOURCE_LEVEL), so every badge piece passed a `> 20` test;
  - some heroic pieces carry NO derivable source level at all, so no level test
    could ever reach them.

Three badge items (neck + both rings) and one heroic helm reached the priest kit.
The helm was additionally a RETIRED id: save-compat only, not obtainable in game, so
testers were being handed an item no player can own.

Exclusion is now by the table that DEFINES the item, which is exactly the question
the tier rules ask: HEROIC_ITEMS and RETIRED_HEROIC_ITEMS (heroic dungeon gear),
HEROIC_VENDOR_ITEMS (badge vendor), WARFARE_ITEMS (PvP). Raid loot and Gravewyrm
Sanctum drops stay on their existing drop-table checks. Audited: 0 violations across
all 27 kits.

CONSEQUENCE, deliberate and confirmed with the maintainer: neck and both ring slots
are now EMPTY on every preset. All 19 neck/ring items in the game are either badge
vendor stock (10) or source level 22+ (9), so there is no jewelry below the heroic
badge vendor and a genuinely fresh 20 wears none. Kits fill 8-9 slots instead of 12.
That is the honest baseline for a Sanctum balance run; inflating it with above-tier
jewelry would bias the number the run exists to produce.

Tests: a regression pin walks every one of the 27 finished kits against all five
exclusions and reports violations by name, so a future leak names the spec, slot and
source instead of moving a count. A second test pins the jewelry gap itself, so the
day content adds fresh-20 neck/rings it reds and the kit slots get revisited rather
than silently continuing to ship three empty slots.

The repo's own retired-id guard (tests/retired_heroic_items.test.ts) caught the
retired leak, on a comment naming the id. Comment reworded rather than the rule
relaxed.

* fix(dev): cap fresh-20 presets at rare, no epics

Reported from dev: a shaman kit came through wearing Barrowlord gear. It was epic.
A fresh level 20 does not own epics.

Root cause, and the reason the two previous fixes did not hold: the filter only ever
constrained WHERE an item comes from, never WHAT it is. The kit scorer maximizes
stats, so any epic left reachable through any source is taken every time. Each
earlier fix closed one source and left the whole class of item reachable through the
next. Across the 27 kits, 103 of 239 picks (43%) were epic.

The tier rule was in the original spec all along, "questing blues and greens", and
only the source half of it was implemented. Now: quality must be poor, common,
uncommon or rare. Epic and legendary are rejected outright, and an item with NO
declared quality also fails, because unset cannot be shown to be below the cap and
this is not a place to fail open.

After: 195 rare, 42 uncommon, 2 common, 0 epic, 0 legendary, 0 unset.

Pool health is unaffected: 76 to 151 eligible items per class, every armor and weapon
slot still covered. Neck and both rings stay empty for the separate, already
documented reason that the game has no jewelry below the heroic badge vendor.

Tests: one regression walks every one of the 27 finished kits and fails on any epic
or legendary, naming the spec, slot, id and quality rather than moving a count; a
second rejects epic/legendary from the pool for every class; a third pins that unset
quality fails closed.

feat(sfx): wire real recordings across gathering, crafting, and the enchanting profession (#2134)

* feat(sfx): real recordings for gathering, crafting, and masterwork, wire disenchant

Gathering played zero sound despite gatherResult being purpose-built for it
("so the client can play a gathering audio cue"), craft success reused the
generic loot ding, and the masterwork proc was completely unhandled. Adds
audio.gather(nodeType), audio.craftSuccess(recipeFamily) (resolves the
recipe's professionId via ALL_RECIPES, falls back to the loot ding for an
unrecognized family), and audio.masterwork() (layers alongside the family
cue on a masterwork craftResult, never replaces it). Real recordings for all
3 gather node types (4 takes each) and all 10 CRAFT_RING craft families.

Also gives disenchantItem its first IWorld/wire exposure: it already existed
as a thin Sim delegate (mirroring salvageItem) but emitted no event and had
no client entry point at all. Adds the disenchantResult sim event, exposes
disenchantItem/lastDisenchantResult through IWorldProfessions, implements
both Sim (now also emits the event) and ClientWorld, and adds the
disenchant_item wire command end to end (COMMAND_NAMES, server dispatch,
client send). ui_craft_disenchant is recorded and wired to
audio.disenchant() on a successful disenchantResult. No client UI calls
disenchantItem() yet, by design (that trigger is a separate, deliberately
deferred design pass), so the sound does not fire in-game until one is
built, but every layer beneath it is real and tested.

* fix(sim): suppress generic loot ding when a professions grant has its own cue

Every grant in the game flows through the shared Sim.addItem/addItemInstance
inventory hub, which unconditionally emits a loot event that hud.ts turns into
audio.coin()/audio.lootItem(). This meant every dedicated professions cue
(gather node type, craft family, masterwork, disenchant) was stacking on top
of the generic ding instead of replacing it. Adds an opts.silent flag threaded
through the emit, set only at the professions grant call sites; the loot
event's text feedback still prints as before, only the redundant audio is
suppressed. Also reconciles with upstream Professions 2.0 Phase 4's
gatherResult handler, which landed concurrently on the same hud.ts case.

* docs(sim): flag the silent-loot convention for Professions 2.0's later phases

Fernando's Professions 2.0 ledger (Phase 4: node materials and rare
events, Phase 13: enchanting and salvage reachable) both add new grant
call sites in exactly the code this session's silent-loot fix touched
(gathering.ts harvestNode, enchanting.ts's disenchant UI wiring). Left
a pointer at the opts declaration so those phases carry the { silent:
true } convention forward instead of reintroducing the double-ding bug.

* fix(test): widen the net-pipeline stall-gap clock guard past its 1 ms margin

tests/net_pipeline_stats.test.ts rewinds lastSnapAt by 900 ms to fake a
stall, and the recorder reads lastSnapAt <= 0 as its no-prior-snapshot
sentinel, so the rewind has to land strictly positive. The guard waited
for performance.now() to pass 901 ms, one millisecond of headroom, using
a single setTimeout.

That is not enough: setTimeout takes an integer delay and fires on
libuv's millisecond-truncated loop clock, so one fractional sleep lands
up to about 2 ms short of what performance.now() then reads. Measured
over fresh processes, the old guard leaves a NEGATIVE rewind roughly
once in 25, which nulls the gap sample and fails with gapMs.count 0.
That is the shard-4 failure on this PR, in a file this branch does not
touch.

Poll the clock until the invariant actually holds instead of sleeping
once, keep a 300 ms margin, and assert the precondition so a future
failure names the clock rather than the recorder.

fix(input): match gamepad look-pitch direction to mouse and touch

Gamepad right-stick look pitch was inverted by default versus mouse
and touch. stickToLook used pitchSign = -1 when invertY is off, but
pushing the stick up gives y < 0 per the W3C standard mapping (the
same convention this file's stickToMoveFlags comment documents), so
the result was a positive pitch delta that tilts the camera down.
Mouse's lookPitchSign and touch's touchPitchSign both use the
opposite ternary (on ? -1 : 1) for the identical semantic, giving a
negative delta by default that looks up, matching the function's own
doc comment. Flip the ternary so all three input paths agree, and
strengthen the existing invertY test to pin the absolute pitch
direction so this cannot regress silently again.

* perf(sim): make the physics broadphase allocation-free and pruned

Profiling the solver showed the largest per-tick garbage came from the
collider grid's template-string cell keys, which every movement, camera,
and line-of-sight query builds: empty ground allocated more than dense
ground did any collision work. Cells are keyed by a packed integer now,
multi-cell dedupe uses a stamp buffer owned by the grid instead of a
linear rescan, and the solver prunes the broadphase to what its swept
body can actually reach before running any slide iteration, so the inner
loops scale with obstacles in range rather than cell population. Step-up
also stops re-entering the broadphase per commit attempt.

Efficiency is pinned by counted WORK (candidates, sweeps, overlap tests
per solve) rather than wall clock, which does not rot across machines.

* fix(render): resample the terrain lean on a time budget, not a frame count

A frame-count cadence starves exactly where it matters: on a slow

fix(rift): clear the arrival point so entering a floor never pulls a pack

Rift floors put the player at zMin + 8 and planned the first trash band at
zMin + 22 (plus or minus 2 jitter), so the nearest mob landed about 12 yd from
where players arrive. Aggro is a pure radius check with no line-of-sight gate,
so the entrance porch wall never helped, and rift trash at level 22 to 23
against the level 20 player cap drives aggroRadius + leveldiff * 1.5 to an
effective 15 to 20 yd. The front pack pulled itself on arrival, every time.

sim/dungeon_door_clearance.ts already owned the overworld half of "never aggro
on entry", and authored dungeons got the interior half from hand-placed spawn
data. Rift floors are generated, so the interior half becomes a property of the
generator: new sim/rift/entry_clearance.ts with

  RIFT_ENTRY_CLEAR_RADIUS = MAX_AGGRO_RADIUS + MAX_WANDER_RADIUS

both imported rather than re-typed, so retuning either term moves the clearance
and its guard in lockstep. The wander term is load-bearing: an idle mob drifts
up to MAX_WANDER_RADIUS off spawnPos, so clearing only the aggro radius would
hold at the instant of arrival and then decay as the front pack wandered in.

The clearance is a z-axis floor, not a radial ring, because the generator's
clearance march (toClear) slides x toward the centre spine, which is the entry's
own x. A radial guarantee would not survive the march; z is untouched by it, and
any x offset only increases the true distance.

fix(render): pin the water surface paint order

The horizon apron runs under every per-zone surface plane and both ride
one transparent material with depthWrite off, so the depth buffer cannot
arbitrate between them: whichever paints last wins the blend outright.
Left to three.js's transparent sort that order comes from each object's
bounding-sphere centre, and the apron's is a world-scale sheet near the
origin, so merely orbiting the camera reordered them.

Measured on the Galecrest cliff with the player stationary, the sequence
flipped between APRON > zone (yaw 0.0 to 1.8) and zone > APRON (yaw 4.5),
swapping the sea between the apron's constant deep colour and the zone
plane's shallow tint plus foam band. That is the reported "water changes
texture when you move the camera".

Pin the order with explicit renderOrder: the apron under (-1), the zone
surfaces over (0). The zone planes carry the real per-vertex shore depth,
so they are the surface that must win. The sky dome already holds -10, so
the apron sits between the sky and the default band.

fix(render): key water shading on shore distance, not raw depth

Surveyed 30 shoreline samples across every coastal zone before touching the
shader. Two measured facts drive this:

  - The seabed is HARD CLAMPED at 6 yards below the water line. Max depth
    over all 30 samples is exactly 6.0; depth 15 is reached by none of them.
  - Shelf steepness spans an order of magnitude, from 3.2 yards of depth
    within 4 yards of run (drakelands) to 0.2 yards sustained over 40
    (palmreach).

The old surface keyed everything on absolute depth: foam below 3.2 yards and
a linear colour ramp over 0 to 6. Against that geometry the foam band covers
53% of the entire available depth range and averaged 47 yards wide, which is
why a flat bay rendered as one white sheet, and the colour ramp spent the
whole palette in the shallows and went flat beyond. No depth threshold can
serve both a 4 yard shelf and a 40 yard one.

Key foam on the HORIZONTAL distance to the waterline instead, recovered as
depth / seabed slope, with the slope baked per vertex next to the depth
(shoreSlopeAt). That gives a surf band of constant ground width on any shelf.

Also, since a 6 yard seabed cannot supply open-ocean depth:
  - exponential extinction over the real range rather than a linear ramp,
    reaching ~0.96 at the clamp so the apron stops reading as a seam
  - grade toward deep with VIEW DISTANCE, which is where ocean depth
    actually comes from
  - two decorrelated foam sines faded with range, so the band stops reading
    as wallpaper stripes and stops aliasing at grazing angles

tests/water_shore_shape.test.ts pins the surveyed geometry and asserts the
new band is far more consistent across shelf types than the rule it replaced.

perf(render): clamp outdoor fog on the nearest unbuilt chunk, not the nearest zone

Terrain streams in 60 yd chunks but residency was answered per ZONE, and the
outdoor fog clamp keyed off that answer. A zone rectangle is 36 to 54 chunks, so
one unprepared neighbour within ~53 yd pinned the view at MIN_OUTDOOR_FOG_FAR
until that entire rectangle plus its HDRI finished: measured live at 198 s still
clamped after a Drakelands portal, against an authored ember far of 360, and
about a minute of wall on a Thornpeak login 40 yd from the Mirefen border. The
clamp waited on roughly 20x the work that would have lifted it.

It now asks the terrain view how far the camera is from ground that has not been
built. At that Thornpeak login two of Mirefen's six chunk rows take it from the
45-yard floor to 152, instead of waiting on all 36 chunks and a sky.

New pure core src/render/chunk_residency_core.ts (Three-free, registered in
RENDER_PURE_CORES) owns the lattice, the query and the clamp, plus
orderCellsForEntry: the "which chunk next" decision, moved out of ensureZone so
a later globally nearest-first queue is a swap of one function rather than a
change to the zone lane around it.

The query is an exact bounded outward ring walk that assumes nothing about the
SHAPE of the built set. It deliberately does not cache a frontier radius: that
is only valid once builds are ordered nearest-first, and today they are
zone-ordered, so a radius over a union of rectangles reports a clamp that is too
generous and the player sees through a hole. Two brute-force equivalence tests
pin it, one over a zone-shaped built set and one over a disc-shaped one.

Residency flips on ATTACH, not on claim. terrain.ts already had a `built` set,
but it marks a cell BEFORE awaiting the idle-paced geometry, so keying the fog
off it would open the view over ground that has not arrived. The bitmap clears
in attachChunk, where the mesh joins the group, and a far-band 2x2 super-chunk
clears all four of its cells.

Cells no zone rectangle owns never clamp. 96 of the 792 cells are unowned (the
rects do not tile), so nothing will ever build them, and treating them as
pending would pin the view against a hole that never fills. The old zone clamp
did not clamp for them either, so this half is behaviour-preserving.

Sky gets its own lane (prepareZoneSky). A background prepare no longer waits for
a realm's HDRI before STARTING terrain, which was the second way sky gated the
fog: the chunk clamp alone would not have fixed it, because a neighbour's
terrain did not begin until its sky finished. HDRI plus PMREM is 30 to 70
percent of a prepare (Drakelands: skyMs 6083 of totalMs 8982), and a
neighbouring realm's IBL has nothing to do with whether you can see ground. The
gating path keeps sky first: the player arrives INTO that sky behind an opaque
loading screen, and its progress bar has to stay monotonic. Zone residency still
awaits both lanes, since the HUD map prewarm and the warmup gate key off it.
Note that skyMs and terrainMs in lastZonePrepareStats now OVERLAP on a
background prepare and no longer sum to totalMs.

fogFarForPreparedZones is deleted rather than left beside the new clamp, so
there is exactly one answer to "how far can I see". Its regression pins moved to
tests/chunk_residency.test.ts and now run against the live clamp, which is a
stronger place for them; the zone-policy tests they shared a file with are
untouched.

One trade, flagged rather than hidden: the clamp is terrain-only, so during a
BACKGROUND build a zone's ground can become visible before its water and zone
features land (those still run per zone, after all of its terrain). On the
measured idle numbers that window is about 10 s, against a 45-yard wall for the
full 105 s today.

- it samples the nearest point INSIDE the world, never past it. Real terrain
  out there is another landmass (measured -518 yards, i.e. dry ground), so
  sampling it directly painted land and surf across the open horizon
- slope comes from a finite difference on the depth just filled, not
  shoreSlopeAt, which costs four terrainHeight samples per vertex. It cannot be
  a constant either: the shader reads surf as depth/slope, so a constant 1
  against real shelf depths lands in the surf band and floods open water
- vertices far outside skip sampling entirely, which keeps the bake at 102ms
  rather than 378ms

Same thread, all "the sea has to read continuously from shore to horizon":

- colour rides a smoothstep across the full seabed range rather than an
  exponential still climbing when the seabed hard clamps, which creased the
  colour field along the clamp contour
- opacity gets its own faster curve and reaches full by the clamp, so an apron
  alone and an apron under a zone plane composite to the same colour
- the seabed drives 55% of the palette and view distance carries the rest.
  Bathymetry is not smooth, and a shelf break at a grazing angle compresses
  into a handful of pixels
- the interactive wave field feathers to zero at its window border instead of
  cutting hard, which stepped the surface normal that drives fresnel. Measured
  INVISIBLE on calm water (colour step across the border 11.84 vs 11.78 for
  open sea, ratio 1.01), so this one is defensive rather than the reported bug

perf(render): distance-cull the per-zone feature groups

Terrain culls per chunk against the live fog far, and foliage culls per bucket
against its own fog limit. Zone features did neither: they set frustumCulled =
true and stopped. Frustum culling only removes what is outside the view CONE,
so a feature group a kilometre ahead of the camera, entirely buried in fog, was
submitted every frame for as long as its zone stayed resident.

Measured in the Evergarden and in Mirefen, standing in NEITHER of the zones
involved, both readings byte-identical because nothing about them depended on
where the camera was:

  fen-features    17,214,888 triangles
  water-flora     10,959,942
  jungle-features 10,007,361
  garden-features  1,237,904
  water              777,602
  farshore-features  402,323

About 40M triangles of scenery for zones the player could not see, against a
renderBudget targetTriangles of 1,800,000.

Terrain is the control that proves the diagnosis: over the same two positions it
moved 173,158 -> 994,292, because it actually does the distance check. It was
never the problem, and 994k triangles for 630 yards of view is why long sight
lines are affordable here once this is fixed.

Each group's XZ footprint is measured ONCE at attach (they are static and
matrix-frozen, so bounds never move) and tested per frame against the same fog
far terrain uses. Edge distance, not centre: these groups can be hundreds of
yards across, and a centre test would blank a hedge maze the player is standing
at the corner of. A group whose bounds cannot be measured stays visible, since
drawing something cheap beats blanking a feature.

The decision lives in zone_feature_visibility_core.ts (Three-free, registered in
RENDER_PURE_CORES) because this is the THIRD copy of the same distance test
after terrain and foliage. Tests pin it at the real measured camera positions,
including the conservative case: from the Mirefen spot the Willowfen group is
162 yd out against a marsh far of 165, so it still draws. This only ever hides
what the fog had already made invisible.

Pre-existing, and unrelated to the fog work: these groups have never been
distance-culled. The chunk-streaming change made it noticeable by giving a
reason to go looking at frame cost.

Still worth a separate look: fen-features alone is 17.2M triangles, more than
everything else on that list combined, which smells like a content or merge
problem rather than a culling one.

fix(sim): return expired mail to the sender's stable id, not their name (#2450)

Expired player mail parcels bounced home by re-keying onto the sender's
plain display name (senderName), captured once at send time. If the

fix(sim): give Rupture and Rip the combo-point scaling every other finisher has (#2447)

* fix(sim): scale Rupture and Rip damage with combo points spent

Rogue Rupture and Druid Rip are combo-point finishing moves
(spendsCombo: true) but were authored as a flat 'dot' AbilityEffect
with no per-combo-point term, unlike every other finisher in the same
kits (eviscerate/ferocious_bite, slice_and_dice, kidney_shot all scale
via a perCombo field). Combo points were still unconditionally spent
on cast, so casting at 1 combo point dealt identical total damage to
casting at 5, breaking the combo economy tradeoff classic-era MMOs
rely on for these abilities.

Adds an optional perCombo field to the 'dot' AbilityEffect variant and
consumes it in the effect_dispatch 'dot' case the same way
finisherDamage/finisherHaste/finisherStun already consume spentCombo.
Rupture is now 16 base + 16 per combo point (96 at 5, same max payoff
as the old flat total) and Rip is 10 base + 10 per combo point (60 at
5), so only the shape changes from fixed to combo-scaling, not the
ability's power level at max combo.

* fix(sim): scale perCombo dot damage and fix Rupture/Rip tooltip base

scaleEffect's 'dot' case only scaled total, leaving perCombo (most of
Rupture/Rip's damage at high combo points) nearly inert against melee
and dot damage-percent modifiers; mirror the finisherDamage case and
scale both fields together. Also fix the $d tooltip fallback in
abilityEffectText (and the $o hybrid path in abilityOverTimeText) to
render dot effects with a perCombo term through the same
finisherDamage base/perCombo composition other finishers use, instead
of showing the useless 0-combo-point total.

Tighten the loose combo-scaling assertions in
combat_effect_dispatch.test.ts to exact tick-value deltas, add a
regression case with Assassination's meleeDmgPct baseline proving the
scaleEffect fix, and add tests/rupture_rip_tooltip.test.ts pinning the
$d text so it can never silently regress to the base term again.

* fix(ui): mirror the perCombo dot tooltip arm in the class detail cards

The character-select class detail cards in src/main.ts duplicate the $d
fallback logic and still rendered a bare `total` for a dot effect, so a
combo-point bleed finisher would print the uncastable 0-combo-point base
there. Not user-visible today (SIGNATURE_ABILITIES lists neither rupture
nor rip), but it is a trap for whoever adds one, so mirror the same
abilityUi.tooltip.finisherDamage composition the HUD path now uses.

Also pin the PR's real promise, that the 5-combo-point payload is
unchanged from the old flat totals (96 over 8 ticks for Rupture, 60 over
6 for Rip), which the existing 1-to-5 delta assertions would not catch,
and record why Rupture keeps a fixed 16 sec duration instead of classic's
combo-scaled duration so the next reader does not revert it.

effective weight of the mixer's scheduled actions falls short of 1: the
PropertyMixer blends the deficit back toward the bind transform. The

  weight: fading in from zero with no partner WAS the T-pose. That closes the

* fix(sim): stop a same-tick reciprocal lethal duel hit from killing a duelist

The duels-never-kill guarantee was a synchronous Map lookup: endDuel
deleted the duel entry for both pids the instant the first lethal hit
resolved, so a second, independently lethal hit against the other
duelist later in the same tick missed the lookup and fell through to
a real death. endDuel now defers the ctx.duels delete (marking the
duel with an endedTick instead) until updateDuels() purges it at
tick-tail, and is idempotent so a reciprocal call is a no-op. The
damage-clamp lookup in combat/damage.ts still matches a duel that
ended earlier the same tick, while duelFor() and the isHostileTo
duel check keep treating an ended duel as gone immediately, matching
the prior synchronous-delete behavior for every other caller.

* fix(sim): route duel-busy gates and the 1-HP clamp through duel lifetime, not raw map membership

The deferred-purge duel fix (endDuel keeps an ended entry in ctx.duels
until updateDuels() purges it at tick-tail) left several other consumers
still doing a raw ctx.duels.has(pid) check: duel request/accept in
duel.ts, and the arena/Vale Cup queue-join busy gates. Those saw an
ended-but-not-yet-purged duel as "still busy" for the rest of the tick,
which is unobservable inside a tick but bites when endDuel runs outside
one (Sim.removePlayer on disconnect): a surviving duelist immediately
re-challenging or queueing got a false "already in progress" error for
about one tick.

Route every one of those gates through duelFor(ctx, pid) !== null, the
same purge-order-independent check callers already use elsewhere, so
"ended" means the same thing everywhere except the damage clamp.

Also tighten the damage-clamp condition itself: key it purely on duel
lifetime (endedTick undefined or equal to the current tick) instead of
duel.state === 'active', since state is never flipped when a duel ends
and the old condition would keep clamping for one extra tick on an
ended entry that outlives its own tick.

* test(sim): update remaining raw ctx.duels.has/has(pid) duel-end assertions to duelFor

tests/deeds.test.ts and tests/duel_module.test.ts asserted the duel map
entry was gone immediately after dealDamage's finisher or a direct
endDuel() call, using ctx.duels.has(pid)/sim.duels.has(pid). That was
true before the deferred-purge fix but is no longer: endDuel() now
marks the entry ended (endedTick) and defers the actual delete to
updateDuels()'s tick-tail purge, on purpose, so a same-tick reciprocal
lethal hit can still find and clamp it. These two suites call
dealDamage/endDuel directly without running a tick, so they never see
the purge and the raw map-membership check now fails.

Switch both to duelFor(ctx, pid) === null, the same purge-order-
independent "has the duel ended" check every other consumer besides
the damage clamp already uses (tests/duel.test.ts was updated for this
in the original fix; these two were missed).

* fix(server): make the admin overview active/returning-account filter sargable

The admin Overview's active-account and returning-account subqueries
filtered on COALESCE(ended_at, now()) > cutoff, which embeds a volatile
function (now()) inside the filtered expression. Postgres can never
turn that into an index condition, so on a large play_sessions table
each of the four affected subqueries has to walk nearly every row on
every 60s admin Overview refresh, confirmed against a throwaway
Postgres container with 500k rows.

Rewrite the filter to the sargable (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at >
cutoff) form and add a new concurrent index on play_sessions(ended_at,
account_id) through the existing post-commit CONCURRENTLY seam
(server/concurrent_indexes.ts), so the planner can serve both arms of
the OR from a BitmapOr instead of scanning the table. A new
EXPLAIN-plan-pinning integration test reproduces the bug at 500k rows
and pins the fixed plan.

The duels-never-kill guarantee was a synchronous Map lookup: endDuel

damage-clamp lookup in combat/damage.ts still matches a duel that

ended-but-not-yet-purged duel as "still busy" for the rest of the tick,

The mobile report-window rule pins left and right to 10px so the box

rule still shifts it left by half its own width, pushing most of the

* fix(server): retire password_reset_requests, email_change_requests, and email_log from unbounded growth (#2622)

These three per-event tables were absent from the nightly retention
sweep and had no RETENTION_DAYS env key, unlike every sibling swept
table. Their per-account supersede DELETE (run when a new reset or
email-change request is created) only removes a duplicate still-PENDING
row, never a consumed or abandoned-and-expired one, so every completed
reset or email change left a permanent row forever, and email_log grew
one row per send attempt with nothing pruning it at all. A comment at
each DELETE site claimed this "keeps the table from accumulating dead
rows," which was true only for duplicate PENDING rows, not the actual
long-term growth path.

Adds prunePasswordResetRequestsBatch, pruneEmailChangeRequestsBatch, and
pruneEmailLogBatch (mirroring pruneClientPerfReportsBatch's shape),
registers them in main.ts's retentionSweep.tables, adds the matching
PASSWORD_RESET_REQUEST_RETENTION_DAYS, EMAIL_CHANGE_REQUEST_RETENTION_DAYS,
and EMAIL_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS config keys and .env.example entries, adds
a dedicated age-column index per table for the batch scan, and corrects
the misleading DDL and DELETE-site comments.

* fix(server): make the admin overview active/returning-account filter sargable

The admin Overview's active-account and returning-account subqueries
filtered on COALESCE(ended_at, now()) > cutoff, which embeds a volatile
function (now()) inside the filtered expression. Postgres can never
turn that into an index condition, so on a large play_sessions table
each of the four affected subqueries has to walk nearly every row on
every 60s admin Overview refresh, confirmed against a throwaway
Postgres container with 500k rows.

Rewrite the filter to the sargable (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at >
cutoff) form and add a new concurrent index on play_sessions(ended_at,
account_id) through the existing post-commit CONCURRENTLY seam
(server/concurrent_indexes.ts), so the planner can serve both arms of
the OR from a BitmapOr instead of scanning the table. A new
EXPLAIN-plan-pinning integration test reproduces the bug at 500k rows
and pins the fixed plan.

fix(auth): stop exempting a live session by bearer-token equality

Rubsey's OSSBrain review flagged that disconnectAccount's caller-session
exemption (server/game.ts) compared a live socket's stored auth token against
the HTTP caller's bearer token. A bearer token is a reusable wire credential,
not a per-socket identity: an attacker holding a stolen or shared token could
open their own live WebSocket with it, and that comparison would spare the
attacker's session exactly as readily as the legitimate device's, defeating
the whole point of force-disconnecting on a password change.

There is no channel today that lets the HTTP password-change request (served
by a standalone account portal page with no live WebSocket of its own) prove
which specific live socket, if any, belongs to the same user without relying
on that same reusable secret, so removing the exemption is the safe fix
rather than trying to patch it: disconnectAccount now always force-closes
every live session for the account, matching the password-reset path's
existing unconditional behavior. revokeTokensExcept still keeps the caller's
own bearer token valid so the portal page's own session is unaffected.

Reverts the ClientSession.authToken plumbing (game.ts, ws_auth.ts) and the
exceptToken parameter (game.ts, account.ts, main.ts) introduced for the
exemption, and updates the tests that pinned it: linkdead.test.ts now asserts
two sessions sharing one bearer token both get kicked, account_server.test.ts
and tests/server/account.test.ts assert the unconditional (2-arg) call shape.

fix(sim): per-zone respawn tiers, the coin curve for the ten July zones, and the escort ambush leak (#2677)

* fix(sim): respawn open-world trash on a per-zone tier instead of a flat 25s

Every open-world mob shared one 25s respawn, so a farmed camp regenerated
about three times a minute and dense packs paid gold and XP far past what
their zone was tuned for. Trash now respawns on its zone's level band
(60s up to level 7, 120s through 14, 180s above), resolved by a new pure
leaf that the death site calls with the mob's spawn point.

Templates that carry their OWN schedule keep the historical base: an
authored respawnMult (every shipped coefficient is a wall-clock target
expressed as a multiple of 25, so 144 is an hour and 864 six) and a bare
`rare: true` (whose 4x is the 100s every rare shipped with). Named rares
and minibosses are therefore byte-identical; trash and the four
open-world bosses that never declared a cadence are what move.

A host that passes SimConfig.respawnSeconds (the RL env, the fast unit
suites) still pins the whole world to that base, and mobs outside every
zone rect keep the 25s default, so instanced interiors are unaffected.

* fix(content): put the ten July zones on the coin curve and trim the outliers

Every open-world mob in amberfall, drakelands, evergarden, farshore,
frostveil, galecrest, nightbloom, palmreach, willowfen and wraithwood
dropped zero copper, while the pre-expansion zones paid a deliberate ~5
copper per mob level. Purse-carrying families now pay that same curve as
a guaranteed drop, and beast, spider and reptile trash stays coinless but
gains the harvest componentTags it should always have had.

Three mobs sat far above the curve and come back to it: ogre_crusher
200c to 85c, ancient_guardian 170c to 95c, treant_elder 150c to 90c.
bog_bloat and veiled_doe were coin-carrying beasts with no tags at all,
so they get theirs too rather than being grandfathered past the guard.

* docs(content): record why the Glimmermere camps stay on the waterline

These five sit in the gap between Thornpeak's ogre and revenant packs, so
all three fall into one farm cluster, and that reads like a spacing bug.
It is not one, and this pass verified it: the tarn itself lies inside the
corridor and the binding neighbours are the WESTERN packs, with Brutok
34yd from the first wader camp and an ogre camp 51yd from it. The best
separation reachable within 20yd of the shore is 54yd, under the 60yd
cluster link, so splitting the cluster means marching the mobs 50 to 70yd
uphill, against their own quest text ("climb out of the mere", and
Sethrael "glides the deep shelf... go down to the shelf"). Camps also
stamp terrain, so the move visibly reshaped the tarn's water dressing.

Comment only, no camp value changes. The farm problem is fixed at the
source: the respawn tier takes this corridor from 189 gold and 1.29M XP
per hour to 27.5 and 183k.

* test(sim): guard open-world farm density and the gold and XP ceilings

Adds farm_yield.ts, a pure leaf that prices a stretch of world by what it
sustainably pays per hour: union-find camp clustering plus per-cluster
kills, coin, item and XP throughput. Nothing in the live sim calls it; it
exists so this balance question has one shared model the guards pin.
Corpse-harvest income is deliberately outside it, since that yield is a
property of the harvester rather than of the camp.

camp_density caps fast-respawn trash per cluster, caps total mobs in
every band, pins the link distance that gives the other assertions their
teeth, and records the Thornpeak corridor as one deliberate dense cluster
bounded by yield. economy pins the ceilings about 25% over the shipped
maxima, the coin curve band with a negative control on each edge, the
guaranteed-drop rule, and the harvest-tag standard.

* test(professions): refresh the harvest partition pins for the new tags

Giving beast, spider and reptile trash their harvest componentTags moves
the harvestable population from 21 to 36 and the untagged one from 199 to
184. Both suites partition MOBS three ways and assert the sum, so the
counts move together; fen_troll is still the only tagged template whose
tags all miss the yield table.

* test(parity): re-mint the goldens for the respawn tiers

Mechanical regeneration via UPDATE_PARITY=1, no harness or scenario
change. The shared rng stream is untouched: zero draw-count or
draw-digest lines differ from the base branch. Five goldens move, and
only on respawnTimer (25 to 60, Eastbrook Vale's starter tier) plus the
state hashes that fold it in.

* test(sim): pin the respawn tier against the corpse-decay window

A review noted that giving coinless trash harvest tags makes those
corpses lootable where they were not, and updateMob defers an in-place
respawn while a corpse is still lootable. The effective delay is
therefore max(tier, corpse window), which farm_yield does not model.

It is safe today and now pinned rather than reasoned about: CORPSE_DURATION
is 60 and the fastest tier is 60, so the tier wins in every band. Exports
that constant so the guard compares the real values, and adds an
end-to-end check that a harvestable Eastbrook beast is back within a tick
of its 60s tier rather than 60 plus a corpse window.

Also drops a now-stale template census from the isHarvestableCorpse
docstring, which the new tags moved.

* fix(sim): stop escort ambush waves leaking permanent mobs into the world

A killed ambush mob outlived its run and became a permanent world spawn.
endRun drops surviving wave members but guarded on `!mob.dead`, so a
corpse was skipped; handleDeath had already given it a respawnTimer, and
updateMob then revived it in place with no run left to own it. Every run
therefore added however many of its wave the player actually killed, at
the same ambush point, forever. Escorts exist only in the July zones,
which is why players saw stacked mobs there and the older zones were fine.

Adds Entity.runScoped for a mob spawned by a RUN rather than placed by a
camp: the death site gives it an Infinity respawnTimer, so it never
respawns, and endRun now drops the wave in either state so a slain one
does not linger as a corpse that can no longer decay into a respawn. Both
halves are load-bearing and mutation-checked.

Repro first: tests/escort_ambush_leak.test.ts showed baseline+3 after one
run and baseline+9 after three, which is the reported pile.

* test(sim): add the open-world population invariant as a class detector

Enumerating spawn sites by hand does not scale, and the leak was found

All three respawn paths (releasePlayerSpirit, the shared corpse/Spirit
Healer/instance-reentry revive, and the delve respawn) forced facing
to 0 but left prevFacing stale, breaking the convention every other
forced-facing site in the sim follows. This made the render-
interpolated facing sweep from the pre-death heading instead of

roughly 130 to 140 degrees off with no way to recover if the player

all three sites, and resync the camera's lastInterpFacing on the
dead/ghost transition edge (isRespawnFacingResyncEdge in
camera_follow.ts), mirroring the existing click-to-move release
resync in updateCamera.

fix(social): make guild leader transfer atomic

guildTransferLeader promoted the target and demoted the actor as two
separate, non-transactional setGuildRank writes with no lock or
re-check between them. Two concurrent /gleader calls from the same
Guild Master could both read "actor is still leader" before either
write landed, so both promotions went through and the guild ended up
with two simultaneous Guild Masters.

(SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), re-checks the actor is still leader and the
target is still a member of the same guild, then updates both rows in
one transaction, mirroring addGuildMemberAtomic's shape. Swap the two
independent calls for the single atomic one and add a concurrent-race
regression test to the existing guild-atomicity block.

fix(sim): condition mob armor-DR floor on the mob being below target level

Address EnriqueGF's blocking review on PR #2601 (levy-street/world-of-claudecraft).
armorReduction carries no level-difference term, only the attacker's level and the
raw armor value, unlike meleeMissChance/spellHitChance. Capping mobArmorReduction
unconditionally therefore also neutered armor mitigation against same-level and
higher-level mobs (including raid bosses), redefining tanking balance far beyond
the low-level-mob-vs-high-level-player AFK-farming case issue #1050 targeted. The
floor now only kicks in when attacker.level < target.level, mirroring the exact

fix(sim): ramp the mob armor-DR cap with level gap instead of a hard cliff

Second-round review feedback on PR #2601: gating the armor-DR floor on
attacker.level < target.level fixed the over-broad tanking-mitigation
regression, but a hard min(dr, 0.2) right at that boundary is a
discontinuous cliff, a mob one level below the target snapped straight
from full uncapped DR to 20%, and the jump got larger the more armor a
player stacked. mobArmorReduction now ramps the cap linearly over the
same 3-level span aboveLevelMissPct already uses, so a one-level-down
mob keeps most of its natural mitigation and the cap only fully
saturates 3+ levels below, matching the far-below-level farm-loop case
issue #1050 is actually about.

the check would be a no-op today, but a future tuning change could make

fix(sim): per-zone respawn tiers, the coin curve for the ten July zones, and the escort ambush leak (#2677)

* fix(sim): respawn open-world trash on a per-zone tier instead of a flat 25s

Every open-world mob shared one 25s respawn, so a farmed camp regenerated
about three times a minute and dense packs paid gold and XP far past what
their zone was tuned for. Trash now respawns on its zone's level band
(60s up to level 7, 120s through 14, 180s above), resolved by a new pure
leaf that the death site calls with the mob's spawn point.

Templates that carry their OWN schedule keep the historical base: an
authored respawnMult (every shipped coefficient is a wall-clock target
expressed as a multiple of 25, so 144 is an hour and 864 six) and a bare
`rare: true` (whose 4x is the 100s every rare shipped with). Named rares
and minibosses are therefore byte-identical; trash and the four
open-world bosses that never declared a cadence are what move.

A host that passes SimConfig.respawnSeconds (the RL env, the fast unit
suites) still pins the whole world to that base, and mobs outside every
zone rect keep the 25s default, so instanced interiors are unaffected.

* fix(content): put the ten July zones on the coin curve and trim the outliers

Every open-world mob in amberfall, drakelands, evergarden, farshore,
frostveil, galecrest, nightbloom, palmreach, willowfen and wraithwood
dropped zero copper, while the pre-expansion zones paid a deliberate ~5
copper per mob level. Purse-carrying families now pay that same curve as
a guaranteed drop, and beast, spider and reptile trash stays coinless but
gains the harvest componentTags it should always have had.

Three mobs sat far above the curve and come back to it: ogre_crusher
200c to 85c, ancient_guardian 170c to 95c, treant_elder 150c to 90c.
bog_bloat and veiled_doe were coin-carrying beasts with no tags at all,
so they get theirs too rather than being grandfathered past the guard.

* docs(content): record why the Glimmermere camps stay on the waterline

These five sit in the gap between Thornpeak's ogre and revenant packs, so
all three fall into one farm cluster, and that reads like a spacing bug.
It is not one, and this pass verified it: the tarn itself lies inside the
corridor and the binding neighbours are the WESTERN packs, with Brutok
34yd from the first wader camp and an ogre camp 51yd from it. The best
separation reachable within 20yd of the shore is 54yd, under the 60yd
cluster link, so splitting the cluster means marching the mobs 50 to 70yd
uphill, against their own quest text ("climb out of the mere", and
Sethrael "glides the deep shelf... go down to the shelf"). Camps also
stamp terrain, so the move visibly reshaped the tarn's water dressing.

Comment only, no camp value changes. The farm problem is fixed at the
source: the respawn tier takes this corridor from 189 gold and 1.29M XP
per hour to 27.5 and 183k.

* test(sim): guard open-world farm density and the gold and XP ceilings

Adds farm_yield.ts, a pure leaf that prices a stretch of world by what it
sustainably pays per hour: union-find camp clustering plus per-cluster
kills, coin, item and XP throughput. Nothing in the live sim calls it; it
exists so this balance question has one shared model the guards pin.
Corpse-harvest income is deliberately outside it, since that yield is a
property of the harvester rather than of the camp.

camp_density caps fast-respawn trash per cluster, caps total mobs in
every band, pins the link distance that gives the other assertions their
teeth, and records the Thornpeak corridor as one deliberate dense cluster
bounded by yield. economy pins the ceilings about 25% over the shipped
maxima, the coin curve band with a negative control on each edge, the
guaranteed-drop rule, and the harvest-tag standard.

* test(professions): refresh the harvest partition pins for the new tags

Giving beast, spider and reptile trash their harvest componentTags moves
the harvestable population from 21 to 36 and the untagged one from 199 to
184. Both suites partition MOBS three ways and assert the sum, so the
counts move together; fen_troll is still the only tagged template whose
tags all miss the yield table.

* test(parity): re-mint the goldens for the respawn tiers

Mechanical regeneration via UPDATE_PARITY=1, no harness or scenario
change. The shared rng stream is untouched: zero draw-count or
draw-digest lines differ from the base branch. Five goldens move, and
only on respawnTimer (25 to 60, Eastbrook Vale's starter tier) plus the
state hashes that fold it in.

* test(sim): pin the respawn tier against the corpse-decay window

A review noted that giving coinless trash harvest tags makes those
corpses lootable where they were not, and updateMob defers an in-place
respawn while a corpse is still lootable. The effective delay is
therefore max(tier, corpse window), which farm_yield does not model.

It is safe today and now pinned rather than reasoned about: CORPSE_DURATION
is 60 and the fastest tier is 60, so the tier wins in every band. Exports
that constant so the guard compares the real values, and adds an
end-to-end check that a harvestable Eastbrook beast is back within a tick
of its 60s tier rather than 60 plus a corpse window.

Also drops a now-stale template census from the isHarvestableCorpse
docstring, which the new tags moved.

* fix(sim): stop escort ambush waves leaking permanent mobs into the world

A killed ambush mob outlived its run and became a permanent world spawn.
endRun drops surviving wave members but guarded on `!mob.dead`, so a
corpse was skipped; handleDeath had already given it a respawnTimer, and
updateMob then revived it in place with no run left to own it. Every run
therefore added however many of its wave the player actually killed, at
the same ambush point, forever. Escorts exist only in the July zones,
which is why players saw stacked mobs there and the older zones were fine.

Adds Entity.runScoped for a mob spawned by a RUN rather than placed by a
camp: the death site gives it an Infinity respawnTimer, so it never
respawns, and endRun now drops the wave in either state so a slain one
does not linger as a corpse that can no longer decay into a respawn. Both
halves are load-bearing and mutation-checked.

Repro first: tests/escort_ambush_leak.test.ts showed baseline+3 after one
run and baseline+9 after three, which is the reported pile.

* test(sim): add the open-world population invariant as a class detector

Enumerating spawn sites by hand does not scale, and the leak was found
twice by screenshot rather than by the suite. This asserts the property
instead: the open world may never hold more live mobs of a template than
its authored CAMPS place, plus the wave of a currently active run.

Drives every shipped escort through repeated run-and-kill cycles against
the real content tables. With both halves of the fix reverted it reports
"fen_sprite: 6 live vs 3 allowed" on the first round, so it detects the
original bug rather than restating the fix. A third case pins the eight
wave templates, so a newly authored escort visibly joins the sweep.

* feat(ci): add a dispatch-only OTA publish workflow with a layout-epoch preflight

Publishing reuses the R2 secrets the desktop publish workflow already holds for
this bucket, so no second standing credential can ship JavaScript to installs.

Dispatch only, unlike Desktop publish which fires on a release tag. A tag says
code was merged, never that a server runs it, and an OTA bundle replaces the web
layer on a phone while the server keeps running whatever it already had. A human
picks the moment, and the ref they pick is the bundle. That also enables the case
worth having: a JS-only fix built from the currently deployed commit, published
with no server deploy and no restart. Dry run is the default, so a stray click
uploads nothing.

The guard that replaces a tag's implied ordering is the world-layout epoch, which
is the only thing that actually has to agree between bundle and server: the
server requires the first WebSocket frame's discriminator to equal

still doing a raw ctx.duels.has(pid) check: duel request/accept in
duel.ts, and the arena/Vale Cup queue-join busy gates. Those saw an
ended-but-not-yet-purged duel as "still busy" for the rest of the tick,

Templates that carry their OWN schedule keep the historical base: an
authored respawnMult (every shipped coefficient is a wall-clock target

and minibosses are therefore byte-identical; trash and the four
open-world bosses that never declared a cadence are what move.

A host that passes SimConfig.respawnSeconds (the RL env, the fast unit
suites) still pins the whole world to that base, and mobs outside every
zone rect keep the 25s default, so instanced interiors are unaffected.

Every open-world mob in amberfall, drakelands, evergarden, farshore,
frostveil, galecrest, nightbloom, palmreach, willowfen and wraithwood
dropped zero copper, while the pre-expansion zones paid a deliberate ~5
copper per mob level. Purse-carrying families now pay that same curve as
a guaranteed drop, and beast, spider and reptile trash stays coinless but

feat(mounts): ship a procedural PBR surface pass for the tank mount

The tank shipped one flat colour per material and a constant vertex tint per
part, which its own look-dev spec lists under mustAvoid. It now carries six
procedural maps (metal and fabric, each albedo plus tangent normal plus packed
occlusion/roughness/metalness, every channel authored from its own field) and a
baked macro band in COLOR_0: cavity occlusion against the neighbouring parts,
ground contact and grime, settled dust, thinned paint on the up-facing bevels
and seam darkening on the rest.

UVs are box-projected in world space per triangle, so texel density is fixed in
yards and one shared map set serves parts of any size. Each projection group is
folded back by whole repeats and normalized into the unit range, with the scale
handed to KHR_texture_transform: quantize() skips any texcoord outside [0, 1],
and the float32 fallback cost more than the rest of the geometry put together.
Dark iron, leather and textile were lifted at the same hue, because the baked
darkening bands had no headroom and crushed the treads and cannon to black.

Geometry is untouched: 12,448 triangles, 19 primitives, byte-identical bounds.
Fixes a tiling bug the new test caught, where an anisotropic noise band wrapped
both axes on a single period and left a visible seam.

fix(sim): floor mob-vs-player armor DR and spell resist like the miss floor (#2601)

* fix(sim): floor mob-vs-player armor DR and spell resist like the miss floor

Mob melee/cleave damage and mob-cast spell resist against a player had
no directional floor, unlike swingMissChance's existing
MOB_VS_PLAYER_MAX_MISS cap on mob melee miss. A heavily armored or far
above-level player (or hunter/warlock pet) could still mitigate a
landed hit down toward nothing, so defensive-pet AFK farming of
low-level mobs stayed effectively risk-free (issue #1050).

Add mobArmorReduction (types.ts) and isMobSpellResisted
(combat/spell_resist.ts), mirroring swingMissChance's exact hostile-
mob / player-side directional guard and MOB_VS_PLAYER_MAX_MISS's value
(0.2), and wire them into Sim.mobSwing, the mob_swing.ts cleave
splash, and updateRangedPetAttack's mob-cast resist roll. The reverse
direction (player/pet attacking a mob) is untouched.

* test(parity): regenerate goldens for the mob-vs-player damage floor

The mob-vs-player armor DR and spell resist floor (fix(sim) in this
branch) intentionally changes combat scalars in scenarios where a
hostile mob hits a player or player-owned pet, so the golden-trace
parity gate turns red by design. Regenerated via UPDATE_PARITY=1; the
rng draw counts and digests are unchanged in every affected frame,
confirming only the resulting damage/state values moved, not the draw
order.

* fix(sim): condition mob armor-DR floor on the mob being below target level

Address EnriqueGF's blocking review on PR #2601 (levy-street/world-of-claudecraft).
armorReduction carries no level-difference term, only the attacker's level and the
raw armor value, unlike meleeMissChance/spellHitChance. Capping mobArmorReduction
unconditionally therefore also neutered armor mitigation against same-level and
higher-level mobs (including raid bosses), redefining tanking balance far beyond
the low-level-mob-vs-high-level-player AFK-farming case issue #1050 targeted. The
floor now only kicks in when attacker.level < target.level, mirroring the exact
inverted case swingMissChance and isMobSpellResisted already correct for; a mob at
or above the target's level (Nythraxis's Gravebreaker splash included) keeps the
full, uncapped armorReduction scaling in both directions. Regenerated the affected
parity goldens (fight duration/draw counts shift because mitigated damage moved,
not draw order).

* fix(sim): ramp the mob armor-DR cap with level gap instead of a hard cliff

Second-round review feedback on PR #2601: gating the armor-DR floor on
attacker.level < target.level fixed the over-broad tanking-mitigation
regression, but a hard min(dr, 0.2) right at that boundary is a
discontinuous cliff, a mob one level below the target snapped straight
from full uncapped DR to 20%, and the jump got larger the more armor a
player stacked. mobArmorReduction now ramps the cap linearly over the
same 3-level span aboveLevelMissPct already uses, so a one-level-down
mob keeps most of its natural mitigation and the cap only fully
saturates 3+ levels below, matching the far-below-level farm-loop case
issue #1050 is actually about.

Also documents why isMobSpellResisted omits the same level gate
(spellHitChance already clears the resist floor at or above level, so
the check would be a no-op today, but a future tuning change could make
it bind silently).

The linear armor-DR ramp changes mitigated damage (and downstream
state) for any golden scenario with a hostile mob 1-2 levels below its
target, without touching draw order: rng.draws and rng.digest are
byte-identical in every affected frame across all touched goldens, only
state/entity values moved.

fix(economy): thread crafted-item provenance through trade and market (#2605)

* fix(economy): thread crafted-item provenance through trade and market

Player trade and the World Market re-granted a crafted item's plain
copy with no craftedRecipeId marker (PendingGrant in social/trade.ts
and MarketListing in market.ts both lacked the field), so trading or
selling a crafted item on the World Market laundered its provenance:
the recipient's copy looked indistinguishable from a never-crafted
one, and disenchanting it granted full Enchanting skill, bypassing
the already-shipped equip/buyback anti-farming gate.

Both paths now reuse items.ts's removeVendorSellUnits/VendorRemovedUnit
per-unit removal (already used by vendor sell/buyback) instead of the
old bulk fungible decrement, so every removed unit's craftedRecipeId
is known and carried through the re-grant. Trade buckets its plain
regrant by marker; the market adds craftedRecipeId to MarketListing
and threads it through list/buy/cancel/collect/persistence, splitting
a sell request into one listing per provenance bucket for the rare
items that are both craftable and drop-sourced (boundstone_helm,
gravewyrm_gauntlets) so a listing's marker is never approximate.

* fix(economy): pre-validate market listing cap and per-bucket min price

Review on PR #2605 found the provenance-split marketList could still
exceed MARKET_MAX_LISTINGS (a dual-provenance sell adds multiple rows
but the cap was only checked once, before the split) and could price a
bucket at 0 copper when the ask floored below MARKET_MIN_PRICE per
row, handing the item away for free. Preview the bucket split before
escrowing anything, refuse the sale if it would breach either
invariant, and floor every row's price at MARKET_MIN_PRICE so the
split can never mint or lose copper. Adds two regression tests for the
cap and min-price cases.

* fix(economy): thread crafted-item provenance through bank and mail

EnriqueGF's review on PR #2605 found that the bank and mail systems
launder a crafted item's provenance the same way trade/market did
before this PR: moveBetweenContainers dropped the plain-stack
craftedRecipeId marker on a deposit/withdraw round trip (no
counterparty needed), and mailSendResolved escrowed via a blind
removeFungibleItem while mailTake re-granted with no marker at all.
Both now thread craftedRecipeId through the same countFit/addStacked
pair buyBackItem and the market fix already use; mail additionally
switches its escrow to removeVendorSellUnits (skipping every
instanced copy, matching the existing fungible-only restriction) so
a dual-provenance stack splits into per-bucket attachments instead
of collapsing the marker. Added regression tests in bank.test.ts and
mail.test.ts.

fix(social): make guild leader transfer atomic (#2606)

guildTransferLeader promoted the target and demoted the actor as two
separate, non-transactional setGuildRank writes with no lock or
re-check between them. Two concurrent /gleader calls from the same

regression test to the existing guild-atomicity block.

* feat(sim): evade home when an engaged mob cannot reach its target

Mobs chase in a straight line with a slide fan and no pathfinding, so a mob
whose target stands past a wall (the rift ledge exploit) pinned in place
forever and got killed for free: the leash never fired because it measures
the mob's own displacement, and a wall-pinned mob barely moves.

New src/sim/mob/reachability.ts watches every engaged tick from
updateMobCombatProfile as a postlude: out of reach, zero movement committed,
straight step toward the target eaten by a collider. After 5 seconds of that
(CHASE_STALL_TIMEOUT) the mob enters the existing evade state: walk home
immune, heal to full on arrival. Holds (not resets) under root so root spam
cannot re-arm the clock; casters in spell range, healers holding, CC'd mobs,
and canLeash false encounters never accumulate. Draws no rng and the new
chaseStall field stays 0 in every parity scenario: goldens are byte
identical.

kind 'evade' damage event for direct attacks (DoT and reflect ticks stay
silent) so the client can float the word and log the line.

The new kind 'evade' damage event renders exactly like the other avoidance
results: an Evade word in floating combat text (reusing the miss colour

* fix(render): resume dropped world-entry prewarm entries in idle time

The world-entry prewarm (Renderer.prewarmInitialScene) abandons any
manifest entry that starts past its wall-clock deadline and never
revisits it, so entries like foliage.materials, weather.materials,
landmarks.impact-site, vfx.atlas, interiors.materials,
sky.current-zone, and render.settle-passes were silently and
permanently dropped. Their compile debt then paid out later as a
mid-play shader-compile stall (issue #2571) instead of during the
loading screen.

deadline is now mutable so a resumed entry can get a fresh window,
and dropped entries are collected during the main pass. Once that
pass finishes, a fire-and-forget background pass (new pure module
prewarm_resume.ts, mirroring the existing prewarm_pass.ts hooks
pattern) resumes each dropped entry in original manifest order,
each behind its own idle slot, reusing the exact same runEntry
closure. Because drops always form a contiguous suffix of the
priority-ordered manifest, resuming programs.compile (when it was
also dropped) still whole-scene-compiles whatever the earlier
resumed entries just staged.

Newly staged groups are hidden immediately after each resumed entry
(compile()/compileAsync() traverse hidden objects fine) so nothing
flashes in front of the player once the loading curtain is gone, and
the shared cleanup teardown is extracted so the resume pass can skip
vfx.clear() specifically: it would otherwise wipe live gameplay
particles instead of just the prewarm burst. World-entry timing is
unaffected since the resume pass is never awaited.
