* docs(render): record why compileAsync stays one call per gated target

#2571's third fix asked to batch compileAsync into one call per frame
instead of one per gated view, on the premise that each call compiles
the whole scene individually. Investigated against the pinned three.js
WebGLRenderer.compile()/compileAsync() source directly rather than
taking the premise on faith (the same discipline commit 1 applied to
the sky.biome-variants manifest-entry claim).

Finding: compile(scene, camera, targetScene) only calls getProgram/
prepareMaterial by traversing `scene`, the first argument, which every
call site here already passes as the single gated node, not the whole
scene ("Only initialize materials in the new scene, not the
targetScene" per the source's own comment). The whole-scene traversal
that does happen every call is `targetScene.traverseVisible` for LIGHT
gathering only, needed so the compiled program gets the correct light-
count shader variant; it is a plain isLight check over the scene
graph, not a shader compile, and at the runtime view-create budget
that is at most a handful of redundant walks per frame, not a handful
of redundant scene-wide compiles.

A real batch (one compileAsync call covering several already-placed
targets) is not achievable through the public API without either
reparenting each target out of its real scene position, breaking its
transform, or cloning every target into a scratch container purely to
compile it, which costs more than the cheap traversal it would save.

No functional change: this documents the finding at compileGate (the
shared core commit 2 introduced) so the batching idea does not
resurface from a stale premise.

fix(sim): let the Wildheart chain pull reach the whole basin (#2745)

DungeonDef.bossChainPull (#2645) woke every living mob when Zulgar was
pulled early, but only the packs near the shrine ever arrived. The pull
anchors each woken mob's leash on the PULLER so the group can drag them
70 yards once the fight starts and no further. That anchor is right for
the fight and wrong for the journey: DUNGEON_LEASH_DISTANCE is 70 and
the basin's route is about 180 yards end to end, so a mob woken at the
entrance packs starts 170 yards from its own anchor, already outside its
own sphere. The leash prelude in mob/combat_profile.ts evaded it home on
its first engaged tick, before it took a step.

Measured headless on the real instance with the puller at the shrine:
19 of 19 woke, 13 evaded one tick later, 6 arrived. The six are exactly
the upper-convergence packs inside 70 yards of the shrine.

A pulled mob now carries a transit grace (Entity.chainPullInbound, new
module mob/chain_pull_transit.ts) that suspends the SOFT leash while it
crosses. The flag is self-clearing on arrival rather than on a timer:
once the mob is inside the leash sphere it is where the pull wanted it,
the grace is spent, and the ordinary leash governs from that same
anchor, so a group still cannot walk the instance out through the door
one pack at a time. It reuses the shape and the one-yard hysteresis of
the flee-recovery grace sitting one branch above it.

Deliberately narrow: it holds only the soft leash. The hard tether is
checked first and measures from the spawn, and the unreachable-target
stall still runs as a postlude, so a chain-pulled mob pinned by geometry
evades home on the normal 5s clock. One deliberate consequence,
documented in the module and the PRD: a group that pulls and runs is
chased rather than leashed, since a mob kited away from the pull point
never reaches the sphere that would spend its grace. That stays bounded
by the instance, because the exit portal and a wipe both scrub the pull.

Only bossChainPull dungeons can set the flag, and Wildheart Basin is
still the only one, so every other mob takes the identical branch it
took before. Draws no rng: the parity goldens are unaffected.

Six new tests, each verified to fail with the fix neutered.

fix(gate): measure real memory availability on macOS, not os.freemem() (#2810)

* fix(gate): measure real memory availability on macOS, not os.freemem()

The vitest worker clamp read os.freemem(), which on macOS counts only
completely unused pages. macOS deliberately keeps almost none, filling
idle RAM with file cache and inactive pages it reclaims on demand, so a
healthy Mac reports near zero and the clamp collapsed to a single worker.
Observed on a 14-core / 26 GB host: freemem 1.47 GB (1 worker, the whole
suite serial) while memory_pressure reported 68% free and vm_stat showed
about 12 GB reclaimable.

The failure compounds under the repo's own multi-worktree workflow, since
freemem also drops as sibling gates allocate, tightening the clamp exactly
when throughput matters. New scripts/lib/gate_memory.mjs derives
availability from vm_stat on darwin and leaves every other platform on
os.freemem(); any read or parse failure falls back to it, and the result
never goes below it, so the change can only widen the sensor. The clamp
itself is unchanged: a swapped-out worker still reads as a flaky test.

* fix(gate): wire the availability sensor into gate_profile, drop purgeable

Review follow-ups on the darwin memory sensor.

gate_profile computed its worker count from raw os.freemem() while gate and
gate:fast used the new sensor, so profiling a macOS host under-threaded
relative to the gate it exists to measure, and baselines compare the two
directly. It now uses the same resolver and prints the availability figure
next to free, so a worker count that does not follow freemem is explainable.

The vm_stat sum no longer counts purgeable pages: like file-backed pages,
a purgeable page also sits in the active or inactive queue, so adding it
double counted. Erring low is the right bias for a clamp whose job is to
keep a worker from swapping. Also aligned the gate_fast header and the
tier-workers policy wording with the new sensor.

fix(gate): run the i18n release tier as its own job, not over the whole suite (#2822)

* fix(gate): run the i18n release tier as its own job, not over the whole suite

The release test job carried I18N_RELEASE_TIER at job level, so one red
job meant either "a test is broken" or "the release locale fill has not
run yet". A release branch is red for pending locales through most of a
cycle, so the second reading swallowed the first: a real dungeon finder

release-gate now runs at PR tier, so a red shard there is always a real

flag) by tests/release_i18n_tier_coverage.test.ts: a new tier-sensitive
suite cannot quietly stop running under the tier.

fix(render): guard the shader pow() bases that NaN into a black rectangle (#2790)

* fix(render): guard the shader pow() bases that NaN into a black rectangle

GLSL pow() returns NaN for a negative base, and the weapon-skin fresnel
shell raised 1.0 - abs(dot(n, v)) where both vectors are normalized in
shader, so the base went an ulp negative along the silhouette. The
material is additive, so that NaN reached the bloom, whose separable blur
smeared one bad texel into the hard-edged black rectangle players saw for
a frame near Hoarfrost weapon skins.

Clamps every affected base: the two shell shaders, the aurora ribbon, the
water fresnel whose max() bounded only the low side, and the offline
inspector's mirror of the same shaders. Adds a guard that walks every
pow() in the tree and fails on a base that is not provably non-negative,
plus a pin keeping every shell exponent positive, since the clamp makes
an exact 0.0 base reachable and pow(0.0, y) is undefined for y <= 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(render): close the pow() domain guard the review found open

The base guard shipped fail-open in three places. Its classifier read
max(x, 0.0) / 0.0 and clamp(x, 0.0, -1.0) as clamped terms, though the
first is NaN or Inf on the shipping lowering and the second is undefined
outright, so multiplication and division are now separate arms with a
positive finite divisor, and clamp bounds must be finite literals in
order. The twinkles weight leaned on the range of sin(), whose precision
GLSL leaves to the implementation, so it carries a real clamp now and its
provenance rows anchor that whole expression. The exponent pin imported
src/, so it said nothing about the offline mirror: asset_pipeline now
pins the mirror shell powers equal to the runtime tiers and above zero.

Moves the scan onto a new shared walker, tests/helpers/source_files_under.ts,
which owns the source-extension policy (the JS/TS family plus standalone
shader files), visits each directory realpath once so a symlink cycle
terminates instead of hanging collection, and throws on a link out of the
root rather than narrowing the corpus silently.

Also corrects an inverted explanation in every comment carrying it: the
fresnel base approaches zero where the vectors are aligned, i.e. where the
surface faces the camera head-on, not on the silhouette.

fix(server): unbreak the release gate after the Seeker merge (#2835)

* fix(server): defer the Seeker runtime's db reads to call time

PR 2423 added walletForAccount to server/db and captured it in
seeker_entitlement's module-scope REAL_RUNTIME literal. That literal reads
every imported binding the moment the module loads, so any suite whose
vi.mock('../server/db') factory omitted the new export threw at IMPORT
time and failed to collect. 37 unrelated suites went red that way (xp,
markers, ip_block_kick, playtime_grant and more), none of which touch
Seeker, which is why the release gate failed across all eight shards with
what looked like 37 broken features rather than one missing mock line.

Each entry now forwards at call time, so an under-specified db mock only
matters to a test that actually exercises the path, and the next export
added here cannot repeat it. Forwarding arrows rather than getters
deliberately: setSeekerEntitlementRuntimeForTests spreads REAL_RUNTIME,
and a spread would read getters straight back into the same throw.

Pinned by tests/server/seeker_entitlement_import_isolation.test.ts, which
mocks db WITHOUT the Seeker exports on purpose: fixing that factory
instead would pin the opposite of the invariant.

* test(android): follow the flavor split, and cover every shipped activity

PR 2423 split the Android app into play and solanaStore flavors: the
shared behavior moved to BaseMainActivity and each flavor ships a thin
MainActivity that only overrides plugin registration. This suite still
read the old single-activity path, which no longer exists, so the file
failed to collect and took the release gate red alongside the Seeker
db-binding breakage.

Repointed at the base class, and added the assertion the split now
requires: reading one file only proves the shipped app enters immersive
mode if every flavor's activity actually inherits it. The flavors are
discovered from the source sets rather than listed, so a third one cannot
join without either inheriting the base or failing here.

withdraws it; B's autosave committed its CHARACTER half while the book half
could not be replayed, so B's purse durably gained what the book never durably
lost; A then takes itself over (an ordinary re-login), which fences A and rolls

demand, for any amount and for items too. The retry bound never applied,
because the arm that fires when nothing can resolve short-circuits it.

be applied, the character half must not commit. A refused book half now aborts
the whole transaction, character row included, and the save is retried. An
anomaly row is an audit trail, never a substitute for atomicity.

When the shortfall can never resolve, the session's live state is abandoned
rather than half-committed: its own book ops come back off the live book, it is
quarantined so it can never persist again, and it is disconnected to reload
from its durable row. That is the rollback a lease fence-out already applies,
and it conserves precisely because none of it was ever durable.

plan had accepted: a rung is never granted from a base that has not reached it,
and never without its charge. The residual and settled-prefix machinery is gone
with the arm it existed for, which deletes the two lifecycle bugs that lived in

* fix(guild-bank): close the four security-review gaps in the rollback path

A quarantined session could be RESUMED. planJoin only refuses a resume on
`left`, so a client reconnecting inside the linkdead grace got back a session
whose every save returns early, forever: it plays normally and persists
nothing, with no error and no signal. Silent unbounded data loss is worse than
any refusal, so the resume is refused and the client lands on a fresh join that
loads its durable row, which is what the rollback intends. The guard also has
to sit INSIDE the queued save closure, not only at the call: a save enqueued a
moment before the rollback would otherwise run after it, committing a character
blob whose book ops have just been undone.

The blocked window is the price this design charges an innocent officer, and it
was eight autosave intervals of UNRELATED progress (a refusal commits no
character half either), aimable by an attacker who deposits, waits for an
ordinary withdrawal, and relogs. A refusal now FLUSHES the sessions it is
waiting on, so the ordinary case clears in a round trip rather than 30 seconds,
and the bound drops from 8 to 2. The docs claimed one interval and were
understating it eightfold; they now say what it is and name the griefing
surface.

The netted-replay rescue arm returned without the size bound its sibling
applies, so a write through it could push the row past what the read accepts
and brick the book: every officer of that guild quarantined forever and the
boot load skipping it. Both arms go through one guard now.

Quarantine reverted only the refused guild while abandoning the whole session,
leaving a second book's deltas live as phantom value for another officer to
withdraw and be refused for in turn. It reverts every book the session dirtied.

Tests: the retry bound is reachable (two officers alternating ladder rungs is
the only shape that can deadlock both replays, since gold and items cannot make
both nets negative), the last save resolves rather than retries, a refusal
flushes what it waits on, a save queued before a rollback lands nothing, the
resume refusal, and the guild-delete window's throw-path release and
dirty-mark interaction.

fix(client): close the same-frame zone-warmup teleport race (#2801)

A user-reported clip showed a one-frame black rectangle and an unprepared,
too-close camera right after a death/respawn zone transition. Reading
src/main.ts's frame() loop confirmed the mechanism: maybeWarmCurrentZone()
runs once at the top of frame() and reads offlineSim.player.pos before the
offline tick loop below it runs, but a tick can itself teleport the player
(release-spirit/resurrect, a dungeon door, or a portal trigger) between that
check and the renderer.sync() call later in the same frame. The teleport is
only detected on the FOLLOWING frame, one frame after it already rendered the
new, unprepared zone with no loading curtain.

Add a second maybeWarmCurrentZone() call right after the offline tick loop
and before renderer.sync(), so a mid-tick teleport is caught in the same
frame it happens. The existing top-of-frame call is left in place: it still
owns the input-suspend ordering and catches a teleport triggered from outside
the tick (a UI action) before the tick even runs. The function is already
idempotent per call (early-returns once a warmup is in flight or the zone is
ready), and its lastWarmCheckX/Z and rift-band tracking are safe to update
twice in one frame since the second call correctly measures the displacement
between the pre-tick and post-tick position. Live verification against a
running offline session (instrumented, then reverted) showed the pre-fix
code detecting a real mid-tick teleport (a dungeon door trigger) one frame
late, and the fix detecting the identical teleport in the same frame it
lands.

* fix(render): give the dragonkin real run cycles and measured gait refs

The elite skated because these rigs ship a Walk and no sprint: aliasing
run->Walk asked a cycle whose natural speed is 4.24 yd/s to cover a 9.5 yd/s
chase, and since locomotionTimeScale clamps at 1.6x, no reference speed
could close it (the feet moved 5.75 while the body moved 9.50, a 65% slide;
the broodguard was ~70%).

Two halves. The build now synthesizes a genuine Run per rig by
time-compressing the Walk (elite 1.87x, broodguard 2.6x, whelp 3.5x), which
raises each cycle's natural speed without touching stride, and the ClipMaps
point run at it. Then every dragonkin def declares MEASURED walkRef/runRef
(tmp/dragonkin_gait_measure.mjs computes 2 x stride x normScale x
entityScale / duration, exactly what the matcher divides body speed by)
instead of inheriting defaults tuned for a scale-1 humanoid. Because refs
are per-def and scale-dependent, Cindraleth takes her own def: at scale 2.85
her stride covers 33% more ground per cycle and the lord's refs over-strode
her by 25%.

timeScale 1.10 with its feet at 8.70 yd/s against a 9.50 body, an 8% slide
down from 65%, and the wander walk matches too. The whelp keeps a residual
by physics, not oversight: 0.9yd tall at 10 yd/s is 11 body-lengths/sec and

breakable-fear chances draw per aura) and a gameplay-selection input

Addresses every should-fix from the review, one per area:

Switch to vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300),
matching the pattern already used by the other tests in this file,
so the debounce fires deterministically instead of racing wall-clock
time.

* test: restore real timers via try/finally or afterEach, not a bare trailing call

Three files called vi.useFakeTimers() and only restored real timers as the
last statement of the test body, with several expect() assertions in
between and no try/finally or afterEach safety net:

- tests/moderation_service.test.ts: single fake-timer test, restore was the
  unconditional last line after 6 assertions.
- tests/mobile_chrome_fade.test.ts / tests/touch_tap.test.ts: every test
  in the file used this shape, with no describe-level afterEach at all.

If any assertion in between throws (a real regression, not hypothetical),
the test aborts before reaching vi.useRealTimers(), leaving the fake clock
frozen for every later test in the same file (Vitest isolates by file, not
by test) and turning one real failure into a cascade of unrelated,
confusing ones. Wrap the moderation_service.test.ts body in try/finally and
add a describe-level afterEach(() => vi.useRealTimers()) to the other two,
matching the pattern tests/admin/guilds_page.test.ts already uses.

* test(net): replace a ~1.2s real-clock poll with a fake performance.now()

The stall-gap test needed performance.now() to read strictly past a fixed
rewind point before it could set up its precondition, and did that by
polling the real clock in a setTimeout loop (a prior fix for a genuine
race: a single fractional sleep can land up to ~2ms short of what
performance.now() then reads, since setTimeout fires on libuv's
millisecond-truncated clock). That made the precondition safe but left a
real ~1.2 real-second wait on every run of this file.

tests/interest.test.ts already fakes performance.now() via
vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['performance'] }); do the same here and
vi.advanceTimersByTime() straight to the target instead of polling a real
clock, making the precondition instant and exact rather than a timed race
against libuv.

* test: close real HTTP servers and clear real intervals via try/finally

Two tests started a real resource (a node:http Server bound to a real
ephemeral port; a PeriodicCollector arming a real 60s setInterval) and
only tore it down as a plain sequential statement after the assertion(s)
that used it. Since expect(...) throws on a mismatch, an assertion
failure between start and teardown skipped the cleanup entirely:

- tests/deploy_game_ops.test.ts: the healthcheck probe test leaked its
  listening server (and the second one) past the failing assertion.
- tests/server/http/periodic_collector.test.ts: the immediate-refresh
  test leaked the real, unref'd 60s interval, which keeps calling the
  mocked query()/onError sink after the owning test and its mocks are
  torn down.

Wrap each resource's lifetime in try/finally so cleanup always runs, the
same way tests/server/static_sfx_serving.test.ts's requestStatic() helper
already does for its own listen+use span.

* test(escort): give CPU-bound tick-loop tests headroom under the 20s default

Four escort-quest tests drive real sim.tick() loops (up to 6000 ticks,
i.e. up to 300 simulated seconds at the fixed 20Hz DT) with no explicit
timeout, relying on vite.config.ts's global testTimeout: 20000. One of
them ("a slain wave unravels after its loot window instead of
respawning into the run") reproduced as an actual failure: it timed out
at 26 to 34 real seconds standalone, with zero other CPU contention on
the machine, let alone under CI's parallel workers.

For the three tests that genuinely need to drive terrain movement or
mob AI tick by tick (a deadline that cannot be jumped ahead), add an
explicit timeout sized above measured wall time, following the existing
convention in tests/stable_yard.test.ts and tests/emerald_deck_escape.test.ts.

For the one that reproduced a real timeout, go further: it was ticking
2000 times just to wait out a corpse's 60s loot-window decay, where
every intermediate tick can only ever observe "still dead" or "gone",
the same two states a direct jump proves. Set corpseTimer to the edge of

pattern already used by tests/loot_master_sim.test.ts (da4441ffa4) for

of just giving it more room, and drops that test's wall time from
26-34s to well under a second.

"surfaces guild renames in the realm-wide moderation history" read back

Closes the review's blocking finding, and the gap is one this PR opened. A
druid's maximum armor weight is leather, and the only int/spi families were
Stormbound, which is mail and unwearable, and Cinderweave, which is cloth and a

slot, because the caster budget is the caster budget; armor is Ashstalker's slot
for slot, because armor is a function of weight and item level rather than of
stat identity; prices come off the existing slot ladder. No requiredClass, like
every other WARFARE piece, so it gates on armor type and a rogue may wear it and
gain nothing.

The capstone is Thornguard, dodge on cast rather than a third absorb. That is a
direct answer to the review's per-family finding: this family is the furthest
ahead of the five, and dodge is avoidance, so it does not compound the stamina
weighting the caster families already carry against their PvE counterparts.

fix(ota): offer updates to devices reporting a native build number

Self-hosted OTA has never reached a store-fresh device. Capgo sends
`version_build` as the native BUILD identifier (iOS CFBundleVersion =
CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION, Android versionCode), a plain integer like 47,
and a device that has not yet applied a bundle sends
`version_name: 'builtin'`, which makes planOtaUpdate fall back to exactly
that field. parseSemver only accepts MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, so the value
parsed to null and the endpoint answered no_new_version_available at HTTP
200: silent, and indistinguishable from being up to date.

Reproduced against live prod before the fix: `builtin` + `46` returned no
update, `builtin` + `0.34.0` (the only shape the tests ever used) returned
the offer.

A build number cannot be compared to a semver manifest without knowing
which marketing version a given build shipped as, so this adds that one
data point (server/ota_native_build.ts). Build numbers are monotonic, so
one point is enough: below it the device is on an older store build and
gets the bundle, at or above it the device runs this release's assets and
is compared normally. That keeps a device on the current store build from
re-downloading a half-gigabyte bundle of bytes it already has.

The bridge is a release surface now, so release_version.mjs prepare writes
it from the BUMPED native numbers and check verifies it against the same
project files; a release that forgets it fails the release gate instead of
going dark. minNativeVersion resolves through the same path, since it had
the identical semver assumption.

Tests use REAL build numbers, which is what the old suite never did: every
existing case fed version_build a marketing-style semver, and one even
pinned a non-numeric build resolving to null as correct, so the suite was
green while the product was dark. Verified the new cases fail against the
old behavior (4 red) before they passed.

curtain and the initial scene linked at first live draw. The rework,

  kept 2725 roots alive for ~500 programs (5450 prologues, 12 s of pure
  submission).

  starved behind a resumed unit's off-thread link tail, and it skips
  groups already submitted by the early entry.

modules through src/render/gfx.ts, so ordinary gameplay churn moves it while
every image byte stays identical. A new pure module classifies the drift and

fix(ci): abort dead checkout transfers with git's low-speed floor

The runner-side checkout-stall class rides a git fetch at zero throughput
until the job bound kills it (run 31392590628 bound-killed the same lane
three attempts in a row, 20 minutes each). A workflow-wide git low-speed
abort ends any transfer under 1000 bytes/s for 120 consecutive seconds,
and actions/checkout retries the fetch in-step, so most stalls now
self-heal in about two minutes instead of holding a required check to its
bound. Values and workflow-level placement pinned in ci_workflow.test.ts.

feat(ci): auto-rerun runs killed by the checkout-stall class once

A workflow_run reactor reruns a completed CI run's failed jobs exactly
once when the run died of the stall class: attempt 1 only, and only when
the dead step is a setup step with every later step skipped, so a rerun
can never mask a real test failure or loop. The cancelled arm requires
the runner's own timeout annotation, which separates a bound kill from a
user or concurrency cancellation; the failure arm covers the new git
low-speed fast abort. Decision core is pure and pinned against the real
incident job as fixture; the driver is fail-closed relay glue. This is
docs/merge-queue.md's own triage rule as automation.

re-queued by a rerun), serialize duplicate webhook deliveries with a
per-run concurrency group, make the reactor checkout blobless and give it
the same low-speed floor ci.yml carries, and pin the driver's four
fail-closed paths (malformed env, partial jobs page, annotations read
failure, rerun POST failure) in the stub-gh harness. Also correct the
permissions header claim about nightly.yml and soften the no-test-ran

changes made to 3b88123c4db829dc981cd1d0d7bdcc9494bdd5a1.

fix: scan tracked root wt files

Keep untracked OSS Brain helper worktrees ignored while adding tracked root .wt files back into the malware scanner input set. Fail closed if Git reports the root as a worktree but tracked .wt enumeration cannot complete.

Add regression coverage that force-adds a .wt payload and verifies the scanner includes and flags it.

fix(assets): compress GLB geometry that lacks it, not only re-apply

The mandatory post-exporter step appended quantize + meshopt behind
`if (cls.hadMeshopt)`, so it only ever re-applied a codec that a read had
decoded. Any GLB produced outside build_assets.mjs, which is the whole
Tripo asset-pipeline output, collected its KTX2 textures and skipped
geometry compression permanently, and did so again on every re-run. The
23 WEAPON_VFX skins were dropped from the file walk outright, though
their sanctioned exception is about drawable TEXTURES and says nothing
about geometry.

classifyGlb now reports what a file owes (needsTextures, needsMeshopt)
instead of one texture-driven skip flag, and the WEAPON_VFX partition is
a per-file textureExcluded flag rather than a removal from the walk.

A source that ALREADY carries KHR_mesh_quantization is dequantized back
to float first. Re-quantizing an integer POSITION accessor in place
destroys the model: rift_portal.glb, the one shipped file in that state,
came out with POSITION max [0, 32767, 0], every x and z collapsed to
zero, a 4.7 MB flat line.

public/models/weapons/ is exempt from the geometry ADD, and narrowly: the
pass still RE-APPLIES the codec where it already exists. Quantization
recentres a mesh onto its bounding box and compensates on the node, but
assets.ts documents that a variant weapon's origin IS its grip point and
flattenWeaponScene then discards that node position, so the weapon hangs
low; 36 weapons also carry a hand-tuned grip override calibrated against
the old origin. Confirmed in game before excluding. Lifting this needs
the grips recalibrated first, which is eye work.

The post-transform check had to get stricter rather than looser. It
compared counts, under a comment scoping it to a texture-only pass, and
quantize legitimately inserts an anonymous node to carry a TRS the source
node cannot absorb and copies a shared skin per quantized mesh. Merely
allowing counts to grow would have stopped noticing a node REPLACED
rather than added, so geometryPassViolations checks identities, counts
added wrappers as a DELTA rather than a total (many shipped GLBs already
carry wrapper-shaped nodes, so a total would hand them free slots), and
compares each primitive's POSITION proportions, because the rift_portal
corruption kept its whole graph intact.

One pass of the fixed converter over public/models. 27.01 MB to 15.07 MB,

By family: creatures 15.09 to 6.25 MB, props 8.30 to 7.13, chars 1.84 to

test(assets): lock geometry coverage and re-pin the suites the pass moved

glb_meshopt_coverage.test.ts is the sibling of glb_texture_compression
and owns the geometry half. It scans every shipped GLB and fails on any
file missing EXT_meshopt_compression, with exactly one exemption: the
weapons directory, pinned at its exact count of 65 so a new uncompressed
weapon cannot join it silently, and every member checked to really live
in an excluded directory.

A scan alone would not stop the next regression, since the defect was the
converter declining to ADD the codec, so two subprocess cases drive the
real script: one over a freshly authored GLB, one over a GLB that is
ALREADY quantized whose 4 x 1 x 9 proportions must survive. The second is
the rift_portal.glb regression, where re-quantizing an integer accessor
in place flattened every x and z to zero while meshes, nodes, materials
and vertex count all stayed correct.

Eleven cases pin the guard directly, including a node the source's own
pre-existing wrappers would otherwise have paid for, a skin that only
reorders its joints, and a primitive whose shape changed with its graph
intact.

The rune pads and maledict_eye are re-pinned. Three of their assertions
stopped meaning what they said under quantization rather than merely
moving: the node scale is no longer identity, and POSITION and UV bounds
read raw storage integers, so the `0 <= uv <= 1` claim would have been
false while still passing a re-pin. Those switch to the normalized
accessors. Exact toEqual on the extension lists was kept exact.

src/render/assets/manifest.generated.ts is a transitive input of the

rendererFingerprint and invalidates all 230 portraits, not the 14 whose
model this change actually recompressed. The receipt mechanism then

ground ring, but the renderer dropped the emitted spellfxAt event's
school before calling MageGroundFx.spawnRune, which hardcoded arcane
regardless. A fire boss's windup rang up a violet ring that did not

material can never resurface with a stale tint from a different
school's cast, and caps each tint's HSL lightness before the ring's
additive brightening multipliers: a near-white school (physical,
holy) already sits close to full brightness, so multiplying it
further used to clip every channel to indistinguishable white.

authors no school and falls back to physical, so its windup ring hit
exactly this before the cap.

fix(render): evict far zones under constrained memory to stop iOS crash-reload

preparedZones in renderer.ts only ever grew during play: once a world zone
streamed in, its terrain and water geometry stayed GPU-resident for the
rest of the session, with no eviction path outside an editor-only full
rebuild (docs/design/chunk-streaming.md documents this as unstarted stage
4 work). Desktop/Android tolerate that as an intentional trade, but iOS
WebKit kills the WebContent process outright once its per-process memory
ceiling is crossed, so a player walking through several zones over a few
minutes accumulated geometry that was never freed. This is a different
failure mode than the earlier boot-time iOS fixes (#3139, #2946, #3222):
it only shows up during ordinary continuous play, matching reports of
crashes and silent reloads after several minutes.

Adds a constrained-memory-gated eviction pass: a new pure policy core
(zone_eviction_core.ts) picks the farthest prepared zone beyond a safety
radius from the player, and new TerrainView/WaterView.unloadZone methods
release that zone's geometry and reset its residency to "pending" so it
rebuilds normally on return, indistinguishable from a zone never visited.
Gated entirely behind the existing GFX.constrainedMemory flag, so
desktop/Android behavior is unchanged. Verified live in a real browser
under an iPhone user agent (scripts/ios_zone_eviction_shot.mjs): 141 of
261 resident terrain chunks released across two evicted zones, with the
player's current zone still rendering correctly afterward.

Reviewed by frontend-seam-reviewer and qa-checklist (dispatched fresh in
parallel); addressed a real correctness bug they found (eviction measuring
distance from the camera instead of the player, which could race a
post-teleport arrival-neighborhood prepare under the camera's damped-spring
lag) plus several test-coverage gaps (the Phong/iOS water no-op arm, an
exhaustive per-cell terrain round-trip, and a live-geometry safety-margin
pin against the real zone table).

Also re-mints the Eastbrook polish provenance seal (its composite
fingerprint pins renderer.ts's bytes) via the existing
remint_polish_provenance.mjs tool, required by any renderer.ts edit.

fix(sim): never let a training dummy execute for its full remaining hp

Sentence's 100-Condemnation finisher deals a normal mob's whole
remaining health as one hit once it drops under 20% hp, so a real kill
never overkills. The Training Dummy (999,999 hp, deliberately near
immortal) was never excluded from that finisher, so a long DPS-testing
session that ground it under the threshold reported the dummy's entire
remaining health pool as a single Sentence hit, dwarfing every other
number and corrupting the very combat meter the dummy exists to let
players read (reported: a 149298 hit against normal Needle of Fate/Wand
hits in the low hundreds).

Excludes dummy-flagged mobs from the finisher's normalMob check, the
same pattern already used to keep dummies out of aggro, retaliation,
and deed credit. Added a regression test that reproduces the original
bug (fails before the fix, passes after) alongside a control case
proving real trash mobs still execute normally.

feat(inventory): add a player-controlled item lock

Implements issue #3042: a player can lock/unlock any bag copy from the
right-click context menu. A locked copy refuses salvage, profession-craft
reagent consumption, and vendor sell (single and bulk), each with a clear
denial reason distinct from a genuine shortage, and shows a padlock badge

fix(render): bound the compileAsync isReady poll pass in the three patch

One checkMaterialsReady pass polled every pending material with a
synchronous COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR query each; with hundreds of pending
programs and a link-backlogged GPU process one pass measured 10.2 s on
the production main thread (hitch-hunt S3). A pass now checks materials
round-robin under a 2 ms budget, always at least one, and the reschedule
interval backs off 10 to 320 ms on expensive passes, resetting only when
queries come back cheap: N concurrent pollers can no longer own the main
thread while links settle. Hardware without KHR_parallel_shader_compile
resolves on the first pass exactly as before.

fix(render): pay dropped prewarm debt promptly instead of losing it to the reveal

Production logins overran the 15 s prewarm hard deadline inside the
compile-submit loop (22 s of uninterrupted prologue work), which dropped
the deadline-exempt debt payers behind it: the initial scene first-drew
unlinked programs (blocking uniform reflection, 17 s across two frames)
and the dropped remainder resumed at the lowest queue priority, starved
for minutes behind the cosmetic preview lane (hitch-hunt S1 to S5).

The submit loop now consults prewarmSubmitShouldStop between units and
defers the remainder instead of overrunning; the compile entry drains
deferred units first, bounded by min(gpuSubmitDeadline,
compileAwaitDeadline) so the await reserve protecting world.initial-frame
survives, counts them into its honesty gate, and any leftover hands off
to the resume lane as a programs.compile-submit dropped entry. Dropped
link and upload debt resumes at the new BOOT_DEBT priority, above the
preview lane and below zone prepare, with held tails so batches settle
serially and the driver link queue stays shallow, and the serial resume
lane orders debt entries first (orderPrewarmResumeEntries). Mid-run
deferral withholds warm-pool publication like the whole-entry path.

fix(render): address review round 2, sky recovery, flip staging, ratchet

A half-loaded biome could never repair itself: the any-asset resident
set both drove eviction (correct) and suppressed ensures (wrong), so a
dome that landed while its env arm exhausted retries stranded the biome
half-ready forever. The plan now takes a separate fully-ready set that
alone suppresses re-fetches, and the residency lane gates off the tiers
that never fetch HDRIs. The companion hole: loadHdr left a terminal
rejection in its cache for the session, so the recovered ensure was
handed the old failure without a single new attempt; it now evicts on
failure identity-guarded, the loadGltf black-void precedent. Both are
pinned by regressions at the plan, sky-store and loader levels. The
flip staging moves from a predictable path in the shared os.tmpdir to a
private per-run mkdtemp (0700) removed afterward. And rather than
raising the renderer monolith ratchet, the whole sky-residency lane
extracts to sky_residency_driver.ts behind a read-through host
interface: renderer.ts returns under the original 13800 ceiling
(13768) and the raise is reverted; the polish provenance re-mints for

and material.roughness via geometryRoughness = dFdx/dFdy(nonPerturbedNormal)),

Guard the normal in patches/three@0.185.1.patch: reset it to a valid unit
vector when its squared length underflows to zero. It is a no-op for finite
normals, so it is look neutral; validated NaN to 0 by a direct-to-RT readback
with the composer scrub out of the path. The existing OutputGradePass scrub
stays as defense in depth against any other NaN source on this driver path.

The patch changes pnpm-lock.yaml, a hashed leaf in the source fingerprint of
the Eastbrook-era GLB families, the shared surface atlas, and the Fenbridge
support maps. A re-export is not viable (the current build_assets.mjs emits
WebP but these assets ship KTX2), so remint_lockfile_fingerprints.mjs swaps
the embedded fingerprint in place across 27 GLBs byte-stable (KTX2 and
geometry untouched, sizes identical, no visual change), and the dependent
test literals, evidence JSONs, polish provenance seals, and the media
manifest were re-pinned.

fix(render): keep the self-motion predictor smooth across a long render frame

Online, the local avatar stalled and then lurched around every long render
frame: the browser applies the snapshots queued during the block only
afterwards, so the predictor's authoritative anchor is frozen during the
frame and then sweeps several ticks in one interval. The leash clamped the

rushed at up to twice run speed, sometimes stepping backward.

the frozen anchor could not cover (capacity the episode earns on the wall
clock, bounded by BLOCK_EPISODE_MAX_MS) and the divergence servo sits out the
burst sweep, whichever way the browser ordered the queued snapshots. Steady
low fps opens nothing and keeps its servo behaviour. SelfMotionFrame carries
snapAgeMs and snapIntervalMs for that; the net contract docs record the one
sanctioned exception. Pinned in tests/self_motion.test.ts (long render
frames): 24 of the file's 53 cases fail on the previous predictor.

source so a future bump reds instead of silently killing the prewarm again.

leaving nine skinned mount rigs permanently resident and unreachable by
every cleanup path (matrix/submission/shadow cost paid every frame forever).
Fixed by staging through a single mount_prewarm.ts helper that adds the
group to the scene exactly once.

The desktop-path run() was a no-op that still reported 'completed' via
resolvePrewarmEntryStatus (the exact starvation-hiding bug that function's
own docblock warns about); it now does the real staging work and declares
progress(). resumeUnits now compiles both the color and shadow-depth
program halves (three's shadow material uses a different cache key), not
color alone. The lazy GLB fetch inside the resume lane's serial await is
now bounded by a timeout so a stalled connection cannot park a queue slot
for the session, and a rejected fetch is evicted from the memo cache so a
later sighting can retry. vfx.mount-programs is removed from
CONSTRAINED_PREWARM_RESUME: forcing nine skinned rigs resident contradicts
the GPU-footprint reasoning that list otherwise enforces, and needs a real
constrained-device measurement first. Manifest array order and priority are
now both ascending. Re-minted the Eastbrook polish provenance pins (both
renderer.ts and prewarm_policy.ts moved again).

fix(render): key delve interior builds by z-position, not moduleId

pickDelveModules randomizes which module occupies which slot on every
run, but the renderer's build cache was keyed by
`delve:<delveId>:<slot>:<moduleId>`. Two runs sharing a slot could
randomize a different module into the same z-stacked position; once
that moduleId's geometry had been built anywhere in the slot, the
cache treated the position as done and skipped rebuilding it there,
so the previous run's walls (built at a different z-offset) stayed
standing while this run's mobs, puzzle interactables, and boss spawn
against the server-authoritative geometry of the module actually
occupying that position. Players could walk through the stale/missing
walls and see content spawned "outside" what they could see.

Re-keys the cache by position (`delve:<delveId>:<slot>:<moduleIndex>`)
and retires the stale group when the moduleId at a position changes,
mirroring the existing rift-floor stale-retirement pattern. The
position-vs-module decision is extracted into a pure, unit-tested core
(delve_interior_cache_core.ts); the scheduling/retirement itself moves
into delve_interior_tracker.ts to keep renderer.ts under its monolith
line-count ceiling (lowered after the extraction).

fix(desktop): allow data: in the Electron CSP connect-src so KTX2 zstd GLBs load

Three's ZSTDDecoder (KTX2Loader's Zstandard path, taken by every UASTC
normal/occlusion map) boots its WASM with
fetch("data:application/wasm;base64,...").then(r => r.arrayBuffer()), a
connect-src request to a data: URI. The desktop shell CSP listed

was refused with "Refused to connect" and world entry died on the desktop
app, the only host that ships a CSP. 170 shipped GLBs carry zstd textures,
so this broke the v0.39.0 desktop build at world entry.

data: is a self-contained inline scheme, not a network origin, so unlike a
remote host it opens no exfiltration path; img-src already lists it for the
same embedded-texture reason. The connect-src pin test is updated to match.

feat(tutorial): stage the first death, then teach the walk back

CX asked for a death lesson after the guild board, made very clear. A
new player's first death is the most confusing moment in the genre: the
screen greys, they are somewhere else and translucent, and nothing says
the way back is to walk to their own body. So the island stages it,
somewhere nothing is hunting them.

The death is scripted and consented to (walk to the Passing Stone, press
interact, the same shape as every other lesson's press) and free of
consequence, since this game charges no durability on death. The stone
is sited 65 yd from the island graveyard, which leaves about a 30 yd
ghost run once the corpse-resurrect reach is subtracted: long enough to
teach the walk, short enough that a first death is not a punishment.

Two things keep it from stranding anyone. The rite refuses a player who
has not been asked, with an explanation, so it can never be a griefing
tool. And credit lands on EITHER resurrection path, because a player who
took the Spirit Healer has no corpse left to walk to, and a quest they
can never finish is worse than one finished the long way; the copy still
sends them to their body and the healer arm nudges them there next time.

The coach card swaps body across all three beats, since a card that says
"go kneel" is useless to a corpse.

The island now runs ten lessons on the same XP budget, so the wreck line
and the signpost give some back rather than pushing a graduate past
level 3 before the final hand-in. Parity goldens re-minted: rng digests
and draw counts are byte-identical across all 67, only state hashes
moved, which is the entity-renumber signature of adding one ground
object.

fix(render): route kit surface detail by atlas swatch, and un-collide the pirate kit

The harbour ships and the dock watchtower rendered as masonry over every
surface, sails included. The kit-wide 'stone' entry for khex wins over all
material-name routing, and the whole KayKit hexagon kit ships one mesh with
one material over one shared atlas, so a hull, a sail and a stone footing
are literally the same material: name routing cannot tell them apart, and
the detail layer projects in world space, so it tiled brick across all of
them equally.

What CAN tell them apart is the atlas cell each triangle samples. The new
kit_uv_surface_core routes per triangle from measured UV swatch blocks, and
the partition of the shipped meshes is exact: the ship splits 774 wood /
764 cloth / 42 stone and the watchtower 1144 / 226 / 120, with no triangle
straddling a boundary and none unmapped, which its test asserts rather than
tolerates. Scoped to the ships, boats and tower; the kit's buildings read
correctly on the existing routing and are left alone.

Separately, the white rowboats were a real defect. A kit is a material-dedup
namespace, but 'pirate' spanned two different atlases, so the first file
extracted handed its atlas to the rest: the rowboats took a near-white
palette cell instead of their authored brown and the dock platforms washed
out to pink-grey. Splitting the sea half into its own namespace restores
both. The fishing hull is authored on a near-white cell, so its uvs are
retargeted to the plank cell at extraction, leaving the shipped asset and
its fingerprint pins untouched.

fix(sim): stop bursting pushback-clipped channel ticks at completion

Channeled abilities run two clocks: the overall duration (castRemaining)
and a fixed-count per-tick schedule (channelTickTimer/channelTicksLeft).
A mid-channel hit shortens castRemaining via pushbackCast's channel
fraction (classic-era pushback) but never touches the tick schedule, so
enough hits can end the channel before one or more ticks were ever due.

updateCasting's completion-time flush loop (added only to rescue a
single tick lost to floating-point drift, the Arcane Missiles 5-barrage
bug) unconditionally force-fired every remaining tick regardless of
whether it was actually due, so a pushback-shortened Consume fired every
orphaned tick in the same instant the channel ended: "only one hit
during the channel, then two hits at once" per the report.

Gate the flush on the tick's own schedule (channelTickTimer <=
CAST_COMPLETE_EPS) so it still rescues a genuine float-drift tick, and
explicitly drop channelTicksLeft afterward so an orphaned tick is simply
never fired, matching the reduced total damage a shortened classic-era
channel is meant to deal instead of bursting it.

fix(ui): stop a HoT's periodic tick from extending the combat meter's segment

The damage/heal/threat meter closes its current segment 5 seconds after the
last party combat activity, unless a live mob is still holding aggro. A HoT's
periodic tick was treated as full party activity and refreshed that clock the
same as a direct heal or a hit, so a HoT still ticking down after a kill (or
kept rolling by the healer into the next pull) held the segment open past its
own 5s window indefinitely. Back-to-back pulls with a healer topping off the
tank between them never got their own segment, merging into one and losing
the per-pull breakdown the meter exists to show.

Gate the periodic-tick heal2 events (SimEvent.hot) out of the activity clock:
the tick still tallies into whichever segment is open, so healing recorded
during the fight is unaffected, but it no longer refreshes lastActivity and a
lone tick with no segment open no longer spawns a phantom one. Direct heals
and damage are untouched.

fix(sim): stop a hostile proc or dot outliving the duel-ending blow

Players kept dying seconds after a duel ended: a 4pc set-bonus proc, a
legendary weapon proc, or a dot riding an ability's own direct hit
(Fireball, Immolate) all fire unconditionally right after dealDamage
returns in the swing/cast path. When that very hit is the clamp-and-end
blow, endDuel() clears the loser's auras BEFORE the proc/dot below it
runs, so the fresh hostile effect lands a beat later with nothing left
to purge it: the duel is over, so it ticks freely and kills the 1-hp
loser for real.

Adds duelJustEndedBetween(ctx, recipient, opponent) beside duelFor in
social/duel.ts (resolved through pvpController, the same "opponent"
definition endDuel's clearAurasFromController already uses, and
requiring the OPPOSITE side of recipient so a self-heal or a heal onto
the ex-opponent is never wrongly suppressed) and gates the three
reachable call sites: combat/set_procs.ts (target-applied set procs),
combat/equip_procs.ts (weapon procs whose effects include a persistent
dot/attackSlow, never heal/hot/chainArc), and combat/effect_dispatch.ts's
'dot' case (a same-cast rider). Investigated and ruled out a fourth
candidate, Warlock Evil Eye/Maledict Gaze: it re-checks isHostileTo on
every tick independently, so it already stops dealing damage the
instant a duel ends and needed no code change.

Reproduced test-first against the real Sim for each of the three sites,
plus a direct table of duelJustEndedBetween cases (opponent, self,
third party, active duel, non-player recipient). Three independent
fresh architecture-reviewer passes ran against this diff; the last two
reported zero remaining blocking or should-fix issues.

fix(render): bound the KTX2 restore wait so a graphics-preset switch can't stall for minutes

A live graphics-tier switch (Options > Graphics > Apply) recycles the WebGL
context, which fires the same webglcontextlost handler used for a real GPU
crash: it re-transcodes every KTX2 texture the session has ever loaded (a
weakly-keyed, session-wide registry, not scoped to the zones about to be
shown), and the rebuild curtain awaited that unconditionally. On a session
that has visited many zones, that backlog serializes through a shared
4-worker transcode pool with zero progress reported, turning a routine
settings change into a multi-minute white screen. It also left the socket's
onclose/onmessage events queued and unprocessed for that whole window, so a
connection the server had already closed only surfaced once the stall ended,
plausibly explaining the accompanying "boom, login screen" report.

ktx2MipsRestored() now races its existing Promise.allSettled against a
KTX2_RESTORE_MAX_WAIT_MS (3000ms) watchdog and returns whether it settled or
timed out, mirroring the bounded-wait pattern every sibling stage in this
same rebuild already uses (VIEW_PREWARM_MAX_MS, FAR_VISTA_ENTRY_MAX_WAIT_MS).
It is deliberately the tightest of the three, not the loosest, since this
stage protects only a cosmetic, self-healing transient. ktx2MipsOnContextLost
now starts restores most-recently-armed first so a large backlog does not
starve the zone the player is actually standing in, and a non-finite maxWaitMs
waits outright instead of hitting the setTimeout(fn, Infinity) coercion trap.
Anything still in flight past the bound keeps restoring in the background and
logs a dev-channel warning so a field recurrence stays observable. The call
site in main.ts is unchanged (the bound is the default parameter), so the
pinned wiring test's literal call-site match still holds.

Two independent fresh reviews (general-purpose plus render-performance-
reviewer) adversarially checked this diff; their actionable findings (bound
sizing, restore order, default-path/literal test coverage, the Infinity trap,
timeout observability) are folded in above. Their remaining finding, that the
restore fan-out still is not registered with background_gpu_queue.ts (so
restores that outlive the bound now upload in a live frame instead of behind
the curtain), and properly scoping restoration to only the zones about to be
shown, are both left as follow-ups rather than risking a larger change here.

fix(render): pace KTX2 restore re-uploads through the GPU work queue

Closes one of the two follow-ups this PR deliberately deferred: a released
texture's re-upload (mipmap swap-in plus needsUpdate) used to fire the
instant its transcode resolved, unpaced, in whichever live frame that
happened to land in. On a long desktop session (zones are never evicted off
unconstrained hosts) a webglcontextlost can carry a large backlog through the
shared transcode pool, and letting every finished restore's re-upload land
together turns context-loss recovery, including a real GPU/driver hiccup
mid-play with no curtain at all, into an unbudgeted GPU work burst right
after the canvas just recovered from one loss.

ktx2MipsOnContextLost now takes the current renderer's background_gpu_queue
(read live from src/main.ts, since the renderer is rebuilt in place) and, so
each restore's re-upload runs as one queued unit at the cosmetic BACKGROUND
priority instead of applying immediately. The graphics-rebuild curtain still
waits on the full pipeline (transcode plus its queued re-upload), so it
cannot reveal stubs. No queue, or a queue that refuses (a rebuild/shutdown
racing the restore), falls back to the pre-existing immediate apply: this
stage is a self-healing cosmetic transient, never worth stranding a texture
on stubs over.

The remaining follow-up (scoping restoration to only the zones about to be
shown, instead of the whole session-wide registry) still needs new
on-demand-restore-on-zone-visit plumbing that doesn't exist yet, and stays a
separate follow-up.

fix(desktop): no Linux PRIME offload when the NVIDIA card drives the screen

two or more meant a laptop with an integrated GPU on the screen and an

fix(render): make the NaN guard unconditional, module-scoped, and driver-tested

Round two of review (madmatah) found two blocking issues in the reworked
final-color NaN guard: the !GFX.gradePass gate installed it on the tier
cohort with the LEAST exposure (composer tiers, where a NaN survives and
smears via bloom, never got it; direct tiers, which the guard's own
rationale said were already safe, got it anyway), and nothing in the test
suite ever compiled the patched GLSL against a real driver, so a broken
chunk could ship as a silent all-black frame.

The gate is gone: installFinalColorNanGuard() is now unconditional,
argued from GLES leaving NaN-to-fixed-point conversion undefined rather
than from "the composer path already covers it". A new browser test
compiles the patched chunks in real headless Chromium with
checkShaderErrors forced on, then goes further than the literal ask and
injects a runtime NaN into outgoingLight (both fogged and unfogged) and
diffuseColor.a, reading back via a FloatType target so a NaN that a
driver's own UNSIGNED_BYTE clamp would otherwise mask stays observable.
Each of the three injection tests was confirmed to actually discriminate
by temporarily gutting the relevant scrub and watching only the matching
test fail.

Chasing the review's CharacterPreview ordering nit further than the one
example given surfaced two more renderers with the identical gap
(characters/portrait.ts, armory_preview.ts): neither runs through
initGfxTier either. Rather than chase every current and future call site
(a per-site call was tried first and missed two of those three), the
guard now installs itself unconditionally at module scope in
final_color_nan_guard.ts, so importing it (transitively true for every
renderer in this codebase via gfx.ts) is what covers all of them. gfx.ts
keeps the import for that side effect but no longer calls the function
itself: a fresh review caught that the old explicit call had become a
provable no-op there, with a comment that no longer matched.

Also fixes the alpha channel (diffuseColor.a was never scrubbed before,
though fog_fragment never touches it either), adds a ShaderLib coupling
pin for the #ifndef USE_FOG optimization's load-bearing assumption
(every stock shader with <opaque_fragment> also has <fog_fragment>), and
corrects the PR's prior coverage claim: several of the repo's custom
ShaderMaterials (water, terrain, the delve portal) do include
<fog_fragment> and get that arm of the guard.

fix(net): apply the staged OTA bundle instead of reloading the stale one

The visible OTA gate applied a finished download by calling the plugin's
reload() on downloadComplete. The plugin emits that event from inside its
download routine, before it verifies the bundle or records it as next (and
even updateAvailable fires one statement before setNextBundle, on both
platforms), so reload() found no pending bundle and rebooted the running
one. Players then met the incompatible-version rejection at the door until
a force-quit let the plugin's apply-on-background run.

- Key the apply on the updateAvailable (staged) signal and switch by id
  through set({ id }); reload() stays only as the no-set() fallback.
- Probe the plugin (getNextBundle + current) at install and again when the
  incompatible rejection lands with nothing in flight, so a bundle that
  finished before this JS context existed is still applied.
- Hold the applying screen on downloadComplete alone, bounded by a 30 s
  staging grace window; never switch to the running bundle (reload-loop
  guard).

move, not a rewrite) so the dispatcher and the catalog call the same

Don't sort MultipartBody fields by default

Some web services rely on the original entry list order, and sorting of
the entry list furthermore makes it impossible to emulate web browsers.

Alphabetical sorting of multipart/form-data fields directly contradicts
RFC 7578, which states:

5.2.  Ordered Fields and Duplicated Field Names

   Form processors given forms with a well-defined ordering SHOULD send
   back results in order.  (Note that there are some forms that do not
   define a natural order.)  Intermediaries MUST NOT reorder the
   results.  Form parts with identical field names MUST NOT be
   coalesced.

This commit removes the default sorting of MultipartBody fields.

To achieve alphabetical sorting of fields, there are two simple options:

* Call field() following the alphabetical order of fields names.
* Call fields() with a TreeMap parameter (LinkedHashMap for entry order).

In case someone should rely on functionality to sort fields after having
them added, the function sortFields() is also provided.

Fix silent exception swallow in LocalFsBlobStore.prepare()

If ClusterUtils.mkStormClusterState() threw (e.g. ZooKeeper unreachable),
the exception was caught and printed to stderr via e.printStackTrace(),
leaving stormClusterState null. Every subsequent blob store operation
(startSyncBlobs, setupBlobstore, blobSync) would then crash with a
NullPointerException rather than a meaningful error.

Rethrow as RuntimeException to match the existing pattern used a few
lines above for FileBlobStoreImpl initialization, and to surface the
root cause at startup instead of at first use.

now-fixed silent catch to let prepare() succeed with a null stormClusterState.

and pass its port in the conf used by initLocalFs(), matching the pattern
already established in LocalFsBlobStoreTest.

AsyncLocalizerTest.testKeyNotFoundException: wrap the test body in a
try-with-resources InProcessZookeeper and pass its port in the conf,
so that prepare() can initialise cluster state successfully before

The root cause of the CI failure was that the old code's SSLContext.setDefault() silently weakened TLS for the entire JVM, and the
  test's readContent was unknowingly piggy-backing on that global relaxation. After the hardening fix, readContent now does its own    per-connection trust-all + hostname-verifier override (same pattern as the production fix), so the test no longer depends on JVM-wide
  state. This also makes the test an implicit regression guard: if someone reintroduces SSLContext.setDefault() in the reporter, nothing
   in the test relies on it.

Fix TLS client auth socket configuration and modernize certificate handling

 - The SSLServerSocket setup called setWantClientAuth() after setNeedClientAuth(),      which per the JSSE specification clears the needClientAuth flag. Remove the redundant setWantClientAuth() call so the configured client-auth mode is applied correctly.

    with java.security.cert.X509Certificate / getPeerCertificates()

    distinguish encryption-only from mutual-auth mode when handling peer certificate lookup failures

fix(webapp): guard Flux viewer against js-yaml 5.x empty-input throw

js-yaml 5.x (merged on 2.x via #8863) changed load('') to throw a
YAMLException ('expected a document, but the input is empty') instead of
returning undefined (see js-yaml migrate_v4_to_v5). The Flux Topology
Viewer calls parseAndRender() on page load while the textarea holds only
a comment (# YAML Definition), so jsyaml.load() now throws before the
existing if(doc==null) guard, breaking the viewer at runtime.

This latent bug shipped untested on 2.x because cypress-tests.yml was
scoped to master only, so 2.x PRs never ran the e2e suite.

Wrap the load in try/catch and treat empty/comment-only or malformed
input as 'no document', and broaden cypress-tests.yml to run on 2.x.

Optimize ZooKeeper read requests and remove redundant checks (#8714)

* init

* add test case to check armed watch on absent zk node

Move workers to returning idle supervisors

EvenScheduler/DefaultScheduler do not move workers onto a supervisor
that returns to service after maintenance: the topology already has
its desired worker count spread across the surviving supervisors, so
the returned supervisor sits at used=0 until an operator rebalances by
hand. Add an opt-in, binary-trigger pass that relocates workers onto
such idle supervisors, round-robin across topologies, in a single
scheduling round. The feature is disabled by default, so existing
clusters see no behavior change.

needsScheduling is deliberately left untouched. The new trigger lives
in Cluster.hasIdleSupervisorReusableBy and is reached only from
EvenScheduler.redistributeOntoIdleSupervisors, which runs at the top of
scheduleTopologiesEvenly and DefaultScheduler.defaultSchedule.
ResourceAwareScheduler (needsSchedulingRas) and the multitenant pools
keep their existing needsScheduling behavior and never enter the new
path, so the feature is scoped to EvenScheduler/DefaultScheduler (and
the leftover topologies IsolationScheduler delegates to them) only.

The trigger is binary -- it fires only when at least one stable,
non-blacklisted supervisor has zero used slots and the topology is not
already on it -- so an "almost balanced" cluster never moves. Each
topology contributes at most one worker per round-robin iteration, so
the returned supervisor ends up hosting workers from several topologies
(preserving the per-supervisor workload diversity a fresh submission
has) instead of letting the first scheduled topology grab the whole
idle capacity. Per-topology relocations in one round are capped at
floor(numWorkers / nonBlacklistedSupervisorCount) * idleSupervisorCount,
tightened further by max.free.per.topology when positive. Workers are
pulled from the supervisor where the topology has the most workers
(ties broken by supervisor id, lexicographically), never draining one
below a single worker, and each pulled worker is placed directly onto
an idle slot so the regular sortSlots/interleave pass cannot drop it
back into the just-vacated slot.

  - DaemonConfig / conf/defaults.yaml (dot-only keys):
      nimbus.even.rebalance.idle.supervisor.enabled (false)
      nimbus.even.rebalance.max.free.per.topology (0 = unbounded)
      nimbus.even.rebalance.idle.supervisor.min.stable.rounds (3)
  - Cluster: new hasIdleSupervisorReusableBy (trigger) plus
    isIdleSupervisorAvailableForEvenRebalance and
    hasMinimumIdleSupervisorStability (eligibility + uptime guard,
    uptime >= min.stable.rounds * supervisor.monitor.frequency.secs)
    that skips a just-returned, possibly-flapping supervisor. All gated
    by the enabled flag; needsScheduling itself is unchanged.
  - SupervisorDetails.uptimeSecs surfaced from SupervisorInfo so the
    uptime guard can be evaluated; legacy constructors default it to
    Long.MAX_VALUE (always stable) to leave existing callers unchanged.
  - EvenScheduler.redistributeOntoIdleSupervisors returns immediately
    when the feature is disabled, so a default (disabled) cluster does
    no per-scheduling-round supervisor scanning.
  - Add TestEvenSchedulerIdleSupervisor covering the trigger, the
    per-topology drain cap, single-worker no-op, one-round even
    distribution, round-robin sharing across topologies, the uptime
    flap guard, deterministic donor tie-break, blacklist handling, the
    DefaultScheduler leftover-subset path, and the IsolationScheduler
    interaction (idle non-isolated target only; a reserved host stays
    out even when its isolated topology is down).

Skip stale worker heartbeats from orphaned worker directories

The supervisor builds the heartbeat batch it sends to Nimbus from every
worker directory present on disk, with no check on whether the worker is
still alive. If a worker directory is ever left behind (a worker that died
before the supervisor finished cleanup), its frozen heartbeat keeps being
reported until the next supervisor restart -- the only time orphaned
directories are reclaimed. Nimbus then repeatedly reads the (often deleted)
topology conf, flooding its log with "Exception when getting heartbeat
timeout" / NotAliveException.

Filter out heartbeats older than supervisor.worker.timeout.secs in
ReportWorkerHeartbeats: such a worker is already considered dead by the
same timeout the slot uses, so it should not be reported. A live worker
always refreshes its heartbeat well within the timeout, so this never
drops a valid heartbeat.

Fix double max.free.per.topology cap in idle rebalance

DefaultScheduler.defaultSchedule ran the idle-supervisor redistribute
twice per scheduling round: once over the full topology set at the top
(the round-robin fairness pass), then again inside the per-leftover
EvenScheduler.scheduleTopologiesEvenly call, which also redistributes on
entry. The full-set pass consumes one idle supervisor, leaving any other
idle supervisor for the per-topology pass to fill again, so the
per-topology max.free.per.topology cap was applied twice. With the
feature enabled, a positive cap and two or more idle supervisors, an
under-assigned topology could relocate up to 2 * cap existing workers in
a single round -- throttle-exceeding churn, not a crash or loss. Scoped
to the DefaultScheduler (and IsolationScheduler leftover) path;
EvenScheduler used directly schedules each topology once and is
unaffected.

The redistribute was added at both entry points by apache/storm#8778
without a re-entry guard. Add a redistributeOntoIdle toggle to
scheduleTopologiesEvenly: the public two-arg entry point keeps
redistribute=true (EvenScheduler's own single full-set pass is
unchanged), while DefaultScheduler runs the single full-set redistribute
itself and delegates per leftover topology with the toggle off. The cap
then binds once per round and the full-set round-robin fairness across
topologies is preserved -- simply dropping the first call would break
that fairness.

The redistribute pass is gated off by default, so there is no behavior
change for existing clusters.

Add a regression test exercising the DefaultScheduler path with two idle
supervisors, max.free.per.topology=1 and an under-assigned topology:
before the fix it relocates two workers (one onto each idle supervisor),
after the fix exactly one.

Filter worker heartbeats by per-topology timeout

ReportWorkerHeartbeats dropped stale local heartbeats using only the
global supervisor.worker.timeout.secs. The worker-kill authority,
Slot.getHbTimeoutMs(), instead uses
max(topology.worker.timeout.secs, supervisor.worker.timeout.secs).
A slow-but-alive worker of a topology that raised its own timeout was
therefore excluded from the report one round before Slot would treat
it as dead.

Compute the effective timeout per topology to mirror Slot: read the
localized topology conf and use max(global, min(override, max)). The
topology override is bounded by worker.max.timeout.secs -- Nimbus
already clamps it at submission, re-applied here defensively against
the override component only so the global floor is never reduced.
When the topology conf cannot be read (the orphaned worker dirs this
filter targets often outlive their conf) fall back to the global
timeout. The per-topology result is cached within a reporting round.

Add regression tests for a longer per-topology override, the
worker.max.timeout.secs cap, and the conf-read-failure fallback.

utils: use WeakReference in BatchInserter to fix ThreadLocal retention of JCQueue

BatchInserter held a strong reference to its owning JCQueue, and the
inserters live in instance-field ThreadLocals on the same JCQueue. This
formed a cycle through ThreadLocalMap:

  value (BatchInserter) -> queue (JCQueue) -> thdLocalBatcher (ThreadLocal) = key

Because the key was strongly reachable via the value, the weak-key
expunge path in ThreadLocalMap never triggered, and the JCQueue (along
with its metrics, recv/overflow queues and batch buffers) could not be
GC'd for as long as any producer thread that ever published to it stayed
alive.

The fix stores the JCQueue as a WeakReference inside BatchInserter,
cutting the value->key path. When the last external strong ref to the
JCQueue is dropped, the ThreadLocal field it owns becomes weakly
reachable, the ThreadLocalMap key can be expunged, and both the
BatchInserter and the JCQueue are released.

flush() and tryFlush() dereference the WeakReference once at entry and
bail out cleanly if the queue has already been collected (dead topology
in LocalCluster/embedded scenarios). publish() and tryPublish() are
unchanged — they only manipulate currentBatch.

Fixes #8810

Reduce binary distribution size: unbundle optional Hadoop/Kafka deps + de-duplicate shared jars (#8819)

* build: stop bundling storm-autocreds in the binary distribution

storm-autocreds pulls in the full Hadoop/HBase client dependency tree
(~79 MB, 43 jars unique to it) but is only needed on secure (Kerberos)
clusters and is off by default. Ship only the README, consistent with
the other external/* connectors, and add bin/storm-autocreds-fetch to
retrieve the plugin and its runtime dependencies from Maven Central into
extlib-daemon on demand.

Also removes the now-unused storm-autocreds-bin assembly module.

* build: stop bundling storm-kafka-monitor in the binary distribution

The storm-kafka-monitor jars (and their Kafka client dependencies, ~38 MB)
are only needed to display Kafka spout lag in the UI or to run the
bin/storm-kafka-monitor command. Ship only the README, consistent with the
other external/* connectors, and add bin/storm-kafka-monitor-fetch to
retrieve the tool and its runtime dependencies from Maven Central into
lib-tools/storm-kafka-monitor on demand.

Guard the UI against the jars being absent: TopologySpoutLag now detects
whether storm-kafka-monitor is installed and, when it is not, surfaces an
actionable message (and logs it once) instead of failing the lag shell-out.
The bin/storm-kafka-monitor wrapper prints the same hint instead of a
ClassNotFound error.

Also removes the now-unused storm-kafka-monitor-bin assembly module.

* build: add lib-common to the daemon and worker classpaths

Prepares de-duplication of the jars shared by the daemon (lib) and worker
(lib-worker) classpaths into a single lib-common directory. storm.py now
includes lib-common on both classpaths; when the directory is absent (older
layouts) it contributes nothing, so the change is backward compatible.

* build: add dedup-libs script to share daemon/worker jars via lib-common

The worker classpath (lib-worker) is a byte-identical subset of the daemon
classpath (lib). dedup-libs.py moves the shared jars into a single lib-common
directory and removes the duplicate copies from lib, reclaiming ~71 MB. It only
de-duplicates byte-identical jars (same name and sha-256), so a version
mismatch is never silently merged; tool classpaths (lib-tools/*, lib-webapp)
are left untouched.

Paired with the lib-common classpath support in bin/storm.py. Wiring this into
the binary assembly is a follow-up (it must be validated by a full -Pdist
distribution build).

* build: wire lib-common de-duplication into the binary assembly

final-package now stages the daemon jars (copy-dependencies -> staging/lib) and
the shared jars (storm-client-bin's lib-worker -> staging/lib-common), runs
dedup-libs.py to remove the byte-identical copies from lib, and the assembly
packages the staged lib/ and lib-common/ directories. The storm-client-bin tree
(which only carried lib-worker) is no longer copied directly.

Verified through the prepare-package phase: staging/lib = 48 jars, staging/
lib-common = 40 jars, zero overlap, full 88-jar daemon set preserved across
lib + lib-common, ~71 MB reclaimed. The final tar/zip packaging requires a full
-Pdist (native) distribution build and must be validated in CI / on Linux.

* test: add lib-common to expected classpaths in storm CLI tests

The binary distribution now de-duplicates jars shared by the daemon and
worker classpaths into a lib-common directory, which bin/storm.py adds to
the classpath after the storm home wildcard. Update the expected classpath
assertions in test_storm_cli.py to include lib-common.

* build: add a lean "storm-lite" distribution alongside the full one

The full distribution keeps bundling storm-autocreds (Hadoop/HBase) and
storm-kafka-monitor (Kafka client) so existing and air-gapped deployments are
unaffected. A second "storm-lite" artifact omits those jars and ships only their
READMEs, for users who do not need them and want a much smaller download.

The shared assembly content moves into a common.xml component descriptor, so
binary.xml (full) and binary-lite.xml differ only in the optional plugin jars.
The lite artifact is attached with the "lite" Maven classifier and is signed by
the existing GPG plugin. Both distributions keep the lib-common de-duplication.

Measured (3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, tar.gz): baseline 367 MB, full now 303 MB (-64 MB via
lib-common), lite 196 MB (-171 MB, ~47%).

RELEASING.md documents the new artifact and the extra signing/checksum steps.

* build: keep tooling on the full distribution now that storm-lite is built

The binary build produces two zips/tarballs, which broke consumers that assumed
exactly one artifact:

- integration-test/run-it.sh failed its "expected exactly one zip file" guard.
- integration-test/config/Vagrantfile raised "Expected one storm-binary".

Both now ignore apache-storm-*-lite.zip and run against the full distribution.
The cluster Dockerfile ADDs the full tarball by name, so its .dockerignore also
excludes the lite tarball to keep it out of the build context.

* build: fail dedup-libs on same-name/different-sha jars, add test coverage

Address review feedback: detect every same-name/different-sha-256 conflict
between the daemon (lib) and worker (lib-common/lib-worker) jars in a
read-only pass and fail the build before any file is moved or removed, so
a diverged jar can never silently shadow its counterpart on the daemon
classpath. The summary now also reports the number of worker-only jars
promoted to lib-common (expected 0) as a drift canary.

Add unit tests for dedup-libs.py, run on every PR/push via a workflow step
and during dist builds via a unix_py_tests profile mirroring storm-client.

* build: catch version drift in dedup-libs by comparing artifact base names

The jars are maven artifacts named <artifactId>-<version>.jar, so a version
bump changes the file name and the same-name/different-sha guard alone would
let e.g. lib/foo-1.0.jar and lib-worker/foo-1.1.jar pass as unrelated jars,
promoting the worker copy onto the daemon classpath next to the lib copy.
Compare jars by their version-stripped artifact base name (the part before
the first "-<digit>") as well and fail the build when the same artifact is
present with different versions; only artifacts absent from lib entirely are
counted as worker-only.

* Fix supervisor-launched workers: add lib-common to the worker framework classpath

Since the lib de-duplication (#8819) the distribution ships the worker jars
in lib-common instead of lib-worker. bin/storm.py was updated, but
BasicContainer.frameworkClasspath() still built the worker launch classpath
from lib-worker only, so supervisor-launched workers crashed with
ClassNotFoundException: org.apache.storm.LogWriter.

Add lib-common to the framework classpath, keeping lib-worker as the
drop-in location for worker-only jars.

* test: cover the real frameworkClasspath() in BasicContainerTest

The existing launch tests mock frameworkClasspath() away (FRAMEWORK_CP),
which is how the lib-common regression slipped through. Exercise the real
implementation via a hook in MockBasicContainer and assert that both
lib-common/* and lib-worker/* are on the worker classpath.

* build: ship an empty lib-worker drop-in directory in the distribution

The lib de-duplication removed lib-worker entirely, but both bin/storm.py
and BasicContainer keep lib-worker/* on the worker classpath, and operators
use the directory as the drop-in point for worker-only jars. Restore it as
an empty directory holding only a README that documents the new
lib / lib-common / lib-worker layout, in both the full and lite
distributions.

* Clarify worker/supervisor heartbeat docs and deprecate unused nimbus.supervisor.timeout.secs

Documentation still described the pre-2.0 model in which workers/tasks
heartbeat directly into ZooKeeper. Since 2.0 (STORM-2693), worker liveness

in an in-memory heartbeat cache; supervisor liveness is an ephemeral ZooKeeper
node detected via session expiry.
